title: Sakit kepala sebelah kanan, kiri atau belakang: what headache location can mean, relief and red flags
desc: One-sided throbbing, a tight band, pain behind one eye or at the back of the head: where a headache sits gives clues to its type. What each pattern can mean, how to ease it, how to avoid painkiller-overuse headaches, and the warning signs that need a doctor straight away.
headings: Headache by location · Sakit kepala sebelah kanan atau kiri · Sakit kepala bahagian belakang · Common triggers · Cara hilangkan sakit kepala: relief · When a headache is an emergency
keywords: Guides Sakit kepala by location Headache Migraine Sakit kepala denggi aedes nyamuk mosquito darah tinggi hypertension bp tekanan darah mengandung hamil pregnancy antenatal kecemasan emergency a&e hospital
body: A one-sided throbbing headache with nausea or sensitivity to light is typical of migraine. A tight band on both sides or at the back of the head is typical of a tension-type headache. Severe pain around one eye with a red, watering eye, lasting 15 minutes to 3 hours, suggests cluster headache. Pain over the cheeks and forehead with a blocked nose suggests sinusitis. Pain at the back of the head that gets worse when you move your neck may come from the neck. A new headache at the temples in someone over 50 needs checking the same day. Take painkillers early, but on no more than 2 days a week. Taking them more often can cause medication-overuse headaches. Avoid ibuprofen and aspirin if you might have dengue. Call 999 for a sudden, severe headache that peaks within seconds or minutes, or a headache with fever and a stiff neck, weakness, confusion, a seizure or loss of vision. Where Common causes Clues One side (sebelah kanan atau kiri) Migraine, hormonal headaches Throbbing, worse with movement, nausea, light and noise sensitivity Around or behind one eye Cluster headache Very severe, red watering eye, drooping lid, runny nose on the same side Both sides, like a tight band Tension-type headache Pressing or tightening, can include the forehead, temples and neck Back of the head (bahagian belakang) Tension-type, neck-related (cervicogenic) headache, occipital neuralgia Worse with neck movement, or sharp electric-shock pain at the base of the skull Forehead, cheeks, bridge of the nose (depan) Sinusitis, tension-type, eye strain Blocked nose, green or yellow mucus, tenderness over the cheeks Temples , in people over 50 Giant cell (temporal) arteritis New headache, tender scalp, jaw pain when chewing, vision changes Face, jaw or teeth on one side Trigeminal neuralgia Brief electric-shock attacks triggered by touch, eating or wind Anywhere Dehydration, missed meals, caffeine withdrawal, a fever Often eases with fluids, food and rest Sinus headaches are commonly mistaken for migraine, and a headache can move or change. Use this as a guide only. See our main headaches guide for more on each type. Migraine is the most common cause of a one-sided headache. About 9 in 100 Malaysians have migraine. Typical features: a throbbing pain, often on one side, that gets worse with movement nausea or vomiting, and sensitivity to light and sound attacks lasting 4 hours to 3 days in about 1 in 10, an aura before the headache, such as zigzag lights, numbness or difficulty speaking, lasting up to an hour Cluster headache is rarer but extremely painful: always on one side, around or above the eye or at the temple, lasting 15 minutes to 3 hours, up to several times a day, often with restlessness. It is more common in men in their 30s and 40s. Ordinary painkillers don’t work, so see a doctor. Trigeminal neuralgia causes sudden electric-shock pain on one side of the face or jaw, lasting seconds, often triggered by eating, brushing teeth, touching the face or air-conditioning. It usually starts after age 50. Most headaches are tension-type headaches or migraines and aren’t dangerous. Tension-type headache often starts at the back of the head or neck and spreads forwards, feeling like pressure or a tight band. It lasts from 30 minutes to several days, and is linked to stress, poor posture, tiredness and long hours at a screen. Neck-related (cervicogenic) headache usually starts on one side at the base of the skull, may spread to the front or behind the eye, and gets worse when you move your neck. Occipital neuralgia causes piercing, burning or electric-shock pain at the back of the head, sometimes spreading behind one eye. High blood pressure rarely causes headaches unless it is very high, so don’t rely on a headache to tell you your blood pressure is up. Check it with a monitor. See our guide to blood pressure . not drinking enough, especially in hot weather, and time in the hot sun skipping meals too much or too little sleep stress, and the “let-down” at weekends bright lights, screens and eye strain. Get your eyes tested if you often have headaches when reading. periods and hormonal changes alcohol, and cutting down suddenly on coffee or tea if you usually drink more than about 2 cups a day taking painkillers too often Keeping a headache diary can help you spot your triggers. Paracetamol (adults): 500mg to 1g, at least 4 hours apart, no more than 4g in 24 hours. Ibuprofen (adults): 200 to 400mg with food, at least 4 hours apart, no more than 1,200mg a day without a doctor’s advice. Not suitable with stomach ulcers, some types of asthma, kidney or heart disease, or in pregnancy. Aspirin (adults only): not for anyone under 16. Dengue caution: a severe headache and pain behind the eyes can be dengue. If you have a fever and could have dengue, take paracetamol only and avoid ibuprofen and aspirin. Migraine: painkillers work best taken early in an attack. If they don’t help, a doctor can prescribe a triptan. Rest in a quiet, dark room, drink water, eat something if you have skipped a meal, and apply a cool or warm compress. Don’t take painkillers too often. Using simple painkillers on 15 or more days a month, or triptans or codeine-containing painkillers on 10 or more days a month, can cause a medication-overuse headache. Keep painkillers to no more than 2 days a week, and see a doctor if you need them more. See our painkiller guide . Call 999 or go to an emergency department for a headache that: comes on suddenly and severely, reaching its worst within seconds to minutes (a “thunderclap” headache) comes with a fever and stiff neck, or a rash that doesn’t fade when pressed comes with weakness, numbness, slurred speech, confusion, a seizure or loss of vision. See our guide to stroke . follows a head injury See a doctor the same day if you are over 50 with a new headache, scalp tenderness or jaw pain when chewing, especially with vision changes, as giant cell arteritis can cause blindness if untreated. Pregnant women with a severe headache, vision problems or swelling should be seen urgently, as this can be pre-eclampsia. See a doctor soon if your headaches are getting more frequent or severe, change pattern, are worse when coughing, sneezing or bending, wake you from sleep, or come with vomiting. Children: migraine affects 4 to 10 in 100 children, and attacks are often shorter, sometimes with tummy pain. See a doctor if headaches start before age 7, change pattern, or come with behaviour changes, fits or balance problems. What does sakit kepala sebelah kanan mean? A headache on the right side. It is often a migraine, and less often a cluster headache or a neck-related headache. The same causes apply to the left side. What causes a headache at the back of the head? Usually a tension-type headache, often linked to stress, posture or long screen time. A neck problem or occipital neuralgia can also cause it. Is a one-sided headache serious? Usually not. Migraine is the most common cause. See a doctor urgently if it is sudden and severe, or comes with weakness, confusion or vision loss. How do I get rid of a headache quickly? Take paracetamol or ibuprofen early, drink water, eat if you have skipped a meal, and rest in a quiet, dark room. Avoid ibuprofen if you might have dengue. Can high blood pressure cause headaches? Rarely, unless it is very high. Most people with high blood pressure have no symptoms, so check it with a monitor. Why do I keep getting headaches? Common reasons include stress, poor sleep, dehydration, skipped meals, eye strain and taking painkillers too often. See a doctor if they are frequent or changing. When is a headache an emergency? When it is sudden and severe, or comes with fever and a stiff neck, weakness, confusion, a seizure or loss of vision, or after a head injury. Call 999.

title: Tanda-tanda awal kanser: early warning signs of the most common cancers in Malaysia
desc: Two in three cancers in Malaysia are found at a late stage, when they are harder to treat. The early warning signs of the most common cancers, the general symptoms not to ignore, when to see a doctor, and the free and subsidised screening available.
headings: Cancer in Malaysia · General warning signs · Breast, cervical, womb and ovarian cancer · Bowel, lung, liver and nasopharyngeal cancer · Mouth, blood and bone cancers · When to see a doctor, and free screening
keywords: Prevention Tanda-tanda awal kanser Cancer symptoms Early detection Tanda kanser payudara kanser cancer mammogram pink october vaksin suntikan jab immunisation klinik doctor doktor gp saringan check-up checkup medical aesthetic estetik kecantikan beauty kulit skin botox filler laser facial
body: Malaysia recorded 168,823 new cancers between 2017 and 2021. The most common are breast, colorectal, lung, lymphoma and liver cancer. About 1 in 8 Malaysians will get cancer in their lifetime. About 65% of cancers in Malaysia are found at stage 3 or 4. For lung cancer the figure is about 95%, and for colorectal cancer about 75%. General warning signs include unexplained weight loss, ongoing tiredness, night sweats, a new lump, unexplained bleeding, and a cough, sore or ulcer that doesn’t heal. See a doctor for a cough lasting more than 3 weeks, a mouth ulcer lasting more than 3 weeks, or any symptom that doesn’t get better, gets worse or keeps coming back. Free or subsidised screening includes mammograms through LPPKN, HPV self-sampling through Program ROSE, and checks through PeKa B40. The Malaysia National Cancer Registry recorded 168,823 new cancers between 2017 and 2021. About 1 in 8 Malaysians will get cancer during their lifetime. Cancer Share of all cancers Found at stage 3 or 4 Breast 17.6% About 1 in 2 Colorectal (bowel) 14.1% About 3 in 4 Lung 10.1% About 19 in 20 Liver 4.9% Nearly 9 in 10 in men Nasopharynx (nose and throat) 3.1% About 3 in 4 Cervix Among the top 6 in women About 1 in 2 Late diagnosis is a major reason for poorer survival. For cervical cancer, for example, five-year survival in a Malaysian study was about 75% at stage 1 but 23% at stage 4. See a doctor if you notice any of these, especially if they don’t go away, get worse or keep coming back: unexplained weight loss tiredness that doesn’t improve heavy night sweats or unexplained fevers a new lump anywhere in the body unexplained bleeding or bruising a sore, ulcer or rash that won’t heal ongoing indigestion, bloating or difficulty swallowing a hoarse voice or cough that won’t go away yellow skin or eyes (jaundice) Cancer Research UK stresses that most of the time these are caused by something less serious, but they are still worth checking. Breast cancer (tanda kanser payudara): a lump in the breast, chest or armpit, dimpled skin like orange peel, a change in breast size or shape, nipple discharge (sometimes bloody), a nipple that turns inwards, or a rash on the nipple. Breast pain alone is not usually a sign. Men can get breast cancer too. See our breast screening guide . Cervical cancer (tanda kanser servik): bleeding during or after sex, between periods or after the menopause, changes in vaginal discharge, and pelvic or back pain. See our guide to Pap smears and HPV tests . Womb cancer (tanda kanser rahim): bleeding after the menopause is the key sign. Unusually heavy periods or bleeding between periods also need checking. Ovarian cancer: persistent bloating, tummy or pelvic pain, feeling full quickly and needing to pass urine more often, on most days. See our guide to ovarian cysts and fibroids . About half of breast cancers in Malaysia are found at a late stage. Knowing the signs and getting screened helps. Colorectal cancer (tanda kanser usus): a change in bowel habit, blood in the stool (red or black), bleeding from the back passage, tummy pain or a lump, bloating, weight loss, and tiredness or breathlessness from anaemia. See our bowel cancer screening guide . Lung cancer (tanda kanser paru-paru): a cough lasting more than 3 weeks, coughing up blood, breathlessness, chest or shoulder pain, repeated chest infections and weight loss. A Malaysian lung specialist group says more than 60% of women with lung cancer have never smoked, so don’t ignore these signs if you don’t smoke. Nasopharyngeal cancer: particularly common among Chinese and some Bumiputera communities in Sarawak. Signs include a painless lump in the neck (the most common), nosebleeds, a blocked nose, blood in saliva, a blocked ear or hearing loss on one side, ringing in the ear, headache and facial numbness. Liver cancer: often has no early symptoms. Later signs include yellow skin or eyes, weight loss, pain or a lump under the right ribs, and feeling full quickly. Hepatitis B is the leading cause in Malaysia, so get tested and vaccinated. See our hepatitis B guide . Mouth cancer: a mouth ulcer that lasts more than 3 weeks, a red or white patch, a lump, ongoing pain or hoarseness. Smoking, alcohol and chewing betel quid increase the risk. See our guide to mouth ulcers . Lymphoma: painless swelling in the neck, armpit or groin, night sweats, fever, itching and weight loss. Leukaemia: tiredness, pale skin, breathlessness, easy bruising or bleeding, frequent infections and bone aches. See our guide to anaemia . Bone cancer (tanda kanser tulang): bone pain that is often worse at night, swelling and a limp. Bone cancer is rare, and most bone pain has other causes. Prostate cancer: often has no early symptoms. See our guide to the PSA test . See a doctor if a symptom doesn’t get better, gets worse or keeps coming back. For a cough or a mouth ulcer, see a doctor if it lasts more than 3 weeks. You aren’t wasting the doctor’s time. Screening can find some cancers before symptoms start: Mammogram (LPPKN): free for women with a household income of RM10,000 or less, with a subsidy for others, at registered centres. Cervical screening: Program ROSE offers HPV self-sampling for women aged 30 to 65, free depending on nationality and income, with results by SMS. Bowel screening: a stool test (FOBT) is recommended from around age 50. The National Cancer Society Malaysia offers it for a small fee. PeKa B40 : includes a clinical breast examination and, for men at risk, a prostate check, for eligible Malaysians aged 40 and over. See our guide to free health screening in Malaysia for more options. What are the early signs of cancer? Unexplained weight loss, ongoing tiredness, night sweats, a new lump, unexplained bleeding, and a cough, sore or ulcer that doesn’t heal. Most have other causes, but get them checked. What are the signs of breast cancer? A lump in the breast or armpit, dimpled skin, a change in size or shape, nipple discharge or a nipple that turns inwards. Breast pain alone is not usually a sign. What are the signs of bowel cancer? A change in bowel habit, blood in the stool, tummy pain or a lump, weight loss, and tiredness from anaemia. What are the signs of cervical cancer? Bleeding after sex, between periods or after the menopause, and changes in discharge. Regular screening can find changes before cancer develops. Can non-smokers get lung cancer? Yes. In Malaysia, more than 60% of women with lung cancer have never smoked, according to lung specialists. See a doctor for a cough lasting more than 3 weeks or coughing up blood. Is cancer screening free in Malaysia? Some is. LPPKN mammograms are free for lower-income households, Program ROSE offers free HPV self-tests depending on eligibility, and PeKa B40 includes some checks. How common is late diagnosis of cancer in Malaysia? About 65% of cancers are found at stage 3 or 4, including about 95% of lung cancers and 75% of colorectal cancers.

title: Tanda sakit jantung: signs of heart disease, from angina to heart failure, and when to get checked
desc: Heart disease is Malaysia’s leading cause of death, and many people have warning signs before an emergency. What angina, heart failure and an irregular heartbeat feel like, why women often don’t get chest pain, the risk factors and tests, and when to call 999.
headings: Angina: chest tightness on exertion · Warning signs before a heart attack · Heart failure · Irregular heartbeat and palpitations · Valve disease, cardiomyopathy and young people · Your risk and getting checked
keywords: Heart & diabetes Tanda sakit jantung Heart disease Angina Heart failure kencing manis gula hba1c darah tinggi hypertension bp tekanan darah kecemasan emergency a&e hospital saringan check-up checkup medical
body: Ischaemic heart disease was Malaysia’s leading cause of death in 2024, with 17,421 deaths. It is the top cause of death in men and in people aged 41 to 59. Angina is chest tightness that comes on with exertion or stress and eases with rest, usually within 5 minutes. Angina at rest, or that is getting worse, is an emergency. In a US study, 95% of women noticed new symptoms such as unusual tiredness, poor sleep or breathlessness in the month before a heart attack, and 43% had no chest pain during it. Heart failure causes breathlessness on exertion or lying flat, swollen ankles, sudden weight gain and tiredness. An irregular pulse can mean atrial fibrillation, which raises the risk of stroke. Malaysian guidelines suggest a heart risk check from age 30. A third of Malaysian adults have high cholesterol and nearly a third have high blood pressure. Angina is chest pain or tightness caused by narrowed heart arteries that can’t deliver enough blood when the heart works harder. Stable angina comes on with exertion, such as walking uphill or climbing stairs, emotional stress, cold weather or a heavy meal. It usually eases with rest within 5 minutes, and feels similar each time. Unstable angina happens at rest, is more severe, lasts longer, or doesn’t ease with rest or medicine. Call 999 . If you have angina and a GTN spray: stop and rest, use your GTN, take a second dose after 5 minutes if needed, and call 999 if the pain continues 5 minutes after the second dose. See a doctor if your angina is getting worse, more frequent, longer, or comes on at rest. Angina means a higher risk of heart attack and stroke, so it should always be assessed. See our guide to chest pain . A widely cited US study of 515 women who had had a heart attack found that about 95% had noticed new or different symptoms a month or more beforehand: unusual tiredness (71%) sleep problems (48%) breathlessness (42%) indigestion (39%) anxiety (35%) Fewer than 30% had chest discomfort beforehand, and 43% had no chest pain even during the heart attack. Instead they had breathlessness, weakness, tiredness, a cold sweat and dizziness. A caution: these symptoms are common and usually have other causes, and the study couldn’t show they reliably predict a heart attack. Social media posts promising “5 signs before a heart attack” overstate this. The real lesson is that no chest pain doesn’t mean no heart attack , especially in women, older people and people with diabetes. If new symptoms worry you, and you have risk factors, see a doctor. For heart attack symptoms and what to do, see our guide to heart attack and stroke . High blood pressure, diabetes and high cholesterol are the main treatable risks for heart disease. Heart failure means the heart isn’t pumping as well as it should. It is often caused by past heart attacks or long-term high blood pressure. Signs include: breathlessness with activity, or when lying flat tiredness, weakness or dizziness swollen ankles, legs or tummy sudden weight gain over a few days a cough at night, or frothy pink phlegm Call 999 for severe breathlessness, blue or grey lips, or collapse. Treatment can improve symptoms and help people live longer. A normal resting pulse is steady and usually 60 to 100 beats a minute. See our guide to normal heart rate (bacaan jantung normal) and palpitations . Atrial fibrillation (AF) causes an irregular pulse with no set pattern, sometimes fast, with palpitations, tiredness, breathlessness or dizziness. Some people have no symptoms at all. AF raises the risk of stroke, so doctors use a risk score to decide on blood-thinning medicine. Call 999 if a fast or irregular heartbeat comes with chest pain, fainting, breathlessness or signs of stroke. Heart valve disease can cause breathlessness, tiredness, dizziness, palpitations, swollen ankles or chest pain, or no symptoms with only a murmur heard by a doctor. Cardiomyopathy (heart muscle disease) is often inherited. It can cause dizziness, chest pain, breathlessness or blackouts, and many people have no symptoms. Relatives can be tested. Young people: chest pain, breathlessness, palpitations, light-headedness or fainting, especially with a family history of sudden unexplained death at a young age, should be checked. An ECG can detect many of the conditions involved. Risk factors in Malaysia (National Health and Morbidity Survey 2023 and other national data): high cholesterol : 33% of adults high blood pressure : 29% diabetes : 16% overweight or obesity: 54% smoking: 19% of people aged 15 and over physical inactivity, and a family history of early heart disease (a parent or sibling affected before 55 in men or 65 in women) Malaysians tend to have heart attacks younger than people in neighbouring countries, with an average age of about 58 to 59 in Malaysian registries. Getting checked: Malaysia’s heart disease prevention guideline recommends a risk check from age 30, using a score based on your age, blood pressure, cholesterol, diabetes and smoking. People with high blood pressure or diabetes should have an ECG at their first assessment. Tests your doctor may arrange include an ECG (heart tracing), blood tests for cholesterol and sugar, an echocardiogram (heart ultrasound), an exercise stress test, a CT scan of the heart arteries, or an angiogram. Routine stress tests and echocardiograms aren’t recommended for people without symptoms. Free screening is available through some schemes. See our guide to free health screening . What are the signs of heart disease? Chest tightness on exertion that eases with rest (angina), breathlessness, swollen ankles, an irregular or racing pulse, dizziness or fainting, and unusual tiredness. Are there warning signs before a heart attack? Many people, especially women, notice new tiredness, poor sleep, breathlessness or indigestion in the weeks before. These are common and not specific, so see a doctor if you are worried and have risk factors. Can you have a heart attack without chest pain? Yes. In one study, 43% of women had no chest pain during their heart attack. Breathlessness, weakness, sweating and dizziness can be the main signs. What is a normal heart rate? For adults at rest, usually 60 to 100 beats a minute, with a steady rhythm. At what age should I check my heart? Malaysian guidelines suggest a heart risk assessment from age 30, and earlier if you have diabetes, high blood pressure or a strong family history. What tests check for heart disease? An ECG, blood tests for cholesterol and sugar, an echocardiogram, an exercise stress test, a CT scan of the heart arteries or an angiogram, depending on your symptoms. When should I call 999? For chest pain or tightness at rest or lasting more than a few minutes, severe breathlessness, fainting, or a racing or irregular heartbeat with chest pain.

title: Bacaan kolesterol normal: cholesterol levels in mmol/L, LDL targets, and how to lower cholesterol
desc: A third of Malaysian adults have high cholesterol, and half of them don’t know it. What each number on your lipid test means, the LDL target for your level of risk, whether you need to fast, which foods and lifestyle changes help, and the truth about statins and supplements.
headings: What is a normal cholesterol reading? · Your LDL target depends on your risk · Testing: who, when and do I need to fast? · How to lower cholesterol with diet and lifestyle · Statins and other medicines
keywords: Heart & diabetes Bacaan kolesterol normal Cholesterol LDL cholesterol Dyslipidaemia kencing manis gula hba1c darah tinggi hypertension bp tekanan darah payudara kanser cancer mammogram pink october mengandung hamil pregnancy antenatal saringan check-up checkup medical
body: Malaysia’s guideline flags total cholesterol above 5.2 mmol/L, HDL below 1.0 in men or 1.2 in women, and triglycerides above 1.7 mmol/L. There is no single normal LDL. Under the 2017 guideline, people at low or intermediate risk aim for below 3.0 mmol/L. People at high or very high risk aim much lower, and the 2023 update lowered these targets to 1.8 and 1.4 mmol/L. You usually don’t need to fast for a cholesterol test. Adults should be screened from age 30, or from 18 with a strong family history or diabetes. A third of Malaysian adults have high cholesterol, and about half of them don’t know it. About 1 in 100 Malaysians has inherited high cholesterol. Cutting saturated fat (including santan and coconut oil), eating more fibre, exercising and losing weight help. Statins lower LDL by up to about half, and most muscle aches people blame on them aren’t caused by the statin. These are the levels Malaysia’s dyslipidaemia guideline flags as abnormal: Test Flagged as abnormal In mg/dL Total cholesterol Above 5.2 mmol/L Above about 200 HDL (“good”) cholesterol Below 1.0 (men) or 1.2 (women) Below about 39 or 46 Triglycerides Above 1.7 mmol/L Above about 150 LDL (“bad”) cholesterol Depends on your risk (see below) Optimal is below about 100 The guideline describes an LDL of 1.3 to 1.8 mmol/L as physiologically normal, and below 2.6 as optimal for adults. Non-HDL cholesterol (total cholesterol minus HDL) is a useful extra measure, especially if you have diabetes or high triglycerides. Its target is your LDL target plus 0.8. To convert cholesterol from mmol/L to mg/dL, multiply by about 38.7. For triglycerides, multiply by about 88.6. See also our guide to blood test results . Doctors first decide your risk of a heart attack or stroke. If you already have heart disease, diabetes or kidney disease, you are automatically at high or very high risk. Otherwise, your doctor uses a score based on your age, sex, blood pressure, cholesterol, diabetes and smoking to estimate your 10-year risk. Risk LDL target (2017 guideline) 2023 update Low (under 10% in 10 years) Below 3.0 mmol/L Below 3.0 mmol/L Intermediate (10 to 20%) Below 3.0 mmol/L Reported as below 2.6 mmol/L High (over 20%, diabetes, kidney disease) 2.6 mmol/L, or a 50% reduction 1.8 mmol/L or less, and at least a 50% reduction Very high (heart attack, stroke, narrowed arteries) Below 1.8 mmol/L, or a 50% reduction 1.4 mmol/L or less, and at least a 50% reduction An LDL above 4.9 mmol/L on its own puts you at high risk. The 2023 targets come from published summaries of the update, so your doctor may use slightly different figures. See our guide to signs of heart disease . A non-fasting blood test is fine for most cholesterol checks. Who: all adults over 30 should have a full lipid profile. Start from age 18 if you have a family history of early heart disease, diabetes, obesity around the waist or a known inherited cholesterol problem. Fasting: usually not needed. Results differ by only about 0.2 mmol/L. You may be asked to fast if your triglycerides were very high, or if you are having other tests that need fasting. How often: typically every few years if normal. If you start or change treatment, your doctor will recheck in 1 to 3 months, then every 6 to 12 months. In Malaysia: the 2023 National Health and Morbidity Survey found high cholesterol in a third of adults, about 7.5 million people, and about half didn’t know it. Free screening is available through some schemes. See our guide to free health screening . Inherited high cholesterol (familial hypercholesterolaemia) affects about 1 in 100 Malaysians. Suspect it if your LDL is very high, a parent or sibling had heart disease before 55 (men) or 65 (women), or you have fatty lumps on the tendons of your fingers or heels. Family members should be tested too. Cut saturated fat to less than 10% of your energy. Santan, coconut oil and palm oil are high in saturated fat, as are fatty meat and fried food. A review of 16 trials found coconut oil raised LDL compared with other vegetable oils. Avoid trans fats , found in some biscuits, pastries and fried snacks. Eat more fibre : aim for 20 to 30g a day, from vegetables, fruit, beans and whole grains. Oats with 3g of beta-glucan a day lower LDL by about 0.25 mmol/L. Juicing removes fibre, so eat whole fruit. Reduce refined carbohydrates such as white rice and sugary drinks, especially if your triglycerides are high. Exercise: regular aerobic exercise raises HDL and lowers triglycerides. Lose weight if you are overweight. Even 5 to 10% helps. See our BMI calculator . Stop smoking , which raises HDL. Eggs: cholesterol in food has only a weak effect on blood cholesterol for most people. The American Heart Association says one egg a day is reasonable as part of a healthy diet. Statins lower LDL by about 21 to 55%, depending on the type and dose. Common generic statins include atorvastatin, rosuvastatin, simvastatin and pravastatin. Other options, such as ezetimibe or injections (PCSK9 inhibitors), may be added if targets aren’t reached. Muscle aches: in blinded trials, muscle aches were almost as common on placebo (26.6%) as on statins (27.1%), and more than 90% of reported muscle symptoms weren’t caused by the statin. If you do get symptoms, most people can take a different statin. Liver: a mild rise in liver tests happens in fewer than 3 in 100 people. Serious liver problems are very rare. Diabetes: statins slightly increase the chance of developing diabetes, but the benefit for the heart is much greater. Pregnancy: stop statins before trying for a baby, and don’t take them while pregnant or breastfeeding. Grapefruit can interact with some statins. Supplements: Red yeast rice contains monacolin K, which is the same as the statin lovastatin. In Malaysia, these products must be registered, are limited to 10mg of monacolin K a day, and must carry warnings. Don’t take them with a prescribed statin, and check for a MAL number. Fish oil at high doses lowers triglycerides, but doesn’t replace statins for LDL. What is a normal cholesterol level in Malaysia? Malaysia’s guideline flags total cholesterol above 5.2 mmol/L, HDL below 1.0 (men) or 1.2 (women) and triglycerides above 1.7 mmol/L. The LDL target depends on your heart risk. What is a normal LDL level? An LDL below 2.6 mmol/L is optimal for most adults. People at low or intermediate risk aim for below 3.0, and people at high or very high risk aim much lower, down to 1.4 mmol/L. Do I need to fast for a cholesterol test? Usually not. Your doctor may ask you to fast if your triglycerides were very high before, or for other tests. How can I lower my cholesterol naturally? Cut saturated fat such as santan and fried food, eat more fibre and oats, exercise regularly, lose weight if needed and stop smoking. Are eggs bad for cholesterol? For most people, eating eggs has only a small effect on blood cholesterol. About one egg a day is reasonable as part of a healthy diet. Do statins cause muscle pain? Muscle aches are common whether or not people take statins. Trials found that more than 90% of reported muscle symptoms weren’t caused by the statin. Is red yeast rice safe? It contains the same substance as a statin. Use only registered products with a MAL number, and don’t take it with a prescribed statin.

title: Prednisolone untuk sakit apa? What this steroid treats, how to take it safely, and side effects
desc: Prednisolone is a steroid medicine used for asthma attacks, allergies, skin, joint and bowel conditions, and more. What it treats, how to take it, why long courses must be tapered, the side effects to watch for, and why steroids hidden in unregistered “ubat sakit urat” products are dangerous.
headings: Prednisolone untuk sakit apa? What it treats · How to take prednisolone · Side effects · Other medicines, pregnancy and children · Hidden steroids in unregistered products
keywords: Guides Prednisolone: untuk apa Prednisolone Corticosteroid Steroid medicine kencing manis gula hba1c darah tinggi hypertension bp tekanan darah payudara kanser cancer mammogram pink october kesihatan mental depression anxiety stress kemurungan mengandung hamil pregnancy antenatal vaksin suntikan jab immunisation aesthetic estetik kecantikan beauty kulit skin botox filler laser facial
body: Prednisolone treats inflammation and immune conditions, including asthma and COPD flare-ups, severe allergies and hives, eczema, rheumatoid arthritis, lupus, inflammatory bowel disease, gout flares and some kidney conditions. Take it in the morning with or after breakfast. Don’t stop suddenly if you have taken it for more than 3 weeks or at a high dose. Your doctor will reduce the dose gradually. Short courses usually cause only mild side effects such as a bigger appetite, poor sleep, mood changes and higher blood sugar. Long-term use can weaken bones, raise blood pressure and increase the risk of infection. Avoid anti-inflammatory painkillers unless your doctor agrees, as together they raise the risk of stomach bleeding. Avoid live vaccines while taking it. The Ministry of Health has found prednisolone and dexamethasone hidden in unregistered traditional products. Check for a MAL number and hologram before buying any remedy. Prednisolone is used for conditions where inflammation or the immune system is causing harm, including: Breathing: flare-ups of asthma and COPD Allergy and skin: severe allergic reactions and hives , severe eczema flares, psoriasis , and blistering skin conditions Joints and muscles: rheumatoid arthritis, polymyalgia rheumatica, and gout flares when other painkillers aren’t suitable Immune conditions: lupus, vasculitis and sarcoidosis Bowel: ulcerative colitis and Crohn’s disease Kidneys: nephrotic syndrome, particularly in children Nerves: Bell’s palsy, ideally started within 72 hours Other uses: preventing transplant rejection, Addison’s disease, and as part of some cancer treatments Courses range from a few days, for an asthma attack, to a year or more, for polymyalgia rheumatica. Prednisolone is a prescription medicine. Never take tablets prescribed for someone else. Take it once a day in the morning , with or after breakfast, unless your doctor says otherwise. This reduces stomach upset and sleep problems. Swallow the tablets whole with water. Don’t stop suddenly if you have taken it for more than 3 weeks or at a high dose. Your body stops making its own steroid hormones while you take it, so the dose is lowered gradually. Stopping too fast can cause weakness, fever, muscle pain and dangerously low blood pressure. Carry a steroid card if you take it for more than 3 weeks, and tell any doctor, dentist or nurse treating you. People who depend on daily steroids may need a higher dose during serious illness or surgery. Short courses of 3 weeks or less are unlikely to cause long-term side effects, and can usually be stopped as prescribed. Take prednisolone in the morning with food, and don’t stop a long course suddenly. Common, especially with short courses: a bigger appetite and weight gain difficulty sleeping, mood changes, irritability or anxiety indigestion, nausea or headache higher blood sugar, and fluid retention With long-term or high-dose use: a rounder face and weight gain (Cushing’s syndrome) weaker bones, and slowed growth in children more infections high blood pressure and diabetes. See our blood sugar guide . cataracts and glaucoma thin skin, easy bruising and slow wound healing Get medical help urgently if you have: black, tarry stools, or vomit with blood in it signs of infection, such as a fever or sore throat severe mood changes, low mood, or thoughts of harming yourself. About 5 in 100 people have serious mental health effects. contact with chickenpox, shingles or measles, if you haven’t had chickenpox, while taking prednisolone or within 3 months of stopping. See our guides to chickenpox and shingles . blurred vision Anti-inflammatory painkillers such as ibuprofen and diclofenac raise the risk of stomach ulcers and bleeding when taken with prednisolone. Ask your doctor before taking them. See our painkiller guide . Diabetes medicines: prednisolone raises blood sugar, so you may need to check it more often or adjust your treatment. Warfarin, some antibiotics, liquorice, and traditional or herbal medicines can interact. Tell your doctor and pharmacist everything you take. Vaccines: avoid live vaccines, such as MMR, chickenpox, BCG, yellow fever and oral typhoid, while taking prednisolone. Non-live vaccines such as flu are safe. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: prednisolone can be used if needed, and is usually fine while breastfeeding. Your doctor will weigh up the benefits and risks. Children can take it, but long-term use may slow growth, so it is monitored. Steroids are controlled medicines in Malaysia and should only be used with a doctor’s prescription. Dexamethasone and prednisolone are never allowed in traditional medicines. Yet the Ministry of Health has repeatedly found them hidden in unregistered products: In December 2025, the ministry warned that an unregistered powder sold online contained dexamethasone, prednisolone and diclofenac, with risks including kidney damage, diabetes, high blood pressure and hormonal problems. In 2016, unregistered traditional products sold for joint, back and muscle pain were found to contain dexamethasone, with reports of Cushing’s syndrome (“moon face”) and liver failure. In May 2026, Singapore’s health authority reported people hospitalised with kidney injury, Cushing’s syndrome and adrenal failure after taking pain relief products laced with steroids. A warning sign: a remedy that brings unusually fast relief for long-standing pain or skin problems may contain a hidden steroid. Before buying any remedy, check for a MAL registration number and the hologram security label, and search it on NPRA’s website. If you have been taking an unregistered product for a long time, don’t stop it suddenly . See a doctor, as your body may need the steroid dose reduced gradually. Prednisolone 5mg untuk sakit apa? Prednisolone treats inflammation and immune conditions such as asthma flare-ups, severe allergies, eczema, arthritis, lupus, bowel inflammation and gout flares. The dose depends on the condition, and 5mg tablets are combined to make up the prescribed dose. Is prednisolone a painkiller? Not exactly. It reduces inflammation, which can ease pain in conditions such as arthritis or gout, but it isn’t a general painkiller. Should I take prednisolone in the morning or at night? In the morning, with or after breakfast. Taking it at night can cause sleep problems. Can I stop prednisolone suddenly? Not if you have taken it for more than 3 weeks or at a high dose. Your doctor will lower the dose gradually. Short courses can usually be stopped as prescribed. Does prednisolone cause weight gain? It often increases appetite, and long-term use can cause weight gain and a rounder face. Short courses usually have a smaller effect. Can I take ibuprofen with prednisolone? Only if your doctor agrees, because together they raise the risk of stomach ulcers and bleeding. Paracetamol is usually safer. How do I know if a product has hidden steroids? You can’t tell by looking. Buy only registered products with a MAL number and hologram, and be suspicious of remedies that work unusually fast for long-term pain.

title: Pantang larang makanan pesakit buah pinggang: a kidney disease diet guide for Malaysians
desc: There is no single kidney diet: what you need to limit depends on your stage, your blood results and whether you are on dialysis. A practical guide to salt, potassium, phosphate, protein and fluids, Malaysian foods to watch, why star fruit is dangerous, and where to get dietitian help.
headings: There is no one kidney diet · Salt: the change that helps almost everyone · Potassium: only if your blood test is high · Phosphate and protein · How much should I drink? · Foods and remedies to avoid
keywords: Heart & diabetes Kidney disease diet Chronic kidney disease Renal diet Pantang larang makanan kencing manis gula hba1c
body: There is no one “kidney diet”. Your limits depend on your stage, blood results and whether you are on dialysis, so ask for a dietitian referral. Malaysia’s kidney guideline advises less than 2,400mg of sodium a day, about a teaspoon of salt. Soy sauce, budu and cencalok contain around 5g of sodium per 100g. Only limit potassium if your blood tests show it is high. Never use potassium-based salt substitutes if you have kidney disease. People not on dialysis are usually advised moderate protein (0.6 to 0.8g per kg of body weight a day), while people on dialysis need more (1.0 to 1.2g per kg). Avoid star fruit (belimbing) and belimbing buluh if you have kidney disease: they can cause confusion, seizures and kidney injury. Diet advice for kidney disease depends on: your stage of chronic kidney disease. See our guide to kidney disease and its stages . your blood test results , especially potassium and phosphate whether you are on dialysis other conditions, such as diabetes UK kidney specialists warn that a low-potassium diet is irrelevant for most people with early kidney disease, and that unnecessary limits can lead people to cut out healthy fruit and vegetables. So don’t follow a generic list of “pantang larang” without checking with your doctor or a dietitian. In a Malaysian study, only about a third of dialysis centres had access to a dietitian, so ask your doctor for a referral, especially at a government hospital. Malaysia’s kidney disease guideline advises less than 2,400mg of sodium a day , about one teaspoon of salt in total, including salt already in food. Malaysian adults eat about 3,400mg a day on average. Watch out for: Food Sodium per 100g (average, Malaysian survey) Budu and cencalok About 5,200mg Light soy sauce (kicap cair) About 5,100mg Salty soy sauce About 4,800mg Oyster sauce About 3,200mg Other high-salt foods include instant noodles, salted fish (ikan masin), salted eggs, pickles, sausages, luncheon meat and nuggets, canned soups, MSG, ready-made cooking pastes and chilli sauces. Cook with herbs, spices, lime, garlic and ginger instead of extra salt or sauces. Taste before adding sauce at the table. Choose fresh rather than processed or preserved foods. Never use potassium-based salt substitutes (often sold as “low sodium” or “sodium-free” salt) if you have kidney disease, as they can raise your potassium dangerously. Fresh food cooked with herbs and spices instead of salty sauces is the most useful change for most people with kidney disease. Potassium only needs limiting if your doctor tells you your blood potassium is high, which is more common in advanced kidney disease and with some medicines. Both high and low potassium can affect the heart. Foods high in potassium include bananas, avocado, dried fruit, coconut and coconut products, potatoes and chips, tomato purée, mushrooms, spinach, fruit juices, chocolate and nuts. Many can still be eaten in smaller portions, for example half a banana. Reducing potassium in vegetables and potatoes: cut them into small pieces, soak them in plenty of water, boil them in fresh water and throw the cooking water away. Durian: it is high in potassium, and there have been reports of serious harm in people on dialysis after eating it. If you are on dialysis or have a high potassium level, ask your team before eating it. Phosphate is usually limited in later stages and on dialysis, when blood tests show it is high. High phosphate weakens bones and can harden blood vessels. Phosphate added to processed food (look for “phos” in the ingredients) is absorbed almost completely, so processed meats, dark colas and some bottled drinks are the first things to cut. Dairy, sardines, organ meats, nuts and beans are naturally high in phosphate. If you are prescribed phosphate binders, take them with every meal and snack. Group Protein per day Stages 3 to 5, not on dialysis (Malaysian guideline) 0.6 to 0.8g per kg of body weight, with a dietitian Kidney disease caused by diabetes About 0.8g per kg On haemodialysis or peritoneal dialysis 1.0 to 1.2g per kg Too much protein can strain damaged kidneys, but too little can cause malnutrition, especially on dialysis, so don’t cut it drastically on your own. Plant proteins, such as tofu and lentils, may be easier on the kidneys. Avoid protein shakes and supplements unless your dietitian recommends them. Most people with early kidney disease don’t need to limit fluids. A large trial found that drinking extra water didn’t slow kidney disease. Drinking more than you need won’t “flush” the kidneys. In advanced kidney disease and on dialysis, you may be given a daily fluid allowance, depending on how much urine you still pass. Cutting fluids when you haven’t been told to can be harmful. Eating less salt makes it easier to stick to a fluid limit, because salt makes you thirsty. With diabetes: control carbohydrates and sugar, as you would anyway. A good diabetes diet suits early kidney disease. Star fruit (belimbing besi): contains a toxin that people with kidney disease can’t clear. It can cause hiccups, confusion, seizures and death. Avoid it completely if you have kidney disease. Belimbing buluh (bilimbi): a Sabah case report described acute kidney injury in a young man with healthy kidneys after eating about 1kg a day, from its oxalate content. People with kidney disease should avoid it, especially as juice or on an empty stomach. Herbal remedies and supplements: in a Malaysian study, about two-thirds of dialysis patients used traditional or complementary medicines, and most didn’t tell their doctor. Herbs can build up, raise potassium, cause fluid overload and interact with medicines. Some herbs containing aristolochic acid cause kidney disease. Tell your doctor about everything you take. Anti-inflammatory painkillers such as ibuprofen and diclofenac, unless your doctor agrees. See our painkiller guide . Where to get help: ask your doctor for a dietitian referral. The Malaysian Dietitians’ Association has kidney-friendly recipe books, including resources from the National Kidney Foundation of Malaysia and Hospital Kuala Lumpur. What foods should kidney patients avoid? Most should cut salt and salty sauces, processed meats and instant noodles, and avoid star fruit and herbal remedies. Limits on potassium, phosphate, protein and fluids depend on your stage and blood tests. Can kidney patients eat bananas? Usually yes in early kidney disease. If your blood potassium is high, you may need smaller portions, such as half a banana, or to avoid them. Ask your doctor or dietitian. How much salt can a kidney patient have? Malaysia’s kidney guideline advises less than 2,400mg of sodium a day, about a teaspoon of salt in total. Should kidney patients drink a lot of water? Not necessarily. Most people with early kidney disease don’t need to change how much they drink, and extra water doesn’t protect the kidneys. People on dialysis may need to limit fluids. Why is star fruit dangerous for kidney patients? It contains a toxin that damaged kidneys can’t remove, which can cause hiccups, confusion, seizures and even death. Should kidney patients eat less protein? People with stage 3 to 5 kidney disease not on dialysis are usually advised moderate protein. People on dialysis need more protein. A dietitian can set the right amount. Can I use low-sodium salt? Not if it contains potassium chloride, which most do. It can raise your potassium dangerously.

title: Cara hilangkan sedu (hiccups): what causes them, remedies to try, babies, and when hiccups need a doctor
desc: Hiccups usually stop on their own within minutes. Common triggers, the remedies people swear by and what the evidence says, why baby hiccups are rarely a worry, and the causes and treatment of hiccups that last more than 2 days.
headings: What causes hiccups? · Cara hilangkan sedu: remedies to try · Hiccups in babies · Hiccups that won’t stop · When to see a doctor
keywords: Guides Cara hilangkan sedu (hiccups) Hiccups Sedu Diaphragm kecemasan emergency a&e hospital aesthetic estetik kecantikan beauty kulit skin botox filler laser facial
body: Hiccups are often triggered by eating too much or too fast, fizzy drinks, alcohol, spicy food, swallowing air, stress or excitement. Often there is no obvious cause. Popular remedies include holding your breath, sipping ice-cold water, swallowing a spoonful of sugar and pulling your knees to your chest. They are safe to try, but there is no good evidence that any one works best. Baby hiccups are common and harmless, and usually stop within 5 to 15 minutes. See a doctor if hiccups last more than 48 hours or keep coming back. Causes include acid reflux, some medicines such as dexamethasone, and rarely nerve or brain problems. Get urgent help for hiccups with headache, weakness, numbness or loss of balance, or with chest pain or breathlessness. Hiccups are repeated spasms of the diaphragm. Each spasm is followed by the vocal cords closing suddenly, which makes the “hic”. Doctors group them by how long they last: Short-lived: a few minutes. Almost everyone gets these. Persistent: more than 48 hours, up to a month Intractable: more than a month Common triggers: eating too much or too quickly fizzy drinks and alcohol spicy, very hot or very cold food, or something very cold straight after something hot swallowing air, for example when chewing gum, smoking or talking while eating stress, strong emotions or excitement These are commonly suggested, including by the NHS. They are generally safe, but there is no good evidence that one works better than another, or that they work for everyone: hold your breath for a short while sip ice-cold water, or gargle with it swallow a teaspoon of granulated sugar bite on a lemon or taste a little vinegar pull your knees up to your chest and lean forward breathe into a paper bag, keeping it away from your face. Never use a plastic bag. What about special straws? A 2021 online study of a rigid drinking straw that makes you suck hard and swallow reported success in about 9 out of 10 users. But the study had no comparison group, relied on users’ own reports, and one of the authors invented the device, so better trials are needed. To prevent hiccups: eat slowly, have smaller meals, and cut down on fizzy drinks and alcohol. Eating more slowly and having smaller meals can help prevent hiccups. Hiccups are very common in babies and are usually harmless. A Malaysian Paediatric Association doctor notes that they often last 5 to 15 minutes, sometimes a couple of hours, and tend to bother parents more than the baby. They are often caused by feeding quickly, swallowing air, or crying for a long time. Try changing your baby’s position, burping them and helping them relax. Feed when your baby is calm, check the latch, feed in a more upright position, and keep your baby upright for about 30 minutes after feeds. See a doctor if hiccups come with frequent forceful vomiting, poor weight gain, crying or arching the back during feeds, or coughing or choking. These can be signs of reflux. Hiccups lasting more than 2 days are uncommon and usually have a cause. They can make it hard to eat, sleep and talk. Possible causes: acid reflux (GERD) and gastritis, among the most common medicines, including the steroid dexamethasone, sleeping tablets (benzodiazepines), strong painkillers and some chemotherapy. See also our guide to steroid tablets . recent surgery, especially under general anaesthetic chest problems such as pneumonia or pleurisy kidney failure and low calcium levels. See our guide to kidney disease . shingles rarely, stroke, a brain tumour, multiple sclerosis, or a tumour in the chest or tummy What doctors do: blood tests for salts and kidney function, a chest X-ray and an ECG, and sometimes a camera test for reflux or a scan. Treating the cause, for example reflux, often stops the hiccups. Don’t stop a prescribed medicine without talking to your doctor. If hiccups continue, doctors may try medicines such as baclofen, gabapentin, metoclopramide or chlorpromazine. Evidence for these is limited, and they don’t work for everyone. See a GP if: hiccups last more than 48 hours they keep coming back and affect your daily life, eating or sleep a baby’s hiccups come with feeding problems or poor weight gain Get urgent help or call 999 if hiccups come with: headache, weakness, numbness, slurred speech or loss of balance, which can be signs of a stroke chest pain or sudden breathlessness. See our guide to chest pain . What is sedu in English? Hiccups. Sedu is also called cegukan in Malay. How do I stop hiccups fast? Try holding your breath, sipping ice-cold water, swallowing a spoonful of sugar or pulling your knees to your chest. They are safe, but no remedy works for everyone, and most hiccups stop on their own within minutes. Why do I keep getting hiccups? Common triggers are eating too fast, big meals, fizzy drinks, alcohol, spicy food and stress. If they keep coming back or last more than 2 days, see a doctor to check for reflux or a medicine side effect. Are hiccups in babies normal? Yes. They are common and harmless. See a doctor if they come with forceful vomiting, poor weight gain or distress during feeds. How long is too long for hiccups? See a doctor if they last more than 48 hours. Can medicines cause hiccups? Yes. Steroids such as dexamethasone, sleeping tablets, strong painkillers and some chemotherapy can cause hiccups. Don’t stop a medicine without talking to your doctor.

title: Ubat sakit tekak: sore throat remedies that work, lozenges and sprays, and when you need a doctor
desc: Most sore throats are caused by viruses and get better within a week. What genuinely helps the pain, which lozenges and sprays are worth buying and who shouldn’t use them, what about honey and traditional remedies, when antibiotics are needed, and the warning signs.
headings: What causes a sore throat? · What helps a sore throat · Lozenges and sprays: are they worth buying? · Do I need antibiotics? · When to get help
keywords: Guides Ubat sakit tekak (sore throat) Sore throat Pharyngitis Sakit tekak denggi aedes nyamuk mosquito jerebu api ipu air pollutant index smoke mengandung hamil pregnancy antenatal kecemasan emergency a&e hospital aesthetic estetik kecantikan beauty kulit skin botox filler laser facial
body: Most sore throats are viral and last about a week. Most people recover without antibiotics, even when bacteria are the cause. Paracetamol is the safest painkiller to start with. Ibuprofen can help too, but avoid it if you might have dengue. Medicated lozenges and sprays reduce pain a little. Flurbiprofen lozenges are for ages 12 and over, and no lozenges should be given to children under 4. Cold drinks, ice lollies, soft food and, for adults, salt water gargles can ease the pain. Honey may help, but never give it to babies under 1. Get urgent help for difficulty breathing or swallowing, drooling, noisy breathing, or one-sided swelling at the back of the mouth. People taking carbimazole should get urgent advice for any sore throat. Viruses: the most common cause, including colds (selsema) and flu Bacteria: mainly group A streptococcus (strep throat). See our tonsillitis guide . Irritation: smoking or vaping, second-hand smoke, shouting or overusing your voice, dry air and mouth breathing Acid reflux , especially with a sore throat in the morning. See our GERD guide . Allergies and post-nasal drip . See our resdung guide . Haze: the Ministry of Health lists sore throat among the effects of haze, and advises staying indoors, drinking plenty of water and wearing a mask outdoors. See our haze guide . Painkillers: Paracetamol for pain or fever. Check the label of any cold remedy, as many already contain paracetamol. Ibuprofen can also help if it suits you. Avoid it if you might have dengue, if you have a stomach ulcer, or in late pregnancy. See our painkiller guide . Home measures: Cold or warm drinks, whichever feels better, and plenty of fluids Ice cubes, ice lollies and soft, cool foods. Avoid small hard sweets for young children, as they can cause choking. Salt water gargle for adults: half a teaspoon of salt in a glass of warm water. Don’t ask children to gargle. Honey may help symptoms of colds, and is commonly used in warm water. Don’t give honey to babies under 1. Rest your voice and avoid smoke. Traditional remedies such as asam jawa, halia (ginger) and limau are widely used. We found no good trials of them for sore throat. They are generally harmless in food amounts, but don’t rely on them if you have warning signs. Most sore throats are caused by viruses and clear up within about a week. UK guidance says medicated lozenges containing a local anaesthetic, an anti-inflammatory or an antiseptic may reduce sore throat pain by a small amount in adults. There is no evidence that ordinary sweets, plain lozenges or mouthwashes help. Product type Good to know Anti-inflammatory lozenge (flurbiprofen) Ages 12 and over. Up to 5 a day for no more than 3 days. Not for people allergic to aspirin or anti-inflammatories, with a stomach ulcer, or in late pregnancy. Up to half of users notice taste changes, numbness or nausea. Antiseptic lozenge (such as amylmetacresol with dichlorobenzyl alcohol) Not for children under 6. See a doctor if you aren’t better after 3 days. Anti-inflammatory spray (benzydamine) Dose depends on age and weight. Use with caution if you have asthma. Numbing products (benzocaine, lidocaine) Benzocaine shouldn’t be used in children under 2, because of a rare but dangerous blood reaction. Children: don’t give any lozenge to a child under 4, because of the choking risk. Ask a pharmacist which products suit your child’s age. Usually not. Antibiotics shorten a sore throat by only about 16 hours on average, and most people get better without them. In a Malaysian survey, 79% of people wrongly believed antibiotics cure viral infections. Malaysia’s national antimicrobial guideline uses a scoring system based on fever, swollen neck glands, pus on the tonsils, the absence of a cough, and age. A doctor considers antibiotics, usually penicillin or amoxicillin, only when the score is high enough to suggest strep throat. See our tonsillitis guide for details. Steroids: a single dose of a steroid can ease severe sore throat pain a little faster. A 2017 BMJ guideline suggests it as an option for some people aged 5 and over, but UK guidance doesn’t recommend it routinely. It is a decision for your doctor. Call 999 or go to an emergency department for: difficulty breathing, or high-pitched noisy breathing being unable to swallow, or drooling symptoms getting worse very quickly See a doctor urgently for: swelling on one side at the back of the mouth, or difficulty speaking or opening your mouth. This can be a throat abscess (quinsy). a sore throat, fever or mouth ulcers if you take carbimazole for an overactive thyroid. Stop the medicine and get urgent advice, as it can rarely affect your white blood cells. See our thyroid guide . a baby under 3 months with a temperature of 38°C or more See a doctor if: your sore throat hasn’t improved after a week you have a weakened immune system you have a rash or swollen joints your child is under 5 and unwell A sore throat can also be part of a flu-like illness a few weeks after HIV infection, and some sexually transmitted infections can affect the throat. If you are worried, see our guides to HIV and STI testing . What is sakit tekak in English? Sore throat. Ubat sakit tekak means sore throat medicine. What is the best ubat sakit tekak? Paracetamol is a good first choice for pain. Medicated lozenges or sprays can help a little in adults. Cold drinks, ice lollies and salt water gargles also help. Avoid ibuprofen if you might have dengue. How can I get rid of a sore throat fast? There is no instant cure, as most sore throats are viral and last about a week. Painkillers, cool drinks, lozenges and resting your voice ease the pain while it heals. Do I need antibiotics for a sore throat? Usually not. Antibiotics only shorten symptoms by about 16 hours and are used when a doctor suspects strep throat. Can I give my child lozenges? Not under 4, because of the choking risk. Many medicated lozenges are only for children over 6 or 12. Ask a pharmacist. Does salt water help a sore throat? Many people find it soothing. Use half a teaspoon of salt in a glass of warm water, and don’t ask children to gargle. When is a sore throat serious? When you have difficulty breathing or swallowing, drooling, one-sided swelling at the back of the mouth, or a sore throat while taking carbimazole. Get urgent help.

title: Sakit perut sebelah kiri atau kanan: what tummy pain on each side can mean, and when it’s an emergency
desc: Where your tummy hurts gives useful clues. A guide to the likely causes of pain on the left, right, upper and lower tummy, why diverticulitis in Asians is often on the right, causes in women and children, what to tell your doctor, and the signs that need emergency care.
headings: Tummy pain by area · Sakit perut sebelah kanan: right-sided pain · Sakit perut sebelah kiri: left-sided pain · Causes in women · Tummy pain in children · What to tell the doctor · When tummy pain is an emergency
keywords: Guides Sakit perut kiri dan kanan Abdominal pain Sakit perut Appendicitis denggi aedes nyamuk mosquito mengandung hamil pregnancy antenatal kecemasan emergency a&e hospital klinik doctor doktor gp aesthetic estetik kecantikan beauty kulit skin botox filler laser facial
body: Upper right pain is often from the gallbladder or liver. Upper middle and left pain can be gastritis, an ulcer, or pancreatitis, which spreads to the back. Appendicitis usually starts around the belly button and moves to the lower right within hours. In Western countries diverticulitis is usually on the left, but in Asian studies it is often on the right, so it can mimic appendicitis. Women with lower tummy pain who could be pregnant should take a pregnancy test. One-sided pain with shoulder-tip pain or fainting can be an ectopic pregnancy. Go to an emergency department for sudden severe pain, a hard swollen tummy, vomiting blood or green vomit, black stools, or pain in pregnancy. Where Common causes Less common but serious Upper right (kanan atas) Gallstones, gallbladder inflammation, hepatitis Bile duct blockage, liver or bile duct cancer Upper middle (ulu hati) Gastritis , stomach ulcer, reflux Pancreatitis, heart attack, stomach cancer Upper left (kiri atas) Gastritis, trapped wind Pancreatitis, enlarged or ruptured spleen Around the belly button Gastroenteritis, early appendicitis Bowel obstruction Lower right (kanan bawah) Appendicitis, constipation, in Asians right-sided diverticulitis Ovarian cyst, ectopic pregnancy, hernia Lower left (kiri bawah) Constipation , trapped wind, IBS, diverticulitis Ovarian cyst, ectopic pregnancy, hernia Lower middle Bladder infection, period pain Pelvic infection, bladder stones Side or back Kidney stones , kidney infection Aortic aneurysm in older people Pain can move, and different people feel the same problem in different places. Use this table as a guide only. See our guides to pain in the side and lower back and chest pain . Gallstones: pain in the middle of the tummy or under the right ribs, lasting more than 30 minutes and sometimes several hours, often with feeling sick, and sometimes spreading to the right shoulder blade. Get urgent help if it lasts more than 30 minutes, and call 999 if you also have a fever or shivering, yellow skin or eyes, or pain spreading to your back with vomiting. Appendicitis: pain usually starts around the belly button and moves to the lower right within a few hours. It gets worse when you move, cough or press on it, often with a fever, poor appetite or vomiting. In pregnancy, young children and older people, the pain may be milder or in a different place. Diverticulitis on the right: in Western countries more than 90% of diverticular disease is on the left. In Asian studies it is often on the right. In one Singapore study, 73% of uncomplicated diverticulitis was right-sided, mostly in people around 50. It can feel like appendicitis, with constant pain, fever and sometimes blood or mucus in the stool. Kidney stone or infection on the right side, often with pain spreading to the groin, urine symptoms or fever. Constipation and trapped wind are very common causes of lower left pain, often with bloating and relief after opening your bowels. Irritable bowel syndrome causes cramping pain, bloating and changes in bowel habit that come and go. Diverticulitis in Western patterns is usually lower left, with constant severe pain, fever and sometimes blood in the stool. Pancreatitis: sudden severe pain in the upper tummy that spreads to the sides and back, is worse after eating or lying down, and eases when you lean forward. It is usually caused by gallstones or heavy drinking, and is an emergency. Spleen: pain under the left ribs, sometimes felt in the left shoulder. A ruptured spleen after an injury is an emergency. Kidney stone or infection on the left side. Where the pain is, how it started and what else you feel all help a doctor narrow down the cause. Ectopic pregnancy: usually between 4 and 12 weeks of pregnancy, with one-sided lower tummy pain, vaginal bleeding, and pain at the tip of the shoulder, which can be a sign of internal bleeding. Sudden sharp pain with dizziness or fainting is an emergency. Take a pregnancy test if there is any chance you are pregnant. Ovarian cysts : a cyst that bursts or twists causes sudden, severe, sharp pain on one side of the pelvis. Get urgent help. Endometriosis, period pain and pelvic infection cause lower tummy pain, often on both sides. Most tummy pain in children is caused by constipation, a stomach bug, a urine infection or a recent virus, and often no clear cause is found. Watch for: Mesenteric adenitis: swollen glands in the tummy after a virus, causing lower right pain and fever. It can look like appendicitis, and settles within 1 to 4 weeks. Appendicitis can occur at any age. Young children may not describe it clearly. Intussusception: the most common cause of a blocked bowel between about 6 months and 3 years. Episodes of severe pain last 15 to 20 minutes, the child seems well in between, and there may be vomiting and dark red, jelly-like stools. This is an emergency. Testicular torsion: boys, especially aged 12 to 18, may feel the pain of a twisted testicle in the tummy. Almost all testicles can be saved within 4 to 6 hours, so go to an emergency department straight away for sudden testicle or groin pain. See a doctor if a child’s tummy pain lasts more than 24 hours, and urgently if they won’t move, have a fever over 38°C, green vomit or a lump in the groin. where the pain is, and whether it has moved or spreads anywhere what it feels like: sharp, cramping, burning, constant or coming in waves whether it started suddenly or gradually, and how bad it is what makes it better or worse, such as eating, moving or lying down other symptoms: vomiting, diarrhoea or constipation, fever, yellow eyes, black stools, blood in the urine, weight loss your medicines, including steroids and blood thinners, and alcohol use whether you could be pregnant Painkillers: hospital studies have found that giving strong painkillers while doctors assess tummy pain doesn’t lead to missed diagnoses. Don’t let painkillers delay you getting checked, and avoid anti-inflammatory painkillers if the pain could be from your stomach or if you might have dengue. Call 999 or go to an emergency department if you have: sudden, severe tummy pain, or pain that suddenly gets much worse a hard, swollen or very tender tummy vomiting blood, or vomit that is green or looks like coffee grounds black, sticky stools, or a lot of blood in your stool pain with yellow skin or eyes, or fever and shivering pain after an injury pain with a rash that doesn’t fade when pressed, or difficulty breathing being unable to pass urine, stool or wind pain in pregnancy upper tummy pain with sweating, breathlessness or pain spreading to the chest, arm or jaw, which can be a heart attack Don’t drive yourself. Older people, and those taking steroids or immune-suppressing medicines, can have serious problems with milder pain, so get checked early. See our guide on clinic or emergency department . What is sakit perut in English? Tummy ache or abdominal pain. Sebelah kiri means the left side and sebelah kanan means the right side. What causes sakit perut sebelah kanan bawah? Appendicitis is the most important cause to rule out. Constipation, right-sided diverticulitis (common in Asians), and in women ovarian cysts or ectopic pregnancy are also possible. What causes sakit perut sebelah kiri bawah? Constipation, trapped wind and irritable bowel syndrome are common causes. Diverticulitis, kidney stones and, in women, ovarian or pregnancy problems are also possible. What causes pain under the right ribs? Often the gallbladder, especially after a fatty meal, or the liver. Get urgent help if it lasts more than 30 minutes or comes with fever or yellow eyes. Can a heart attack feel like stomach pain? Yes. A heart attack can feel like indigestion or upper tummy pain, often with sweating, breathlessness or pain in the chest, arm or jaw. Call 999. When should I go to hospital for stomach pain? For sudden severe pain, a hard swollen tummy, vomiting blood, black stools, pain with fever and yellow eyes, or pain in pregnancy. Should I take painkillers before seeing a doctor? Painkillers don’t usually hide the cause, but don’t let them delay you getting checked. Avoid anti-inflammatory painkillers if the pain could be from your stomach or if you might have dengue.

title: Sakit dada sebelah kiri, kanan atau tengah: chest pain causes and when to call 999
desc: Chest pain is often caused by muscle strain, heartburn or anxiety, but it can be a heart attack, and you can’t tell the difference at home. Heart attack signs, why left-sided pain isn’t the only warning, other serious causes, clues to less serious ones, and what to do.
headings: Is it a heart attack? · What to do if you think it’s your heart · Chest pain on the left, right or centre · Other serious causes · Common, less serious causes · Chest pain in children and young people · When to call 999
keywords: Heart & diabetes Sakit dada (chest pain) Chest pain Heart attack Sakit dada kencing manis gula hba1c darah tinggi hypertension bp tekanan darah payudara kanser cancer mammogram pink october kecemasan emergency a&e hospital klinik doctor doktor gp
body: Heart attack pain is usually in the centre of the chest, not just the left, and can spread to the jaw, either arm, the back or the upper tummy. It often comes with sweating, nausea or breathlessness. Women, older people and people with diabetes may have only breathlessness, tiredness, dizziness or sweating, without obvious chest pain. Call 999 for chest pain that is sudden, severe, doesn’t go away, or comes with sweating, breathlessness or feeling faint. Don’t drive yourself. Malaysia’s heart attack guideline advises chewing one 300mg aspirin tablet straight away if you aren’t already taking aspirin and aren’t allergic. Pain that gets worse when you press on your chest or move is more likely to be muscular. Burning after meals suggests heartburn. But only tests can rule out the heart. Ischaemic heart disease is the leading cause of death in Malaysia, causing 17,421 deaths in 2024. It is the top cause of death in men and in people aged 41 to 59. Malaysians tend to have heart attacks about 6 years younger than people in international studies. Typical heart attack pain , according to Malaysia’s heart attack guideline: usually in the centre of the chest feels like pressure, squeezing, tightness or crushing, and may burn like indigestion may spread to the jaw, neck, either arm, the back or the upper tummy lasts more than a few minutes and doesn’t go away with rest often comes with sweating, nausea, breathlessness or feeling faint It isn’t always in the chest. Older people, women and people with diabetes may have only tiredness, breathlessness, dizziness, sweating or fainting. In a Malaysian study, patients who were women, had unusual symptoms or went to a GP first took longer to reach hospital. See our guide to heart attack and stroke . Call 999 or get someone to take you to the nearest hospital emergency department. Don’t drive yourself. Aspirin: Malaysia’s heart attack guideline advises chewing and swallowing one 300mg aspirin tablet straight away, if you aren’t already taking aspirin regularly and aren’t allergic to it. Plain aspirin is preferred. Don’t give aspirin to children. Use your own heart medicines, such as a GTN spray, as your doctor has advised. Sit down, rest and stay with someone until help arrives. Every minute counts, because treatment works best in the first hours. Hospitals do a heart tracing (ECG) within minutes of arrival, and repeat blood tests (troponin) to look for heart damage. Where Possible causes Centre (tengah) Heart attack or angina, heartburn and GERD , pericarditis, aortic dissection Left (kiri) Heart, muscle strain, costochondritis, pleurisy, pneumonia, collapsed lung, shingles, panic attack Right (kanan) Muscle strain or broken rib, pneumonia, pleurisy, pulmonary embolism, collapsed lung, gallstones, shingles Location doesn’t rule out the heart. Heart pain can spread to the right arm as well as the left, and sometimes isn’t in the chest at all. Don’t assume right-sided or central pain is safe. Pulmonary embolism (a blood clot in the lung): sudden breathlessness, pain that is worse when you breathe in, coughing up blood, and sometimes a swollen, painful calf. The risk is higher after long journeys of 4 hours or more, and after a hospital stay. Aortic dissection (a tear in the main artery): sudden, severe, tearing pain in the chest or upper back, sometimes with fainting or stroke-like weakness. Uncontrolled high blood pressure is a major risk. Collapsed lung (pneumothorax): sudden sharp pain on one side with breathlessness, most common in tall, slim young men and smokers. Pericarditis: sharp, stabbing pain that is worse when lying down, breathing in or swallowing, and eases when you lean forward. Pneumonia and pleurisy: sharp pain when you breathe in or cough, with fever and coloured phlegm. See our guide to pneumonia . All of these need emergency care. High blood pressure raises the risk of both heart attacks and aortic dissection. Muscle strain or costochondritis (inflamed rib cartilage): sharp pain at the front or side of the chest that gets worse when you move, breathe deeply or press on the area, often after exercise or lifting. Heartburn or reflux: burning behind the breastbone after eating or when lying down, with a sour taste, regurgitation or bloating. Anxiety or a panic attack: sharp chest pain with worry, a fast heartbeat, sweating and fast breathing. See our guides to anxiety and palpitations . Shingles: burning or tingling on one side of the chest, followed a few days later by a blistering rash. Antiviral medicine works best within 3 days of the rash. See our shingles guide . Gallstones: pain under the right ribs or in the upper tummy, sometimes felt in the lower chest, lasting more than 30 minutes. These clues can help, but don’t diagnose yourself . Heart pain can feel like heartburn, and people having a heart attack often feel anxious. If you have risk factors such as diabetes, high blood pressure, smoking or a family history of heart disease, get checked. Chest pain in children is rarely due to the heart. It is most often caused by the chest wall muscles or cartilage, asthma, pneumonia, reflux or anxiety. See a doctor promptly if a child has chest pain: during exercise, or with fainting or near-fainting that doesn’t go away with a heart condition or past Kawasaki disease with a family history of sudden unexplained death or heart muscle disease Call 999 for chest pain that: is sudden and doesn’t go away, or lasts more than 10 minutes feels like pressure, squeezing, tightness or burning spreads to your arm, neck, jaw, back or stomach comes with sweating, nausea, breathlessness, light-headedness or fainting is sudden, severe and tearing, or comes with coughing up blood or a swollen calf See a doctor the same day for chest pain that comes and goes with exercise and settles with rest, which can be angina, or for any chest pain you are unsure about. See our guide on clinic or emergency department . What is sakit dada in English? Chest pain. Sebelah kiri means the left side, sebelah kanan the right side, and tengah the centre. Is left-sided chest pain always the heart? No. It is often muscular or caused by heartburn or anxiety. But heart attack pain is usually central and can spread to either side, so you can’t tell at home. Call 999 if unsure. Can right-sided chest pain be a heart attack? Yes, it is possible. Heart pain can spread to the right arm, and right-sided pain can also be serious lung problems such as a blood clot. Get urgent help if it is severe or comes with breathlessness. Should I take aspirin for chest pain? Malaysia’s heart attack guideline advises chewing one 300mg aspirin tablet straight away for a suspected heart attack, if you aren’t already taking aspirin and aren’t allergic. Call 999 first. How do I know if chest pain is muscular? Muscular pain usually gets worse when you press on the area, move or breathe deeply, often after exercise or lifting. But only tests can rule out the heart. Can gastric pain feel like chest pain? Yes. Reflux causes burning behind the breastbone, especially after meals. But heart attack pain can also feel like indigestion, so don’t assume. When should I go to hospital for chest pain? Straight away for sudden, severe or lasting chest pain, or chest pain with sweating, breathlessness, nausea or fainting. Call 999 and don’t drive yourself.

title: Klinik pergigian kerajaan: government dental clinics in Malaysia, fees, appointments and services
desc: Malaysia has more than 1,700 government oral health facilities, with fees of a few ringgit for most treatments. What scaling, fillings, extractions and dentures cost, who is treated free, how to book through MySejahtera, school dental services and specialist referrals.
headings: What government dental services are there? · How much does it cost? · How to get an appointment · Waiting times and when to go private · Oral health in Malaysia
keywords: Guides Government dental clinics Klinik pergigian Government dental clinic Oral health mengandung hamil pregnancy antenatal kecemasan emergency a&e hospital klinik doctor doktor gp
