body: The Ministry of Health had 1,737 oral health facilities in 2023, including 595 dental clinics inside health clinics, 911 school dental clinics and 40 mobile dental clinics. For Malaysian outpatients, the official schedule lists scaling at RM2 a visit, extractions at RM1 a tooth and fillings at RM2 a surface. Children aged 1 to 6 receive free dental treatment, babies under 1 are exempt from fees, and pregnant mothers referred with the pink antenatal book are treated free. You can book an appointment through MySejahtera, available at 610 clinics by the end of 2023. Dental emergencies may be seen as walk-ins after assessment. Root canals, braces, dentures and specialist gum or oral surgery care are available, but some have waiting lists. In 2023, the Ministry of Health had 1,737 oral health facilities : 595 dental clinics inside Klinik Kesihatan or maternal and child health clinics 63 standalone dental clinics, and 77 in hospitals 911 school dental clinics 26 in urban and rural transformation centres (UTC and RTC) 40 mobile dental clinics, with teams visiting schools, kindergartens, toddlers and older people Services at primary dental clinics include check-ups, scaling, fillings, extractions, simple root canal treatment at some clinics, dentures, emergency treatment and an oral cancer check for new adult patients. School dental service: pupils from Standard 1 to Form 5 in government and government-aided schools get a yearly dental check, with prevention, scaling, fillings and extractions. Specialist care: the ministry had 475 dental specialists in 2023, covering orthodontics (braces), gum disease, oral surgery, children’s dentistry, restorative dentistry and special care dentistry. You are usually referred by a government dental officer. Charges are set by the Fees (Medical) Order. These are the official outpatient charges for Malaysian citizens, from the ministry’s Oral Health Programme schedule: Treatment Charge Scaling and polishing RM2 per visit Extraction RM1 per tooth Filling RM2 per surface Root canal treatment RM4 per tooth Crown RM3 Partial denture RM10, plus RM2 per tooth Full denture RM50 per jaw Surgical removal of a tooth RM15 (simple) to RM50 (complex impacted tooth) Fixed braces RM500 per arch Removable orthodontic appliance RM100 to RM200 A general outpatient visit costs RM1. Some websites quote higher figures for fillings, so check the current charges at your clinic. Who is treated free: Babies under 1: exempt from visit and treatment fees Children aged 1 to 6: free dental treatment, apart from orthodontic appliances. Bring a letter from their nursery or kindergarten to waive the visit fee. Pregnant mothers: free registration, and free treatment when referred from antenatal care with the pink book (Buku Rekod Ibu). Dentures and orthodontic appliances aren’t covered, and walk-ins without a referral are charged normally. Civil servants: exempt from outpatient treatment charges Non-citizens pay much higher charges, which vary between facilities. Ask at the clinic before treatment. Most routine treatment at government dental clinics costs a few ringgit for Malaysians. MySejahtera: dental appointments have been bookable nationwide since 15 May 2023. Open Appointments , choose the dental service, then pick a clinic, date and time. By the end of 2023, 610 dental clinics were on the system. Walk-in: dental emergencies such as a painful tooth may be seen without an appointment after assessment, but routine care is mainly by appointment. Bring: your MyKad, your child’s MyKid or birth certificate, the pink book if you are pregnant, and any referral or exemption letter. Finding a clinic: the app shows nearby clinics, and the Oral Health Programme and MyGOV websites list government dental clinics by state. Opening hours vary. Most clinics keep government office hours, so check before you go. Government dental care is very affordable, but demand is high. The Malaysian Dental Association and industry groups have raised concerns about long waiting times, and in 2026 about contract dental officers whose contracts ended. Waits are usually longest for specialist care such as braces. A private dentist may suit you better if you need treatment quickly, after hours or at weekends, or want cosmetic treatment. Private clinics set their own fees, so ask for a quote first. Go to a hospital emergency department or call 999 for facial swelling spreading towards the eye or neck, difficulty swallowing or breathing, a high fever with dental pain, or a serious injury to the face or jaw. See our guide to toothache (sakit gigi) . Of 2.66 million primary school pupils examined in 2023, 38% were free of tooth decay. Only about a third of Malaysians aged 60 and over have 20 or more natural teeth, against a national target of half by 2030. Only 1 in 10 adults used government primary dental care in 2023. Pregnant mothers are referred for a dental check, but in 2023 only 62.5% received one. A yearly check-up helps catch decay and gum disease early, when treatment is simpler and cheaper. Brush twice a day with fluoride toothpaste and cut down on sugary food and drinks. How much does a government dental clinic charge? For Malaysian outpatients, the official schedule lists scaling at RM2 a visit, extractions at RM1 a tooth, fillings at RM2 a surface and root canal treatment at RM4 a tooth. How do I book a government dental appointment? Use the MySejahtera app: open Appointments, choose the dental service, then pick a clinic, date and time. Is dental treatment free for children? Yes for young children. Babies under 1 are exempt from fees, and children aged 1 to 6 receive free dental treatment, apart from orthodontic appliances. School pupils have yearly checks through the school dental service. Can I walk in to a government dental clinic? Dental emergencies such as toothache may be seen after assessment. Routine treatment is mainly by appointment. Can I get braces at a government clinic? Yes, through a specialist orthodontic referral. Fixed braces are charged at RM500 per arch, and there are often waiting lists. Are dental check-ups free for pregnant women? Yes, when you are referred from antenatal care with the pink book. Dentures and orthodontic appliances aren’t covered. What is the English for klinik pergigian? Dental clinic. Klinik pergigian kerajaan means a government dental clinic.

title: Sakit pinggang sebelah kiri atau kanan: lower back and side pain, common causes and red flags
desc: Most lower back pain is a strained muscle that gets better within a few weeks. But pain on one side can also come from the kidneys, gallbladder, pancreas or a gynaecological problem. How to tell them apart, what helps, and the warning signs that need urgent care.
headings: The most common cause: muscle and ligament strain · Pain on the left or right side: what could it be? · Is it my kidneys or my back? · What helps muscular back pain · When to get help
keywords: Guides Sakit pinggang (lower back pain) Low back pain Flank pain Sakit pinggang denggi aedes nyamuk mosquito mengandung hamil pregnancy antenatal kecemasan emergency a&e hospital aesthetic estetik kecantikan beauty kulit skin botox filler laser facial
body: Most lower back pain comes from muscles or ligaments, and up to 85% of people recover within 6 weeks. Staying active helps more than bed rest. Muscle pain usually gets worse when you bend, twist or press on the area. Kidney pain is deeper, higher under the ribs, doesn’t change with movement, and often comes with fever or urine symptoms. One-sided causes include kidney stones, kidney infection, the sacroiliac joint, shingles before the rash, and in women, period pain and endometriosis. Paracetamol on its own isn’t recommended for lower back pain. Short courses of anti-inflammatory painkillers can help, but avoid them in suspected dengue. Get emergency help for numbness around the genitals or bottom, bladder or bowel problems, weakness or numbness in both legs, or sudden severe pain with collapse. Most lower back pain is “non-specific”: it comes from the muscles, ligaments and joints of the back, often after lifting, bending, twisting or sitting for long periods. It is common, and becomes more so with age. Signs that it is muscular: a dull ache or spasm over the lower back, on one or both sides worse when you bend, twist, lift, cough, sneeze or press on the area eases when you rest or change position In Malaysian studies, back pain was especially common among nurses, drivers and office workers. Heavy lifting, long hours of sitting or standing, awkward postures, obesity, smoking and stress all increase the risk. Cause Where and what it feels like Other clues Muscle strain Either side, over the muscles beside the spine Worse with movement and pressing Kidney stone Severe cramping pain in the side or back, coming in waves and spreading to the groin Blood in the urine, nausea, restlessness Kidney infection Pain in the side or back, just under the ribs Fever, shivering, burning or frequent urine. See our UTI guide . Sacroiliac joint Lower back and buttock, one or both sides, sometimes spreading to the hip or thigh Worse with long sitting or standing, or turning Sciatica Back or buttock pain with pain, tingling or numbness down one leg See our slipped disc guide Shingles (kayap) Burning or tingling on one side only A blistering rash appears a few days later. See our shingles guide . Gallbladder (right) Pain under the right ribs or upper tummy, sometimes to the back or right shoulder Often after fatty meals; fever or yellow eyes need urgent care Pancreatitis (often left or central) Sudden severe upper-tummy pain spreading to the back, eased by leaning forward Vomiting. An emergency. Spleen (left) Pain behind the left lower ribs After an injury, can mean a ruptured spleen. An emergency. Women: period pain and endometriosis can cause lower back pain. Pelvic girdle pain affects up to 1 in 5 pregnant women, on one or both sides. Ovarian cysts, pelvic infection and ectopic pregnancy can also refer pain to the back. Sudden severe pelvic pain needs urgent care, and if you could be pregnant, take a pregnancy test . Keeping active and doing gentle exercises usually helps lower back pain recover faster than resting in bed. Kidney pain is felt higher up, under the ribs on one or both sides of the spine, and can spread to the groin. It is a deep, constant ache or sharp pain in waves. It usually doesn’t change when you move, and often comes with fever, nausea, painful urination or blood in the urine. Back pain sits lower, over the spine and the muscles beside it, and changes with movement and position. Long-term kidney disease is usually painless, so pain alone isn’t a good guide to kidney health. If you are worried about your kidneys, a urine test and blood test are what count. See our guide to kidney disease . Keep moving. Carry on with normal activities as much as you can. If you need to rest, keep it to a day or two, as longer bed rest slows recovery. Heat or ice: heat for stiffness or spasm, ice for a recent strain. Gentle exercise: walking, swimming, stretching and yoga can help, and so can physiotherapy for pain that lasts. Painkillers: UK guidance doesn’t recommend paracetamol on its own for lower back pain. A short course of an anti-inflammatory painkiller such as ibuprofen at the lowest effective dose may help, but it isn’t suitable for everyone, including people with stomach ulcers, kidney disease or heart problems. Avoid anti-inflammatories if you might have dengue. See our painkiller guide . Back belts and corsets aren’t recommended. Massage (urut) may give short-term relief. Choose a practitioner registered with the Traditional and Complementary Medicine Council, and avoid forceful manipulation, especially if you have numbness or weakness. Scans aren’t usually needed for ordinary back pain. Doctors consider an MRI if the pain is disabling or lasts more than 6 weeks, after a serious injury, or if there are nerve problems or signs of infection or cancer. Call 999 or go to an emergency department for back pain with: numbness around the genitals or bottom new problems controlling your bladder or bowels weakness, numbness or tingling in both legs chest pain pain after a serious fall or accident sudden, severe tummy or back pain with pale skin, breathlessness or collapse, especially in older men or smokers, as this can be a burst aortic aneurysm See a doctor urgently for: back or side pain with fever or shivering severe pain that comes in waves, or blood in the urine sudden severe pain, or pain in pregnancy See a doctor soon if: you have unexplained weight loss, a history of cancer, a weak immune system, pain that is worse at night or not eased by rest, or pain that isn’t improving after a few weeks. What is sakit pinggang in English? Lower back pain, or pain around the waist. Pain on one side is sometimes called flank pain. What causes sakit pinggang sebelah kiri? Usually a muscle strain. Other causes include a kidney stone or infection, the sacroiliac joint, shingles, and less often the pancreas or spleen. In women, period pain and endometriosis can cause it. What causes sakit pinggang sebelah kanan? Usually a muscle strain. A kidney stone or infection, gallbladder problems and, in women, gynaecological causes are also possible. How do I know if back pain is from my kidneys? Kidney pain is higher, under the ribs, doesn’t change with movement, and often comes with fever, urine symptoms or blood in the urine. Muscle pain changes as you move. Should I rest in bed with back pain? No more than a day or two. Staying active helps you recover faster. When is back pain an emergency? With numbness around the genitals or bottom, bladder or bowel problems, weakness in both legs, chest pain, or sudden severe pain with collapse. Call 999. Is urut good for back pain? Massage may give short-term relief. Use a registered practitioner and avoid forceful manipulation, especially if you have numbness or weakness.

title: Sakit tumit dan tapak kaki (heel and sole pain): plantar fasciitis, stretches and when it’s a sign of something else
desc: A stabbing pain in the heel with your first steps in the morning is usually plantar fasciitis. Most people get better within a year with stretches, good footwear and patience. What helps, what to avoid, other causes of heel and sole pain, and when foot pain is a sign of diabetes.
headings: Plantar fasciitis: the most common cause of heel pain · What helps plantar fasciitis · What about heel spurs? · Other causes of heel and sole pain · Sakit tapak kaki as a sign of disease: diabetes and nerve damage · When to see a doctor
keywords: Guides Sakit tumit (heel pain) Plantar fasciitis Heel pain Diabetic neuropathy denggi aedes nyamuk mosquito kencing manis gula hba1c aesthetic estetik kecantikan beauty kulit skin botox filler laser facial
body: Plantar fasciitis causes a stabbing pain on the inner heel, worst with the first steps in the morning or after resting. It affects about 1 in 10 people at some point. It is most common between ages 40 and 60, and in people who are overweight, stand for long hours, have tight calves or wear shoes with poor cushioning. Stretching the calf and the sole, cushioned shoes with arch support, and ice help most. Off-the-shelf insoles work as well as custom-made ones. Heel spurs are common in people with no pain, and they don’t cause plantar fasciitis. Steroid injections give short-term relief and carry a risk of tearing the fascia. Burning, tingling or numb soles can mean nerve damage from diabetes or low vitamin B12. People with diabetes should have their feet checked at least once a year. The plantar fascia is a thick band of tissue running from the heel to the toes, supporting the arch of the foot. When it is overloaded, it becomes painful. Doctors now sometimes call it plantar fasciopathy, because the tissue is worn rather than truly inflamed. Typical signs: a stabbing pain on the inner part of the heel worst with the first steps in the morning, or after sitting for a while eases after a few minutes of walking, then returns by the end of the day or after activity hurts to climb stairs or raise your toes Who gets it: it is most common between the ages of 40 and 60, and in people who: are overweight. See our BMI calculator . stand or walk for long hours at work, especially on hard floors run or dance, or have suddenly increased their activity have tight calf muscles, flat feet or high arches wear shoes with poor cushioning, or walk barefoot on hard surfaces About 80% of people improve within 12 months without surgery. Stretch: stretching the calf and the sole of the foot is one of the most effective treatments. A common routine is to hold each stretch for about 10 seconds and repeat it several times a day, especially before your first steps in the morning. For the sole, sit down, cross your foot over your knee and gently pull your toes back towards your shin. Strengthen: exercises such as slow heel raises worked better than stretching alone in one trial at 3 months. Footwear: wear cushioned shoes with good arch support, at home as well as outside. Off-the-shelf insoles or heel cups worked as well as custom-made ones. Avoid flip-flops, backless slippers, high heels and going barefoot on hard floors. Ice: roll your foot over a frozen water bottle for up to 20 minutes, a few times a day. Rest from painful activity: swap running for cycling or swimming for a while. Lose weight if you are overweight. Painkillers: paracetamol, or ibuprofen tablets or gel, for short periods. Don’t take anti-inflammatory painkillers for more than a month without seeing a doctor, and avoid them if you might have dengue. See our painkiller guide . Physiotherapy can help, including taping, which gives short-term relief. Evidence for night splints is mixed. If it isn’t getting better: Steroid injections give short-term relief at best. Repeated injections carry a risk of the fascia tearing and thinning of the heel’s fat pad. Shockwave therapy is an option for long-standing cases, with mixed results. Surgery is rarely needed, and is usually only considered after 12 months of other treatment. Scans are usually only needed if pain lasts more than 3 months despite treatment. Supportive shoes, daily stretches and a gradual return to activity help most heel pain settle within a year. A heel spur is a small bony growth on the heel bone that shows up on X-rays. Spurs are common in people who have no heel pain at all, and they stay after the pain has gone. Orthopaedic surgeons say the spur doesn’t cause plantar fasciitis pain, so treatment focuses on the fascia, not the spur. Cause What it feels like Achilles tendinopathy Pain and stiffness at the back of the heel, above the heel bone Heel fat pad bruising Deep bruised pain in the middle of the heel, often after walking on hard ground Stress fracture Pain that builds with activity and hurts when you squeeze the heel, often after a sudden increase in walking or running Tarsal tunnel syndrome Burning, tingling or numbness in the sole, from a trapped nerve Morton’s neuroma Sharp, burning pain near the toes, like standing on a stone Metatarsalgia Pain in the ball of the foot Sever’s disease Heel pain in active children, at the growth plate Arthritis can also cause foot pain. Pain at night or deep bone pain should be checked by a doctor. Pain in the sole that feels like burning, pins and needles or numbness , especially in both feet, is different from plantar fasciitis. It can be a sign of nerve damage (peripheral neuropathy). Diabetes is the most common cause. In Malaysia, about 1 in 6 adults has diabetes, and about 2 in 5 of them don’t know it. Low vitamin B12 is another cause, more likely with a vegan diet, long-term metformin or acid-reducing medicines (PPIs). Up to half of people with diabetic nerve damage have no symptoms, so the feet can be injured without pain. Malaysia’s diabetic foot guideline recommends that everyone with diabetes has their feet checked for nerve damage and poor circulation when diagnosed and at least once a year. If you have diabetes, get help within 24 hours for: a wound or ulcer, signs of infection, black or dark skin, or a foot that is unexpectedly hot, red or swollen. Wear footwear at all times, indoors and outdoors, if your doctor says your feet are at risk. Get urgent help if: you have severe pain after an injury, or heard a snap or pop you can’t walk or put weight on the foot your foot looks misshapen your foot is hot and swollen, or you feel feverish or shivery you have diabetes and a wound, infection or colour change in your foot See a doctor if: heel pain hasn’t improved after 2 weeks of self-care you have tingling, burning or loss of feeling in your feet you have diabetes and any foot pain you have pain at night or deep bone pain What is sakit tumit in English? Heel pain. The most common cause in adults is plantar fasciitis. Why does my heel hurt in the morning? Pain with your first steps in the morning that eases as you walk is typical of plantar fasciitis, a strain of the band of tissue under the foot. How long does plantar fasciitis last? It often takes months. About 8 in 10 people improve within 12 months without surgery, and most get better with stretches and good footwear. What is the best treatment for plantar fasciitis? Calf and sole stretches, cushioned shoes with arch support or insoles, ice, and reducing painful activity. A doctor or physiotherapist can help if it doesn’t improve. Is a heel spur the cause of my pain? Usually not. Heel spurs are common in people without pain and don’t cause plantar fasciitis. Can burning soles be a sign of diabetes? Yes. Burning, tingling or numb feet can be a sign of nerve damage from diabetes or low vitamin B12. See a doctor for a check. Should I walk barefoot at home? If you have heel pain, try not to walk barefoot on hard floors. Wear supportive footwear or cushioned slippers.

title: Sakit gigi (toothache): causes, how to ease the pain until you see a dentist, and when it’s an emergency
desc: Toothache usually means a tooth needs treatment, and painkillers only buy time. What causes it, the painkillers that work best, why you shouldn’t put aspirin on your gum, when antibiotics do and don’t help, and the swelling that needs emergency care.
headings: What causes toothache? · How to ease toothache until you see a dentist · Do I need antibiotics? · Abscess and emergency signs · Toothache and teething in children · Preventing toothache
keywords: Guides Sakit gigi (toothache) Toothache Dental abscess Sakit gigi denggi aedes nyamuk mosquito mengandung hamil pregnancy antenatal kecemasan emergency a&e hospital klinik doctor doktor gp
body: Common causes are tooth decay, an abscess, a cracked tooth or loose filling, gum disease, an infected wisdom tooth, sensitive teeth and grinding. Dental guidelines recommend an anti-inflammatory painkiller such as ibuprofen, alone or with paracetamol, as the first choice for toothache. But avoid ibuprofen if you might have dengue. Don’t put aspirin on your gum: it burns the gum and gives little relief. Clove oil is unproven for toothache and dangerous if swallowed by children. Antibiotics don’t cure toothache. An abscess needs the tooth treated or drained, and antibiotics are used only for spreading infection or fever. Go to an emergency department for facial swelling spreading to the eye or neck, difficulty swallowing, speaking or breathing, or a high fever. Tooth decay reaching the nerve. In Malaysia, a 2020 national survey found tooth decay in 85% of people aged 15 and over. A dental abscess: a pocket of pus from an infected tooth or gum, causing intense throbbing pain, a bad taste, swelling and sometimes fever A cracked tooth or loose filling Gum disease , which affected 38% of Malaysian adults in the 2020 survey A wisdom tooth that has only partly come through and become infected (pericoronitis) Sensitive teeth , with short sharp pain from hot, cold or sweet food Grinding or clenching , which can cause jaw pain and worn or broken teeth Sinusitis , which can cause pain that feels like toothache. See our resdung and sinus guide . Jaw pain together with chest pain can be a heart attack. Call 999 . See our guide to chest pain . Painkillers: the American Dental Association’s 2024 guideline recommends an anti-inflammatory painkiller (NSAID) such as ibuprofen, alone or with paracetamol, as the first choice for toothache in adults and teenagers. Studies after wisdom tooth removal found ibuprofen combined with paracetamol worked better than opioid painkillers, with fewer side effects. Ibuprofen (adults): usually 200 to 400mg up to 3 times a day with food, at least 4 hours apart. It isn’t suitable for everyone, including people with stomach ulcers, some types of asthma, heart, liver or kidney disease, or in pregnancy. Paracetamol (adults): 500mg to 1g, at least 4 hours apart, no more than 4g in 24 hours. Many cold remedies also contain paracetamol. Dengue: if you have a fever and could have dengue, use paracetamol only and avoid ibuprofen and aspirin. See our painkiller guide . Other things that help: rinse with warm salt water (half a teaspoon of salt in a glass of water), but not for young children eat soft food and chew on the other side avoid very hot, very cold or sweet food and drink use a soft toothbrush, and don’t smoke a pharmacist can suggest a pain-relief mouth gel Avoid: Putting aspirin on the gum. It dissolves into an acid that burns the gum and gives little or no pain relief. Relying on clove oil. There is no good evidence for toothache, and swallowing it can poison young children. Numbing gels with benzocaine for babies’ teething. The US FDA warns they can cause a dangerous blood condition. Painkillers buy time, but most toothache only stops when a dentist treats the cause. Usually not. Dental guidelines advise against antibiotics for an inflamed tooth nerve, or for an abscess that hasn’t spread, when dental treatment is available. Antibiotics don’t fix the tooth, and the pain returns. A dental abscess won’t go away on its own. The dentist treats it by draining it, with a root canal treatment or by removing the tooth. Antibiotics are added if the infection is spreading, or if you have a fever or feel unwell. See a dentist urgently for intense pain with swelling of the face or jaw, a bad taste, swollen glands in the neck, a fever or difficulty opening your mouth. Go to an emergency department or call 999 if you have: difficulty breathing, speaking or swallowing drooling, or a swollen or raised tongue swelling around the eye or down the neck, or problems with your vision a high fever with facial swelling These can be signs of a spreading infection under the tongue and in the neck (Ludwig’s angina), which can block the airway. Don’t drive yourself. A knocked-out adult tooth: hold it by the crown, not the root. If it is dirty, rinse it briefly in milk, salt water or saliva, then push it back into the socket and bite on a clean cloth. If you can’t, keep it in milk or in your mouth against your cheek, and see a dentist straight away. Never put a baby tooth back in. Teething babies: a chilled (not frozen) teething ring and gentle gum massage can help. Sugar-free paracetamol can be given from 2 months and ibuprofen from 3 months, at the dose on the pack. Tooth decay in young children is very common in Malaysia. In a national survey, 71% of 5-year-olds had decay, most of it untreated. Children aged 1 to 6 receive free dental treatment at government dental clinics. See our guide to government dental clinics . Brush your child’s teeth twice a day with fluoride toothpaste: a smear for under-3s and a pea-sized amount for ages 3 to 6, with supervision. Brush twice a day for 2 minutes with fluoride toothpaste. Spit out, don’t rinse. Clean between your teeth with floss or interdental brushes. Cut down on sugary food and drinks, especially between meals. Have a dental check-up regularly, even if nothing hurts. Avoid smoking, betel quid and alcohol, the main risks for oral cancer . More than 60% of oral cancers in Malaysia are found late. See a dentist or doctor for any mouth sore that hasn’t healed within 2 to 3 weeks. See our guide to mouth ulcers . Water fluoridation helps protect teeth. About three-quarters of Malaysians had fluoridated water in 2018, but coverage is low in some states, such as Sabah. What is the best ubat sakit gigi? Dental guidelines recommend ibuprofen, alone or with paracetamol, as the first choice for adults. Avoid ibuprofen if you might have dengue, and see a dentist to treat the cause. How can I stop toothache at night? Take an appropriate painkiller, rinse with warm salt water, and avoid very hot, cold or sweet food. Painkillers only help for a while, so book a dentist. Can I put aspirin on my tooth? No. Aspirin placed on the gum burns it and gives little or no relief. Swallow painkillers as directed instead. Will antibiotics cure my toothache? No. Antibiotics don’t fix the tooth. They are only used when an infection is spreading or you have a fever, along with dental treatment. When is toothache an emergency? When there is swelling spreading to the eye or neck, difficulty swallowing, speaking or breathing, or a high fever. Go to an emergency department. Does clove oil work for toothache? There is no good evidence that it works for toothache, and swallowing it can be dangerous for young children. What should I do with a knocked-out tooth? For an adult tooth, hold it by the crown, rinse it in milk if dirty, put it back and bite on a cloth, or keep it in milk, and see a dentist straight away. Never put a baby tooth back.

title: Ubat batuk: which cough medicines work, dry vs chesty cough, children and safety
desc: Pharmacy shelves are full of cough syrups, but the evidence that they work is weak. What is in dry and chesty cough medicines, which ones to avoid for children, Malaysia’s rules on codeine, combination product risks, how to check a product is registered, and when a cough needs a doctor.
headings: Dry cough or chesty cough? · Do cough medicines work? · Cough medicines for children · Codeine cough syrup: Malaysian rules · Safety tips: combinations, blood pressure and pregnancy · Check that a cough product is registered · Kahak: does green phlegm mean I need antibiotics?
keywords: Guides Ubat batuk (cough medicines) Cough medicine Cough Codeine kencing manis gula hba1c darah tinggi hypertension bp tekanan darah payudara kanser cancer mammogram pink october mengandung hamil pregnancy antenatal kecemasan emergency a&e hospital
body: A Cochrane review found no good evidence for or against over-the-counter cough medicines. They may ease a cough a little, but they won’t cure it. Honey is probably better than no treatment for children’s coughs, and works about as well as dextromethorphan. Never give honey to babies under 1 year. In Malaysia, liquid cough and cold medicines are labelled not for children under 2, and should only be used for ages 2 to 6 on a doctor’s or pharmacist’s advice. Codeine is not for children under 12. Codeine cough medicines can only be supplied by a doctor or pharmacist. Misusing cough syrup, including mixing it with ketum, is an offence. Check combination products so you don’t take paracetamol twice, and avoid decongestants such as pseudoephedrine if you have high blood pressure. Type of medicine Meant for Generic names Cough suppressant Dry, tickly cough (batuk kering) Dextromethorphan, codeine Expectorant Chesty cough with phlegm (batuk berkahak) Guaifenesin Mucolytic (loosens phlegm) Chesty cough with thick phlegm Bromhexine, ambroxol, carbocisteine, acetylcysteine Sedating antihistamine Often added to night-time mixtures Chlorpheniramine, diphenhydramine, promethazine Decongestant Blocked nose Pseudoephedrine, phenylephrine Don’t take a suppressant for a chesty cough, as coughing up phlegm helps clear your chest. Many products combine several of these ingredients, so read the label. A 2014 Cochrane review of 29 trials with nearly 5,000 people concluded there is no good evidence for or against over-the-counter cough medicines: Adults: results for suppressants were mixed. One of three trials of guaifenesin found a benefit, and so did one mucolytic trial. Antihistamines worked no better than a dummy treatment. Children: suppressants, antihistamines and antihistamine-decongestant mixtures worked no better than a dummy treatment. The NHS says cough syrups “may help you cough less” but won’t stop a cough, and that decongestants and codeine cough medicines won’t stop one either. A cough after a cold commonly lasts up to 3 weeks. Honey: a 2018 Cochrane review found honey is probably better than no treatment for children’s coughs, works about as well as dextromethorphan, and may work better than diphenhydramine. Try a teaspoon in warm water or on its own. Don’t give honey to babies under 1 year , because of the risk of botulism. Steam: breathing in steam hasn’t been shown to help, and steam bowls can scald children. Read the label: many cough mixtures combine several ingredients, including paracetamol or a decongestant. Under 2 years: Malaysia’s drug authority requires liquid cough and cold medicines containing antihistamines, cough suppressants or decongestants to be labelled “Not to be used in children below two years of age”. 2 to 6 years: use these only with caution, on the advice of a doctor or pharmacist. The UK advises no cough and cold medicines at all under 6. Codeine: Malaysia’s labelling rules say codeine mustn’t be used for coughs and colds in children under 12, isn’t recommended from 12 to 18 for those with breathing problems, and mustn’t be used by anyone under 18 after tonsil or adenoid removal for sleep apnoea. Sedating antihistamines such as promethazine can cause dangerous breathing problems in young children. Mucolytics: acetylcysteine and carbocisteine shouldn’t be given to children under 2. In France, some babies produced more mucus instead of less. Use the measuring device provided, and don’t give two products containing the same ingredient. For most children, rest, fluids and honey (from age 1) are enough. See our guides to colds (selsema) and fever in children . Codeine is a controlled medicine under Malaysia’s Poisons Act. Codeine cough products can only be supplied by a doctor or a pharmacist . The Ministry of Health has said cough medicines containing scheduled poisons can be sold only for medical purposes. Codeine and some other cough syrups have been misused in Malaysia, for example mixed with ketum and fizzy drinks. In 2018, the ministry reported seizing more than 100,000 bottles, and the penalty for illegal sale includes a fine of up to RM3,000, up to a year in prison, or both. Codeine can: cause marked drowsiness, so don’t drive or drink alcohol slow breathing dangerously, especially in children and in people who break it down unusually fast pass into breast milk, so Malaysian labelling says not to use it while breastfeeding be habit-forming The US FDA has limited codeine cough medicines to adults aged 18 and over. Malaysia has also cancelled 14 pholcodine products, after links to severe allergic reactions during general anaesthesia. If you have taken pholcodine in the past, tell your surgical team before an operation. Paracetamol twice: many cold and flu products already contain paracetamol. Don’t take extra paracetamol on top. See our guide to painkillers . Decongestants: pseudoephedrine is in 62 registered combination products in Malaysia. NPRA warns of rare but serious brain blood vessel problems. Avoid it with severe or uncontrolled high blood pressure or kidney disease. Stop and get help for a sudden severe headache, confusion, seizures or vision changes. Check with a pharmacist first if you have heart disease, diabetes, glaucoma, thyroid problems or an enlarged prostate. Antidepressants: dextromethorphan can interact with some antidepressants and cause serotonin syndrome. Ask a pharmacist. Drowsiness: sedating antihistamines and codeine can make you sleepy. Don’t drive or operate machinery. Pregnancy: check with a doctor or pharmacist before taking any cough medicine. Breastfeeding: guaifenesin is probably fine. Avoid codeine, and note that decongestant tablets may reduce milk supply. Registered medicines in Malaysia carry a MAL number (MAL followed by 8 digits and a letter) and a hologram security label. The last letter tells you the type: A: controlled medicine X: over-the-counter medicine T: traditional product, such as herbal cough remedies N: health supplement You can check a product by name or registration number on NPRA’s QUEST3+ product search . Registration of a traditional product doesn’t mean it has been proven to work. No. In a study of more than 3,400 adults with a cough, people with yellow or green phlegm were given antibiotics more often, but the antibiotics didn’t help them recover faster. Most coughs are caused by viruses, which antibiotics don’t treat. For bronchitis, antibiotics shortened the cough by only about half a day, with more side effects. See a doctor if you have: a cough lasting more than 3 weeks. See our guide to persistent cough . blood in your phlegm breathlessness, chest pain or wheezing. See our guide to asthma . a fever lasting more than 5 days weight loss, night sweats or a long-lasting cough, which can be signs of tuberculosis Babies: whooping cough in babies under 3 months may not cause a whoop. Call 999 if a baby turns blue or grey or struggles to breathe, and get urgent help for any baby under 6 months with a bad cough. What is the best ubat batuk? There is no clear winner. For a dry cough, dextromethorphan may help a little. For a chesty cough, guaifenesin may help. Honey is a good option for children over 1. Ask a pharmacist. Which cough medicine is for batuk berkahak? An expectorant such as guaifenesin, or a mucolytic such as bromhexine or carbocisteine. Avoid cough suppressants for a chesty cough. Can I give cough syrup to my baby? No. In Malaysia, liquid cough and cold medicines are labelled not for children under 2. Don’t give honey to babies under 1 year either. See a doctor if a baby has a cough. Is codeine cough syrup available without a prescription? Codeine is controlled and can only be supplied by a doctor or pharmacist. It isn’t for children under 12 and shouldn’t be used while breastfeeding. Does green phlegm mean I need antibiotics? No. Green or yellow phlegm is common with viral infections, and antibiotics don’t speed recovery in most cases. Does honey help a cough? Yes, probably. Studies in children found honey better than no treatment and about as good as dextromethorphan. Don’t give it to babies under 1. How do I check if a cough medicine is registered? Look for a MAL number and hologram on the pack, then search the product on NPRA’s QUEST3+ website.

title: Kencing berbuih (foamy urine) and kidney disease: early signs, tests and protecting your buah pinggang
desc: Foamy urine is usually harmless, but foam that keeps coming back can mean protein is leaking from the kidneys. Malaysia has one of the world’s fastest-rising rates of kidney failure, and early kidney disease has no symptoms. What the tests mean and how to protect your kidneys.
headings: Kencing berbuih: when is foamy urine a problem? · What is chronic kidney disease? · Kidney tests and what the results mean · Sakit buah pinggang: is it kidney pain? · Who should be checked? · How to protect your kidneys
keywords: Heart & diabetes Kencing berbuih and kidney disease Chronic kidney disease Proteinuria Foamy urine kencing manis gula hba1c darah tinggi hypertension bp tekanan darah mengandung hamil pregnancy antenatal saringan check-up checkup medical aesthetic estetik kecantikan beauty kulit skin botox filler laser facial
body: Occasional foam that clears with one flush is usually harmless. See a doctor if foamy urine keeps happening, gets worse, or comes with swelling, tiredness or poor appetite. Chronic kidney disease is usually silent until it is advanced. A Malaysian survey found only 4 in 100 people with it knew they had it. It is found with a urine test for protein (often an albumin-to-creatinine ratio) and a blood test for eGFR. Results must stay abnormal for more than 3 months to confirm it. Diabetes and high blood pressure cause more than 8 in 10 new cases of kidney failure in Malaysia. People with either should have their kidneys checked at least once a year. Protect your kidneys by controlling blood pressure and sugar, avoiding regular anti-inflammatory painkillers and unregistered herbal products, cutting salt, and not smoking. Usually harmless: a fast, forceful stream concentrated, dark urine when you haven’t drunk enough toilet cleaner left in the bowl Occasional foam that clears with one flush is usually normal. Possibly protein in the urine (proteinuria): damaged kidneys can let protein leak into the urine, which makes it froth. Diabetes, high blood pressure, lupus and chronic kidney disease can all cause this. See a doctor if foamy urine: happens regularly or is getting worse needs more than one flush to clear, or looks thick and white lasts more than a few days comes with swollen ankles, feet or hands, unusual tiredness, nausea or poor appetite The first step is a simple urine test. If you also see blood in your urine, see our guide to kencing berdarah . Your kidneys filter about 140 litres of blood a day, removing waste as urine. They also balance fluids and minerals and make hormones that control blood pressure, red blood cell production and bone health. Chronic kidney disease (CKD) means the kidneys have been damaged or working less well for more than 3 months. Malaysia’s Ministry of Health calls it “common but silent”. Most people have no symptoms until the disease is advanced. Later symptoms can include swollen ankles or feet, tiredness, itchy skin, nausea, poor appetite, changes in how often you pass urine, breathlessness, cramps and weight loss. Malaysia’s numbers: A national survey estimated that about 15 in 100 adults had CKD in 2018, up from 9 in 100 in 2011. The health minister said in 2026 that more than 5 million Malaysians have it. More than 55,000 people were on dialysis at the end of 2024, and about 9,500 to 10,000 people start dialysis every year. Diabetes caused 55% and high blood pressure 31% of new cases of kidney failure in 2024. Malaysia’s guideline on CKD recommends two simple tests: Urine test for protein: a dipstick test, or a more sensitive albumin-to-creatinine ratio (ACR) on an early-morning urine sample, especially if you have diabetes. Blood test for eGFR (estimated glomerular filtration rate), worked out from your creatinine level, age and sex. It shows how well your kidneys filter. Creatinine on its own isn’t enough. A positive urine test can be temporary, for example after hard exercise, during a urine infection, fever or a period, or in pregnancy. So abnormal results are repeated within 3 months to confirm them. Stage eGFR (ml/min/1.73m²) What it means G1 90 or more Normal filtering, but with signs of kidney damage such as protein in the urine G2 60 to 89 Mildly reduced G3a 45 to 59 Mildly to moderately reduced G3b 30 to 44 Moderately to severely reduced G4 15 to 29 Severely reduced G5 Below 15 Kidney failure Urine protein (ACR) is graded as A1 (below 3mg/mmol, normal to mildly raised), A2 (3 to 30mg/mmol, moderately raised) or A3 (above 30mg/mmol, severely raised). The higher the protein and the lower the eGFR, the greater the risk. See our guide to blood test results . A blood test for eGFR and a urine test for protein are the main checks for kidney disease. Kidney disease itself is usually painless. Most lower back pain comes from muscles, joints or the spine rather than the kidneys. See our guide to back pain and sciatica . Pain from the kidneys is usually felt in the side or back, just under the ribs. See a doctor urgently if this kind of pain comes with fever, shivering, vomiting or blood in the urine, as it may be a kidney infection. Sudden, severe, coming-and-going pain that spreads to the groin is often a kidney stone . At least once a year , according to Malaysia’s guideline, if you have: diabetes high blood pressure Checking may also be worthwhile if you: are over 65 are obese, or have heart disease or metabolic syndrome have a family history of kidney disease have gout , lupus, kidney stones or an enlarged prostate take painkillers or stomach acid medicines (PPIs) long term have had blood or protein found in your urine by chance Health screening schemes such as PeKa B40 and the SOCSO health screening programme include blood and urine tests. Check what your scheme covers. Control blood pressure. Malaysia’s guideline sets lower targets for people with diabetes or protein in the urine, often around 130/80. Your doctor will set yours. Control blood sugar. An HbA1c of about 7% is a common target for people with diabetes and kidney disease, adjusted for each person. Take kidney-protecting medicines if prescribed. ACE inhibitors or ARBs, and SGLT2 inhibitors, can slow kidney damage in many people with diabetes or protein in the urine. Doctors adjust doses of other medicines to your kidney function. Avoid regular anti-inflammatory painkillers such as ibuprofen, naproxen, diclofenac, mefenamic acid and celecoxib. Ask a pharmacist about safer options. See our guide to painkillers . Be careful with herbal products. Some herbs containing aristolochic acid have caused kidney disease, and products can be contaminated with heavy metals. “Natural” doesn’t mean safe for the kidneys. Cut salt to less than 2,400mg of sodium a day, about a teaspoon of salt. Avoid very high-protein diets if your kidneys are already affected. Stop smoking , stay active and keep to a healthy weight. What about water? Staying hydrated is sensible, but drinking extra water doesn’t prevent kidney disease, and too much can lower your blood sodium. If you have advanced kidney disease, your doctor may limit how much you drink. Is foamy urine a sign of kidney problems? Occasional foam is usually harmless. Foam that keeps coming back, needs more than one flush or comes with swelling can mean protein in the urine, and should be checked with a urine test. What is the English for kencing berbuih? Foamy or frothy urine. What is a normal eGFR? An eGFR of 90 or more is normal. A result below 60 for more than 3 months means chronic kidney disease, as does a higher eGFR with protein in the urine. Can kidney disease be cured? Chronic kidney disease usually can’t be reversed, but controlling blood pressure and sugar and the right medicines can slow it down and prevent kidney failure. Does drinking more water protect the kidneys? Staying hydrated is sensible, but extra water doesn’t prevent kidney disease, and too much can be harmful. People with advanced kidney disease may need to limit fluids. Do medicines damage the kidneys? Regular anti-inflammatory painkillers and some herbal products can. Many other medicines, including some for blood pressure and diabetes, protect the kidneys. Your doctor adjusts doses to your kidney function. How often should I check my kidneys if I have diabetes? At least once a year, with a urine protein test and an eGFR blood test.

title: Asma (asthma) in Malaysia: inhalers, what to do in an attack, and keeping it under control
desc: More than 1.4 million Malaysian adults have been diagnosed with asthma, and many more don’t know they have it. How asthma is diagnosed, the difference between reliever and preventer inhalers, how to use them properly, what to do in an attack, and when to get help.
headings: What is asthma? · How asthma is diagnosed · Reliever and preventer inhalers · How to use your inhaler properly · What to do in an asthma attack · Is your asthma under control? · Children, pregnancy and common myths
keywords: Guides Asma (asthma) and inhalers Asthma Inhaler Asma jerebu api ipu air pollutant index smoke mengandung hamil pregnancy antenatal vaksin suntikan jab immunisation kecemasan emergency a&e hospital
body: The 2023 National Health and Morbidity Survey found more than 1.4 million Malaysian adults have diagnosed asthma, and about 3 in 10 people with asthma don’t know they have it. Malaysia’s 2024 adult guideline says a reliever (SABA, such as salbutamol) shouldn’t be used on its own. Everyone with asthma should have treatment that includes an inhaled steroid. Using a reliever more than twice a week, or waking at night with asthma, is a sign that your asthma isn’t controlled. See your doctor. Inhaler technique matters. Shake the inhaler, breathe out fully, press as you start to breathe in, use a spacer, and rinse your mouth after a steroid inhaler. In an attack, sit up and use your reliever as your action plan says. Call 999 if you aren’t improving, are getting worse, or can’t speak in sentences. In asthma, the airways in the lungs are sensitive and inflamed. When they react to a trigger, they tighten and produce extra mucus, making it hard to breathe. Symptoms come and go, and are often worse at night or during or after exercise: wheezing (a whistling sound when breathing) coughing, especially at night chest tightness shortness of breath ( semput or sesak nafas ) Common triggers in Malaysia: colds and other viral infections, house dust mites, pets, haze, smoke, vaping, strong smells such as perfume and cleaning products, exhaust fumes, cold air (including air-conditioning) and exercise. In Malaysia: more than 1.4 million adults have diagnosed asthma, and almost half a million children aged 6 to 17. Among children with asthma, 1 in 2 had at least one attack in the past year. Your doctor will ask about your symptoms and listen to your chest. The preferred test is spirometry , where you blow hard into a machine that measures how much and how fast you can breathe out. If your breathing improves by a set amount after a reliever inhaler, that supports asthma. A peak flow meter can also help. Readings that vary a lot from day to day, or improve with treatment, point to asthma. Asthma can be missed, so see a doctor if you often cough at night, wheeze or get breathless with colds. Type What it does Generic names Reliever (SABA) Opens the airways within minutes. Doesn’t treat the inflammation. Salbutamol, terbutaline Preventer (inhaled steroid, ICS) Calms the inflammation over time, so attacks are less likely. Must be used every day, even when well. Budesonide, beclometasone, fluticasone, ciclesonide Combination (ICS plus long-acting reliever) A preventer and a long-acting airway opener in one inhaler. Some can also be used as a reliever. Budesonide-formoterol, beclometasone-formoterol, fluticasone-salmeterol Why a blue reliever alone isn’t enough: the Global Initiative for Asthma no longer recommends treating asthma with a short-acting reliever alone, because it raises the risk of severe attacks and death. Using 3 or more reliever canisters a year raises the risk of severe attacks. Malaysia’s 2024 adult guideline agrees that a reliever shouldn’t be used alone and that everyone with asthma should have treatment containing an inhaled steroid. Many doctors now prescribe a single budesonide-formoterol or beclometasone-formoterol inhaler used both as a daily preventer and as a reliever. Others prescribe a daily preventer with a separate reliever. Follow the plan your doctor gives you, and don’t change your inhalers without advice. A preventer inhaler only works if it is used every day, even when you feel well. Many people use their inhaler incorrectly. Malaysia’s guideline lists the most common mistakes: not breathing out fully first, pressing the canister before breathing in, breathing out into the device, not holding it upright, and not holding the breath for long enough. Metered-dose inhaler (spray): Shake the inhaler and remove the cap. Breathe out fully, away from the inhaler. Seal your lips around the mouthpiece, or the spacer. Press the canister once as you start to breathe in slowly and deeply. Hold your breath for up to 10 seconds, or as long as is comfortable. Wait about 30 seconds before a second puff. Use a spacer , especially with a steroid inhaler. It helps more medicine reach the lungs. If you don’t have one, a homemade spacer made from a plastic bottle can be used in an emergency, although it isn’t as effective. Dry powder inhalers need a fast, deep breath in, and shouldn’t be shaken or breathed into. Rinse your mouth with water and spit after using a steroid inhaler, to reduce the risk of a sore mouth, hoarse voice and thrush. Is it empty? Check the dose counter, or count the doses used. Shaking can be misleading, because propellant remains after the medicine runs out. Ask your doctor, nurse or pharmacist to check your technique at every review. Signs of an attack: your reliever isn’t helping or you need it more and more, you are wheezing, coughing or very breathless, or you can’t speak, eat or sleep normally. If you use a blue reliever inhaler (UK guidance): Sit up straight and try to stay calm. Take 1 puff of your reliever every 30 to 60 seconds, up to 10 puffs, using a spacer if you have one. Call 999 if you feel worse at any point, or don’t feel better after 10 puffs. If the ambulance hasn’t arrived after 10 minutes, repeat step 2. If you use a combined preventer-and-reliever inhaler (such as budesonide-formoterol), follow your action plan. UK guidance is 1 puff every 1 to 3 minutes, up to 6 puffs, then call 999 if you aren’t better. Call 999 straight away if the person can only speak in single words, is too breathless to talk, has blue or grey lips, or is drowsy or confused. Even if you recover at home, see a doctor the same day, as an attack means your treatment needs reviewing. Over the past 4 weeks, have you: had daytime symptoms more than twice a week? woken at night because of your asthma? needed your reliever more than twice a week? had to limit your activities because of your asthma? If you answered yes to any of these, your asthma may not be well controlled. See your doctor. Ask for a written asthma action plan that tells you what to take each day, how to spot when you are getting worse, and what to do in an attack. Malaysia’s guideline recommends a review every 3 to 6 months. Haze: on days when the Air Pollutant Index is unhealthy, stay indoors where possible, keep taking your medicines and see a doctor promptly if your asthma gets worse. See our haze guide . Smoking and vaping make asthma worse and increase the risk of attacks. Flu and pneumococcal vaccines may be recommended. See our guides to the flu vaccine and pneumococcal vaccine . Children under 6 should use a spacer with a face mask, and older children a spacer with a mouthpiece. The 2024 Malaysian children’s consensus discourages nebulisers at home. Give a copy of the action plan to your child’s school or nursery. Growth: low to moderate doses of inhaled steroids are considered safe for children. Children on high doses need their growth monitored. Pregnancy: keep taking your preventer. Uncontrolled asthma is a greater risk to you and your baby than the inhaler. “Inhalers are addictive.” They aren’t. Using them correctly keeps asthma under control. “Steroid inhalers are dangerous.” Used as recommended, inhaled steroids are unlikely to cause lasting side effects, because only a small dose reaches the rest of the body. “I only need my inhaler when I’m ill.” A preventer works only if it is used every day, even when you feel well. What is asma in English? Asthma. Many Malaysians also call it lelah, although lelah can also mean tiredness. What is the difference between a reliever and a preventer inhaler? A reliever (such as salbutamol) opens the airways quickly during symptoms. A preventer (an inhaled steroid) calms the inflammation over time and must be used every day. Can I use only a blue inhaler for asthma? Current Malaysian and international guidelines say a short-acting reliever shouldn’t be used on its own. Treatment should include an inhaled steroid. Ask your doctor. What should I do in an asthma attack? Sit up and take your reliever as your action plan says. With a blue reliever, UK guidance is 1 puff every 30 to 60 seconds up to 10 puffs. Call 999 if you are not improving or are getting worse. Are steroid inhalers safe? Yes, when used as recommended. Only a small dose reaches the rest of the body. Rinse your mouth afterwards to prevent a sore mouth or thrush. Can asthma go away? Symptoms can improve, and some children grow out of them. Asthma can return, so keep your action plan and get symptoms checked if they come back. How do I know if my inhaler is empty? Check the dose counter, or count the puffs used. Shaking it can be misleading.

title: Platelet count (bacaan platelet): normal range, low platelets and what it means in dengue
desc: Worried about a low platelet count? What the numbers mean, the many causes besides dengue, why Malaysian dengue guidelines watch haematocrit more closely than platelets, which dengue test to do when, and the remedies that don’t change the outcome.
headings: What is a normal platelet count? · Causes of a low platelet count (platelet rendah) · Platelets in dengue · Dengue tests: NS1, IgM and IgG · Papaya leaf, crab soup and other remedies · When to go to hospital
keywords: Prevention Platelet count and dengue Platelet count Thrombocytopenia Dengue denggi aedes nyamuk mosquito mengandung hamil pregnancy antenatal vaksin suntikan jab immunisation kecemasan emergency a&e hospital klinik doctor doktor gp aesthetic estetik kecantikan beauty kulit skin botox filler laser facial
body: A normal platelet count is roughly 150,000 to 400,000 per microlitre (shown as 150 to 400 ×10⁹/L), although ranges vary between labs. Serious spontaneous bleeding is unusual until platelets fall below about 20,000. Above 50,000, the bleeding risk is minimal. In dengue, platelets usually fall around day 3 to 5 of fever, often as the fever settles. Malaysia’s guideline says the platelet count doesn’t match how severe the illness is. A rising haematocrit with falling platelets is the warning sign. An NS1 test works best in the first 5 days of fever. IgM antibodies usually show up from day 5, so an early negative IgM doesn’t rule dengue out. Papaya leaf, crab soup, isotonic drinks and similar remedies have no robust evidence of changing the course of dengue. Fluids and monitoring are what count. Platelets are tiny cells made in the bone marrow. They stick to damaged blood vessels and clump together to form clots. Each platelet lives about 7 to 10 days. A normal count is roughly 150,000 to 400,000 per microlitre (µL) of blood. Lab reports often write this as 150 to 400 ×10⁹/L , so a result of “90” means 90,000. Reference ranges differ slightly between labs, so compare your result with the range printed on your report. Platelet count (per µL) What it generally means Above about 450,000 High. Usually a reaction to infection, inflammation, bleeding or low iron About 150,000 to 400,000 Normal 50,000 to 150,000 Low, with minimal bleeding risk 20,000 to 50,000 Minor bleeding is possible after an injury Below 20,000 Spontaneous bleeding is possible Below 5,000 Risk of severe, possibly life-threatening bleeding Platelet results are one part of a full blood count , and your doctor will read them alongside your other results and how you are. A low platelet count is called thrombocytopenia . Dengue is a common cause in Malaysia, but there are many others: Other viral infections , including hepatitis C, HIV, glandular fever (EBV) and flu Medicines , such as heparin, quinine, co-trimoxazole, rifampicin and vancomycin. A few vaccines can occasionally cause a temporary drop. Immune thrombocytopenia (ITP) , where the immune system destroys platelets Pregnancy: a mild drop late in pregnancy (gestational thrombocytopenia) affects about 4 to 12 in 100 pregnancies. It usually stays above 70,000, is harmless to the baby, and resolves within about 6 weeks of birth. Liver disease , where an enlarged spleen holds on to platelets, and heavy alcohol use Low vitamin B12 or folate Bone marrow conditions , including leukaemia, lymphoma and aplastic anaemia, and chemotherapy A false low result: in about 1 in 1,000 samples, platelets clump together in the collection tube and the machine undercounts them. This is called pseudothrombocytopenia. A blood film or a repeat test in a different tube confirms it, and it needs no treatment. A single low result may need repeating, especially if you feel well. Malaysia’s clinical practice guideline on dengue in adults describes a typical pattern: Early fever: the white cell count and platelets are usually normal. The white cell count falls first, then platelets start to fall . The critical phase often begins after day 3 of fever, or as the fever comes down, and lasts 24 to 48 hours. This is when the blood vessels can leak fluid, and when platelets are usually lowest. In recovery, platelets rise again . Why the platelet number isn’t everything: the guideline states that there is no correlation between disease severity and platelet count, and that a low count doesn’t predict bleeding. What doctors watch most closely is the haematocrit (HCT), which rises when fluid leaks out of the blood vessels. A rising haematocrit together with a rapid fall in platelets is a warning sign. Monitoring: adults with dengue are usually reviewed daily from day 3 of illness until they have been free of fever for 24 to 48 hours without fever medicine. Children have a daily full blood count until the critical phase is over. Children: the Malaysian children’s guideline treats a platelet count falling to 100,000 or below, with a 20% rise in haematocrit, as a warning sign. Platelet transfusion: the guidelines say there is no role for routine preventive platelet transfusion in dengue. It is reserved for situations such as surgery or invasive procedures. See our guide to the first three days of dengue for symptoms and early care. Test Best time Good to know NS1 antigen Days 1 to 5 of fever Picks up 75 to 97% of first infections, but only 60 to 70% of repeat infections. Less reliable from day 4 to 5. IgM antibody From day 5 Positive in about 80% after day 5 and 93 to 99% from days 6 to 10. A negative result before day 5 to 7 doesn’t rule dengue out. IgG antibody If IgM is still negative after day 7 Can suggest a past or repeat infection Combined rapid test As soon as dengue is suspected NS1 with IgM and IgG together picks up about 93% of cases. Done with a full blood count. A positive test confirms dengue, but a negative early test doesn’t always rule it out. If you still have symptoms, follow your doctor’s advice on repeat tests and daily blood counts. Malaysia’s adult dengue guideline lists papaya leaf, cactus, crab or padi frog soup, bitter gourd, porcupine bezoar, tawa-tawa, pegaga and commercial isotonic drinks as remedies without robust evidence . It notes that changing the platelet count alone doesn’t alter the course of dengue. In 2016, the Ministry of Health said local studies found platelets rose after 3 days of papaya leaf juice, and that the juice wasn’t toxic. But ministry hospitals don’t provide it, and it doesn’t treat the leaking blood vessels that make dengue dangerous. What helps: drinking enough. The Malaysian guideline advises more than 2 litres a day of fluids such as milk, juice, oral rehydration salts and barley water, not plain water alone. Avoid: aspirin, mefenamic acid, ibuprofen and other anti-inflammatory painkillers, and steroids injections, including injections into the muscle massage and cupping antibiotics, which don’t work against dengue Use paracetamol for fever, with no more than 4g a day for adults. See our guide to painkillers and fever in adults . Go to a hospital emergency department straight away, or call 999 , if someone with dengue or a low platelet count has: red spots or patches on the skin, nosebleeds or bleeding gums vomiting blood, or black stools unusually heavy periods or vaginal bleeding vomiting or diarrhoea more than 3 times in 24 hours tummy pain drowsiness, restlessness or irritability pale, cold or clammy skin difficulty breathing Watch most closely as the fever comes down , because that is when dengue can become dangerous. If you have a low platelet count without a clear cause, such as dengue, see a doctor to look for the reason. What is a normal platelet count? Roughly 150,000 to 400,000 per microlitre, written as 150 to 400 ×10⁹/L on many reports. Lab ranges vary slightly. What platelet count is dangerous? Serious spontaneous bleeding becomes possible below about 20,000, and the risk is highest below 5,000. Above 50,000, the bleeding risk is minimal. What platelet count needs hospital admission in dengue? There isn’t one number. Malaysian guidelines look at warning signs and a rising haematocrit with falling platelets, rather than the platelet count alone. When do platelets drop in dengue? Usually around day 3 to 5 of fever, often as the fever starts to come down. They rise again during recovery. Does papaya leaf juice help dengue? Some local studies found platelets rose, but Malaysia’s guideline says there is no robust evidence that it changes the course of dengue. Fluids and medical monitoring matter more. When should I do an NS1 test? In the first 5 days of fever. From day 5, an IgM antibody test is more useful. Can I have a low platelet count without dengue? Yes. Other infections, medicines, immune conditions, pregnancy, liver disease and bone marrow problems can all lower platelets. See a doctor to find the cause.

title: Cuti bersalin: maternity and paternity leave in Malaysia, who qualifies and how it’s paid
desc: How much maternity and paternity leave you are entitled to in Malaysia, who qualifies for pay, when leave can start, what happens after a stillbirth, how the rules differ for civil servants and in Sabah and Sarawak, and what Budget 2027 proposes.
headings: Maternity leave for private-sector employees · Telling your employer · Paternity leave (cuti paterniti) · Stillbirth, miscarriage and premature birth · Protection from dismissal · Sabah, Sarawak and civil servants · Health care during and after pregnancy
keywords: Women's health Maternity and paternity leave Maternity leave Paternity leave Employment Act 1955 kencing manis gula hba1c darah tinggi hypertension bp tekanan darah payudara kanser cancer mammogram pink october kesihatan mental depression anxiety stress kemurungan mengandung hamil pregnancy antenatal vaksin suntikan jab immunisation klinik doctor doktor gp saringan check-up checkup medical
body: Private-sector employees get at least 98 consecutive days of maternity leave for each birth, whatever their salary, since 1 January 2023. To be paid, you need at least 90 days’ service in the 9 months before the birth, and you must have worked for that employer in the 4 months before it. Without this, you still get the leave, unpaid. Married fathers get 7 consecutive days of paid paternity leave after 12 months with the same employer, for up to 5 births. Leave can start up to 30 days before the birth. A stillbirth or birth from 22 weeks of pregnancy counts as a confinement, with full maternity and paternity leave. Sabah and Sarawak moved to 98 days of maternity and 7 days of paternity leave from 1 May 2025. Budget 2027 announced up to 98 days per birth for civil servants. These rules come from section 37 of the Employment Act 1955 , which covers Peninsular Malaysia and Labuan. Since 1 January 2023, they apply to all female employees, whatever their salary , including foreign workers. Rule What it means Length At least 98 consecutive days for each birth. Rest days and public holidays count within the 98 days. Earliest start 30 days before the birth. Days off taken earlier than that don’t count as maternity leave. Latest start The day after the birth Pay Your ordinary rate of pay, if you meet the conditions below Going back early Possible with a doctor’s certificate that you are fit, and your employer’s agreement Conditions for pay (maternity allowance): at least 90 days of service in the 9 months before the birth, and you must have worked for that employer at some time in the 4 months before the birth. If you don’t meet these conditions, you still get the 98 days of leave, but unpaid. The allowance also isn’t payable if you already have 5 or more surviving children at the time of the birth, although you still get the leave. Many employers offer more than the legal minimum, so check your contract. If a doctor certifies that you can’t work in late pregnancy, your employer can require you to start leave in the 14 days before the birth. Within the 60 days before your due date, tell your employer when your leave will start. You can do this verbally or in writing, but writing is easier to prove. If you don’t give notice, your allowance can be held back until you do. Late notice for a good reason doesn’t cancel it. If you leave a job knowing you will give birth within 4 months, you must tell that employer first, or you lose the allowance from them. Under section 60FA of the Employment Act, fathers get 7 consecutive days of paid paternity leave for each birth, at their ordinary rate of pay. To qualify, you must: be married to the mother have worked for the same employer for at least 12 months immediately before the leave give notice at least 30 days before the due date, or as soon as possible after the birth Paternity leave is limited to 5 births in total. The Employment Act defines a confinement as a birth after at least 22 weeks of pregnancy, whether the baby is born alive or dead. So: a stillbirth from 22 weeks gives the mother full maternity leave and allowance, and the father paternity leave a premature birth from 22 weeks starts maternity leave, which can begin no later than the day after the birth a miscarriage before 22 weeks isn’t covered by maternity leave. Time off is usually taken as sick leave with a medical certificate (MC) . Losing a baby at any stage is very hard. Ask your doctor or clinic about support, and talk to your employer about the time you need. See our guide to anxiety and mental health support . While you are pregnant or ill because of your pregnancy, your employer can only dismiss you for wilful breach of contract, misconduct or closure of the business. The employer must prove the dismissal wasn’t because of your pregnancy. Dismissing an employee during maternity leave is an offence, unless the business closes. If a doctor certifies that you are too ill from your pregnancy or the birth to return after your leave, you can’t be dismissed until 90 days after the leave ends. Flexible working: you can apply in writing to change your hours, days or place of work. Your employer must reply in writing within 60 days and give reasons if they refuse. Malaysian law doesn’t currently give a right to breastfeeding breaks at work, but many employers allow them. Ask your employer. If your employer refuses your rights, you can contact the Labour Department (Jabatan Tenaga Kerja, JTK) . The ministry recorded 41 complaints about maternity leave and allowance in 2025. Sabah and Sarawak: from 1 May 2025, the state Labour Ordinances were amended to give 98 days of maternity leave (up from 60) and 7 days of paternity leave, for all employees regardless of salary. Check the detailed conditions with your employer or the state labour department. Civil servants (JPA): The current rule is 60 to 90 days of maternity leave per birth, chosen by the officer, with a lifetime total of 360 days. Budget 2027 , tabled on 9 October 2026, announced an increase to a maximum of 98 days per birth and 490 days in total. We haven’t found a JPA circular putting it into effect yet, so check with your HR department. Officers can also take unpaid childcare leave (cuti menjaga anak). Since 1 December 2024, fathers in the civil service can take 1 to 20 days of leave when their wife gives birth, from a shared pool of 20 days a year, up to 5 times in their career. Proposed, not yet law: in May 2026 the government announced a post-maternity leave allowance of 80% of salary for up to 30 extra days, funded through the Employment Insurance System. As of October 2026, it was still being studied. Maternity leave also covers your postnatal check-up, usually about a month after the birth. Register for antenatal care at a Klinik Kesihatan or private clinic before 12 weeks if you can. You will get a pink antenatal record book (Buku Rekod Ibu). Antenatal screening includes HIV, hepatitis B, syphilis, diabetes and blood pressure. Folic acid, iron and multivitamins are given free at government clinics, and the whooping cough (Tdap) vaccine has been offered since May 2025. After the birth, nurses carry out home visits, and there is a postnatal check-up about a month later. If you are unwell during pregnancy before your maternity leave starts, a doctor can give you an MC for sick leave. See our guides to early pregnancy and your baby’s vaccination schedule . How many days is maternity leave in Malaysia? At least 98 consecutive days for each birth under the Employment Act, for private-sector employees in Peninsular Malaysia and Labuan. Sabah and Sarawak also moved to 98 days from 1 May 2025. Is maternity leave paid in Malaysia? Yes, at your ordinary rate of pay, if you have at least 90 days’ service in the 9 months before the birth and worked for that employer in the 4 months before it. How many days is paternity leave in Malaysia? 7 consecutive days of paid leave for married fathers who have worked for the same employer for 12 months, for up to 5 births. When can maternity leave start? No earlier than 30 days before the birth and no later than the day after it. Can I be dismissed while pregnant? Only for wilful breach of contract, misconduct or closure of the business, and your employer must prove it isn’t because of your pregnancy. Do I get maternity leave after a stillbirth? Yes, if the stillbirth happens at 22 weeks of pregnancy or later. The father also gets paternity leave. How long is maternity leave for civil servants? Currently 60 to 90 days per birth. Budget 2027 announced up to 98 days per birth, but check with your HR department for when it takes effect.

title: Muntah (vomiting) and loya (nausea): causes, muntah darah, medicines and when to see a doctor
desc: Most vomiting stops within a day or two. What usually causes it, why vomiting blood or green vomit needs urgent care, how to keep fluids down, which anti-sickness medicines are used and which aren’t for children, and the warning signs.
headings: What causes vomiting? · Muntah darah: vomiting blood · Home care for vomiting · Ubat muntah: anti-sickness medicines · Vomiting in babies and children · Vomiting in pregnancy · When to get urgent help
keywords: Guides Muntah (vomiting) and nausea Vomiting Nausea Haematemesis denggi aedes nyamuk mosquito kencing manis gula hba1c payudara kanser cancer mammogram pink october mengandung hamil pregnancy antenatal kecemasan emergency a&e hospital aesthetic estetik kecantikan beauty kulit skin botox filler laser facial
body: Vomiting usually stops within 1 to 2 days. Take small, frequent sips of oral rehydration salts, keep breastfeeding, and eat when you feel able to. Vomiting blood (muntah darah) always needs medical help. Call 999 or go to an emergency department if you also feel faint, dizzy, confused or cold and clammy, or have black stools. Green or yellow-green vomit can mean a blocked bowel and needs hospital care, even if the person doesn’t seem dehydrated. Anti-sickness medicines aren’t routinely recommended for children with a stomach bug. Domperidone shouldn’t be used under 12 years, and metoclopramide is not for babies under 1 year. Get urgent help for vomiting with a stiff neck, severe headache or tummy pain, after a head injury, or with dengue warning signs. Common causes: a stomach bug (gastroenteritis) or food poisoning , often with diarrhoea medicines, including strong painkillers and chemotherapy alcohol motion sickness and vertigo migraine early pregnancy Serious causes include appendicitis , a blocked bowel, pancreatitis, meningitis, a head injury or bleeding in the brain, diabetic ketoacidosis, and liver or kidney failure. Sudden nausea with heavy chest pain, pain spreading to the arm, jaw or back, or breathlessness can be a heart attack. Call 999 . In dengue: vomiting more than 3 times in 24 hours is a warning sign. See our guide to platelets and dengue . Vomiting blood always needs medical help. The vomit may be bright red, brown or black, or look like coffee grounds . Coffee-ground vomit is blood that has been partly digested by stomach acid, which usually means the bleeding has slowed or stopped. Bright red blood suggests faster bleeding that may still be going on. Call 999 or go to an emergency department if you vomit blood and also: feel faint, dizzy or confused are breathing fast have cold, clammy or pale skin have tummy pain have black, tarry stools Don’t drive yourself. If the bleeding has stopped and you have no other symptoms, get an urgent appointment with a doctor the same day. Common causes: inflammation of the stomach lining (gastritis), stomach ulcers and reflux damage. See our guides to gastric pain and GERD . aspirin, ibuprofen and other anti-inflammatory painkillers, and blood thinners a tear in the food pipe after forceful retching (a Mallory-Weiss tear) swollen veins in the food pipe (varices) in people with liver disease, which can bleed heavily less often, cancer or a bleeding disorder Not always from the stomach: blood swallowed during a nosebleed can be vomited, and a breastfed baby can swallow blood from a cracked nipple. In hospital, doctors may use a camera test (endoscopy) to find and treat the bleeding, and give acid-reducing medicines. Vomiting blood always needs a doctor, the same day or as an emergency. Take small, frequent sips. Oral rehydration salts (ORS) replace both water and salts. For a child, start with about 1 teaspoon (5ml) every 5 minutes, and increase slowly if they keep it down. See our diarrhoea guide for how to mix ORS. Avoid fizzy drinks, sports drinks and undiluted juice, especially for children. Babies: keep breastfeeding, with smaller and more frequent feeds. Never make formula weaker than the instructions say. Food: go back to your normal diet once you are keeping fluids down. Plain food is easier at first, and it’s best to avoid fatty or spicy food. Stay off work or school for 48 hours after the last episode of vomiting if it was caused by a stomach bug, to avoid spreading it. Wash your hands with soap and water. Most vomiting from a stomach bug settles without medicine. If needed, a doctor may prescribe an anti-sickness medicine. Children with gastroenteritis: the 2026 Malaysian children’s guideline doesn’t recommend routine anti-sickness medicines. It says domperidone, metoclopramide and dimenhydrinate don’t work well enough and cause side effects. A single dose of ondansetron may be considered by a doctor for persistent vomiting in children from 6 months. Domperidone: Malaysia’s drug regulator, NPRA, says it shouldn’t be used in children under 12 years or under 35kg. It can cause dangerous heart rhythm problems, so it isn’t suitable for people with heart disease or taking certain other medicines. In Europe, it is limited to a maximum of 30mg a day, usually for no more than a week. Metoclopramide: must not be given to babies under 1 year. NPRA has warned about a reaction in which the eyes roll upward uncontrollably (oculogyric crisis), with 241 reports in Malaysia. In children over 1, it is only a second-line choice for limited uses.
