Adults: doctors may use prochlorperazine, promethazine or metoclopramide for mild to moderate vomiting, and ondansetron for severe vomiting or vomiting caused by chemotherapy. Motion sickness: tablets such as dimenhydrinate or hyoscine, taken before the journey, can help. Ginger may help some people. Ask a pharmacist or doctor before taking any anti-sickness medicine, especially for a child, in pregnancy, or if you have a heart condition. A stomach bug is the most common cause. Get medical help urgently if a child: has green or yellow-green vomit , or blood in the vomit is a baby aged about 3 to 6 weeks who has forceful (projectile) vomiting after every feed, stays hungry and isn’t gaining weight. This can be pyloric stenosis, a narrowing at the stomach exit. has a bulging soft spot on the head, a stiff neck, a rash or a high fever is unusually sleepy, floppy or crying in a way that can’t be settled has a swollen tummy, or vomiting without diarrhoea that keeps going has vomited more than 6 to 8 times, or for more than 24 to 48 hours hasn’t passed urine or has refused to drink for more than 8 hours See our guide to fever in children . Morning sickness is common and usually settles by 16 to 20 weeks. Rest, small frequent meals, plain starchy snacks and sips of fluid can help. Ask a pharmacist before taking supplements, including ginger. A doctor can prescribe anti-sickness medicines that are considered safe in pregnancy. Hyperemesis gravidarum is severe vomiting in pregnancy, affecting 1 to 3 in 100 women. It often needs fluids through a drip in hospital. See a doctor if you are pregnant and: can’t keep food or fluids down for 24 hours have dark urine, or haven’t passed urine for 8 hours feel faint, or have tummy pain or a fever are losing weight, or vomit blood Call 999 or go to an emergency department for vomiting with: blood, or vomit that looks like coffee grounds green vomit, in adults or children a stiff neck, a sudden severe headache or a rash that doesn’t fade sudden or severe tummy pain confusion or unusual drowsiness chest pain or breathlessness Get urgent advice the same day if: you have vomited after a head injury you can’t keep fluids down, or vomiting has lasted more than 2 days you have signs of dehydration, such as dark urine, passing little urine and dizziness you have diabetes and are vomiting, especially if your ketones are high. Ask your doctor about a sick day plan. you have a fever in dengue season and are vomiting more than 3 times a day Repeated bouts: attacks of vomiting that come back again and again with normal health in between can be cyclic vomiting syndrome, which is often linked to migraine. Regular cannabis use can also cause repeated vomiting that only stops when the person stops using it. What is muntah in English? Muntah means vomiting, or being sick. Loya means nausea, the feeling that you might be sick. Is vomiting blood an emergency? It always needs medical help. Call 999 or go to an emergency department if you also feel faint, dizzy or confused, or have black stools. Otherwise, see a doctor the same day. What does coffee-ground vomit mean? It is blood that has been partly digested by stomach acid, often from a stomach ulcer or gastritis. It needs medical help the same day. What should I drink after vomiting? Small, frequent sips of oral rehydration salts. For children, start with a teaspoon every 5 minutes. Avoid fizzy drinks and sports drinks. Can I give my child medicine for vomiting? Anti-sickness medicines aren’t routinely recommended for children with a stomach bug. Domperidone shouldn’t be used under 12 years. Ask a doctor if vomiting persists. What does green vomit mean? Green or yellow-green vomit can mean a blocked bowel, especially in babies and children. It needs urgent hospital assessment. How long does vomiting last? Vomiting from a stomach bug usually stops within 1 to 2 days. Get advice if it lasts longer, or if you can’t keep fluids down.

title: Kencing berdarah (blood in urine): causes, tests and when it could be serious
desc: Pink, red or brown urine is alarming, but the cause is often an infection or a stone. Even so, blood in the urine should always be checked, because it can be the first sign of bladder or kidney cancer. Causes, foods that mimic it, the tests involved, and when to get help urgently.
headings: What does blood in urine look like? · Causes of kencing berdarah · Could it be cancer? · What tests to expect · Blood in urine in children and pregnancy · When to get help
keywords: Guides Kencing berdarah (blood in urine) Haematuria Blood in urine Bladder cancer darah tinggi hypertension bp tekanan darah mengandung hamil pregnancy antenatal kecemasan emergency a&e hospital klinik doctor doktor gp aesthetic estetik kecantikan beauty kulit skin botox filler laser facial
body: Blood in the urine can look pink, red or dark brown like weak tea. Beetroot, dragon fruit, food dyes and some medicines can colour urine red without any blood. A urine infection is the most common cause. Others include kidney stones, an enlarged prostate, kidney inflammation, injury, hard exercise and blood thinners. Always get visible blood in the urine checked, even if it stops. About 1 in 5 adults with visible blood in the urine is found to have bladder cancer. In a Malaysian hospital study, the most common causes found were an enlarged prostate, stones and urine infections, and no cause was found in about 1 in 5 people. Get help urgently for lots of blood or clots, being unable to pass urine, or blood with fever, back or side pain, or vomiting. Visible blood (gross haematuria): urine that looks pink, red, or dark brown like weak black tea. Sometimes there are clots. Non-visible blood (microscopic haematuria): urine looks normal, but blood is found on a dipstick or under a microscope. A positive dipstick is usually confirmed with a laboratory test. Red urine that isn’t blood: Foods: beetroot, dragon fruit, blackberries, rhubarb and food dyes Medicines: rifampicin, used to treat tuberculosis , and nitrofurantoin, used for urine infections Blood from somewhere else: a period, or bleeding from the vagina or back passage that mixes with urine If you have eaten dragon fruit or beetroot, the colour should clear within about 48 hours. If it doesn’t, or you haven’t eaten any of these foods, see a doctor. Urinary tract infection (UTI) : the most common cause, usually with burning, needing to pass urine often, or tummy pain Kidney or bladder stones (batu karang): often with severe pain in the side that spreads to the groin Enlarged prostate : common in older men Kidney inflammation (glomerulonephritis) , including IgA nephropathy. This often causes visible blood during a sore throat or stomach upset, and mainly affects young adults. See our guide to kidney disease . Injury to the kidneys or bladder, or vigorous exercise Blood-thinning medicines such as warfarin, apixaban, rivaroxaban, aspirin and clopidogrel, and blood disorders Infections such as TB , and schistosomiasis, caught from fresh water in some parts of Africa, Asia and the Middle East Cancer of the bladder, kidney or prostate A urine test is the first step, but visible blood often needs a scan and a bladder check as well. Most blood in the urine isn’t cancer, but it is an important early warning sign of bladder and kidney cancer. UK urologists report that about 1 in 5 adults with visible blood in the urine, and about 1 in 12 with non-visible blood, are found to have bladder cancer. In a study of 390 patients at a Malaysian university hospital, the causes found were an enlarged prostate (23%), stones (12%) and urine infections (11%). No cause was found in 22%. New bladder cancer was found in about 5 in 100 people with visible blood. The authors recommend fully investigating visible blood in the urine, especially over the age of 50. Higher risk: Smoking: smokers have up to 4 times the risk of bladder cancer, and smoking causes about half of bladder cancers in the UK. It also increases the risk of kidney cancer. age over 60, and being male long-term exposure to certain industrial chemicals past schistosomiasis UK guidance advises urgent investigation for anyone aged 45 or over with visible blood in the urine and no infection, or blood that continues or comes back after an infection is treated. In Malaysia, bladder and kidney cancer were each diagnosed in about 2,000 men between 2017 and 2021. At the clinic: questions about your symptoms, smoking, work and medicines a physical examination and blood pressure check a urine test for infection, and urine microscopy blood tests for kidney function, blood count and clotting, and a PSA test for men where appropriate If an infection is found and treated, the urine is often tested again 6 to 12 weeks later to make sure the blood has gone. Specialist tests (urologist): Ultrasound of the kidneys and bladder CT urogram: a detailed scan with a contrast injection. Mention any allergies or kidney problems. Cystoscopy: a thin camera passed into the bladder. A flexible cystoscopy takes about 10 to 15 minutes with numbing gel, and you can usually go home straight afterwards. A little blood and stinging for a few days afterwards is normal. Urine cytology: looking for abnormal cells in the urine On blood thinners? You still need to be checked. These medicines can make an underlying problem bleed, but they rarely cause bleeding on their own. Don’t stop them without speaking to your doctor. Children: cancer is rare. Common causes are urine infections, kidney inflammation, viral illness, injury and stones. One important cause is post-infectious glomerulonephritis , most often at ages 5 to 12, which appears 1 to 2 weeks after a strep throat or a few weeks after a skin infection. Urine looks tea- or cola-coloured, and there may be puffy eyelids in the morning. See a doctor promptly, and urgently if your child is passing less urine or is swelling up. In newborn babies, orange or pink “brick dust” in the nappy is usually urate crystals rather than blood, but ask your doctor if you are unsure. Pregnancy: a urine infection is a common cause of blood in the urine in pregnancy, and needs treatment. Any vaginal bleeding in pregnancy should also be checked. Call 999 for heavy bleeding, severe pain or feeling faint. Go to an emergency department or call 999 if: there is a lot of blood, or large clots you can’t pass urine you have blood in your urine with fever, shivering, pain in your back or side, or vomiting you have severe tummy pain, or feel faint See a doctor within a few days for any blood you can see in your urine, even if it has stopped, or if blood has been found on a urine test. Don’t ignore it just because it is painless. What is kencing berdarah in English? Blood in the urine, or haematuria. It can be visible, or found only on a urine test. Is blood in urine always serious? Not always. It is often caused by an infection or a stone. But it can be an early sign of bladder or kidney cancer, so always get it checked. Can dragon fruit turn urine red? Yes. Dragon fruit, beetroot and some food dyes can make urine pink or red for up to about 48 hours. If the colour lasts longer, see a doctor. Should I worry if the blood stopped by itself? You should still see a doctor. Bleeding from a bladder or kidney tumour can come and go. Can a UTI cause blood in urine? Yes, a urine infection is the most common cause. Your urine should be retested after treatment to make sure the blood has gone. What test will the urologist do? Usually an ultrasound or CT scan of the kidneys, and a cystoscopy, which is a camera check of the bladder. I take blood thinners. Do I still need checking? Yes. Blood thinners can make an underlying problem bleed, so you still need investigating. Don’t stop them without advice.

title: Klinik Kesihatan in Malaysia: waktu operasi, RM1 fees, appointments and services
desc: Malaysia has more than 1,100 government health clinics. When they open, what the RM1 fee covers, who is treated free, how to book through MySejahtera, what services you can get, and when a private GP or a hospital is the better choice.
headings: What is a Klinik Kesihatan? · Waktu operasi: when are Klinik Kesihatan open? · How much does it cost? · What services can you get? · Temujanji: how to book · Klinik Kesihatan, private clinic or hospital?
keywords: Guides Klinik Kesihatan guide Klinik Kesihatan Government clinic Public healthcare in Malaysia kencing manis gula hba1c darah tinggi hypertension bp tekanan darah kesihatan mental depression anxiety stress kemurungan mengandung hamil pregnancy antenatal vaksin suntikan jab immunisation kecemasan emergency a&e hospital klinik doctor doktor gp saringan check-up checkup medical
body: Malaysia had 1,131 Klinik Kesihatan at the end of 2024, along with Klinik Komuniti, rural clinics and maternal and child health clinics. Malaysians pay RM1 to see a doctor and RM5 to see a specialist. People aged 60 and over are treated free as outpatients, and other groups may be exempt. Most Klinik Kesihatan keep government office hours. About 49 have extended hours on weekday evenings and Saturday mornings, and a few are also open on Sundays and public holidays. You can book through MySejahtera for many services, but walk-ins are still accepted. Booked patients are prioritised, and fever or infectious cases don’t need an appointment. Non-citizens can attend any government clinic but pay much more, listed by the ministry at RM40 for general outpatient care and RM120 for a specialist, with tests charged extra. A Klinik Kesihatan (KK) is a primary care clinic run by the Ministry of Health (KKM). Ministry data to December 2024 lists 1,131 Klinik Kesihatan , 1,656 rural clinics (Klinik Desa), 205 Klinik Komuniti and 77 maternal and child health clinics. Klinik Kesihatan range from very large clinics seeing more than 800 patients a day to small ones seeing fewer than 50. Type What it offers Klinik Kesihatan Doctors, nurses and a wide range of outpatient, family and chronic disease care Klinik Komuniti Smaller clinics for primary care, some with evening hours Klinik Desa Rural clinics, mainly for basic care Hospital specialist clinic Specialist care, usually with a referral letter Hospital emergency department Emergencies, with no referral needed Private GP clinic Walk-in care, often with longer hours. Each clinic sets its own charges Hours vary by clinic, so check your own clinic before you go . We couldn’t find one current national list. Ordinary hours: Klinik Kesihatan generally keep government office hours on working days. Klinik Kesihatan Jalan Masjid, for example, opens from 8am to 5pm on weekdays. Kedah, Kelantan and Terengganu have a Friday and Saturday weekend, so check which days your clinic is open. Johor returned to a Saturday and Sunday weekend from 1 January 2025. Extended hours (waktu lanjutan): 49 clinics were running extended hours in March 2025, usually on weekdays from 5pm to 9.30pm and on Saturdays from 9am to 1pm . Hours differ between clinics, and some close at 9pm. Sundays and public holidays: six pilot clinics also opened on these days as of March 2025: Bandar Botanik, Ampang, Taman Ehsan, Kuala Lumpur, Greentown and Mahmoodiah. Penang, October 2026: some clinics in Seberang Jaya and Bayan Baru open on weekday evenings and Saturday mornings, KK UTC Komtar and KK Penang Sentral open at weekends, and eight Klinik Komuniti open daily from noon to 9pm. If your Klinik Kesihatan is closed and you need a doctor, a private clinic may be open. See our lists of clinics open on Sunday and 24-hour clinics . Who Doctor Specialist Malaysian citizens RM1 RM5 Malaysians aged 60 and over Free Free Non-citizens RM40 RM120 Other groups that may be exempt , according to ministry statements and hospital notices, include: government staff, with a letter students or children under 21, with a school letter babies under 1 year old antenatal and postnatal mothers people registered as OKU or receiving welfare help people with infectious diseases, and blood donors Sources differ on the exact rules for children, so bring your documents and ask at the counter. For non-citizens, the fee covers registration, consultation and medicine, and laboratory tests and other services cost extra. Permanent residents and foreign spouses with a Malaysian marriage certificate have been listed as paying RM5 for a specialist. Malaysian citizens pay RM1 to see a doctor at a Klinik Kesihatan. general outpatient care for common illness diabetes , high blood pressure and other long-term conditions antenatal and postnatal care baby and child vaccinations family planning and contraception mental health care and help to stop smoking pre-employment, study, Haj and pre-marital health checks dental care, at clinics with a dental service prescription refills through MyUBAT , including delivery or drive-through collection at some clinics Not every clinic offers every service. PeKa B40 health screening is carried out at registered private clinics, according to the government portal. Update the MySejahtera app. Open Appointments , then choose Book Appointment . Choose the service. Choose the clinic. The app shows clinics near you. Pick a date and time, then confirm. Can you still walk in? Yes. In January 2026 the ministry rejected claims that walk-ins had ended. Walk-in patients are assessed first, and those with appointments are prioritised. Emergencies, fever and infectious cases don’t need an appointment. Bring your MyKad or passport, any referral letter or screening form, and documents showing that you are exempt from fees. Aim to arrive about 30 minutes early for an appointment. Waiting times: the deputy health minister said in 2026 that waits had been up to 3 hours in clinics before a new digital clinic system. After the change, 81% of patients at those clinics saw a doctor within an hour. These figures don’t cover every clinic, and 91 Klinik Kesihatan were operating over capacity in 2025. Choose a Klinik Kesihatan for long-term conditions, pregnancy care, baby vaccinations, and affordable care when you can wait. Choose a private GP for a quick visit, or when you need a doctor at night or at a weekend. Your employer’s panel clinic may be free for you. Go to a hospital emergency department or call 999 for chest pain, stroke symptoms, severe breathlessness, heavy bleeding or a seizure . Don’t wait to book. See our guide on clinic or emergency department . Doctors at government clinics can issue a medical chit (MC) after examining you, and can refer you to a hospital specialist when needed. What are the opening hours of a Klinik Kesihatan? Most keep government office hours on working days. Some have extended hours on weekday evenings and Saturday mornings, and a few open on Sundays and public holidays. Check your own clinic. How much is a Klinik Kesihatan visit? Malaysian citizens pay RM1 to see a doctor and RM5 to see a specialist. People aged 60 and over are treated free as outpatients. Can I go to a Klinik Kesihatan without an appointment? Yes. Walk-ins are still accepted, although those with appointments are prioritised. Fever, infectious illness and emergencies don’t need an appointment. How do I book a Klinik Kesihatan appointment? In the MySejahtera app, open Appointments, choose Book Appointment, then pick the service, clinic, date and time. Are Klinik Kesihatan open on Saturdays or Sundays? Clinics with extended hours open on Saturday mornings. Only a few pilot clinics have also opened on Sundays and public holidays. Can foreigners go to a Klinik Kesihatan? Yes, but they pay unsubsidised rates, listed at RM40 for general outpatient care and RM120 for a specialist. Tests cost extra. What is the difference between Klinik Kesihatan and Klinik Komuniti? Both are government clinics and are counted separately by the ministry. Klinik Kesihatan are usually larger and offer a wider range of services. Can a Klinik Kesihatan give an MC? Yes. A government medical officer can issue a medical certificate after examining you.

title: Cirit birit (diarrhoea): causes, treatment, which medicines work and when to see a doctor
desc: Most diarrhoea clears up within a week, and replacing fluids matters more than any medicine. How to use oral rehydration salts, which diarrhoea medicines help, why antibiotics usually don’t, and the danger signs in adults, children and babies.
headings: What is cirit birit? · Common causes · Oral rehydration salts: the most important treatment · Ubat cirit birit: which medicines work? · What to eat · When to see a doctor · Diabetes, kidney and heart medicines · Travel, and when stool tests are needed
keywords: Guides Cirit birit (diarrhoea) Diarrhoea Cirit birit Oral rehydration denggi aedes nyamuk mosquito kencing manis gula hba1c darah tinggi hypertension bp tekanan darah payudara kanser cancer mammogram pink october mengandung hamil pregnancy antenatal kecemasan emergency a&e hospital aesthetic estetik kecantikan beauty kulit skin botox filler laser facial
body: Diarrhoea means 3 or more loose stools a day. It usually clears up in 5 to 7 days. Diarrhoea that lasts more than 4 weeks is chronic and needs checking. Oral rehydration salts (ORS) are the most important treatment. Follow the instructions on the packet. Plain water, soft drinks, apple juice and young coconut water aren’t good replacements for ORS in children. Adults can use loperamide for short-term relief, but not if there is blood in the stool or a high fever. It is not recommended for children with gastroenteritis. Antibiotics usually don’t help, as most cases are caused by viruses. Kaolin and charcoal have no proven benefit. See a doctor for blood in the stool, diarrhoea lasting more than 7 days, signs of dehydration, or if you can’t keep fluids down. Babies need help sooner. Cirit birit (also written cirit-birit ) means diarrhoea. The World Health Organization defines it as passing 3 or more loose or watery stools a day , or more often than is normal for you. Soft, pasty stools in breastfed babies are normal. Type How long it lasts Acute Usually less than 7 days, and up to 14 days Persistent 14 days or more Chronic More than 4 weeks In Malaysia, a national survey found that about 4 in 100 children under 5 had diarrhoea in the previous two weeks, with higher rates in homes using untreated water. Infections: viruses such as rotavirus and norovirus, bacteria and parasites. See our guide to food poisoning and gastroenteritis . Medicines: antibiotics, metformin, gliptins, magnesium products, anti-inflammatory painkillers and some blood pressure tablets (ACE inhibitors) Food and drink: lactose intolerance, artificial sweeteners and alcohol Bowel conditions: irritable bowel syndrome, coeliac disease, inflammatory bowel disease and bile acid diarrhoea Other conditions: an overactive thyroid Bowel cancer : loose stools or more frequent stools that continue, especially with blood or weight loss, should be checked Diarrhoea drains water and salts from the body. Oral rehydration salts (ORS, or garam rehidrasi oral ) replace both, using the right balance of salt and sugar to help your gut absorb water. Mix it as the packet says. Sachet sizes differ. The Malaysian Ministry of Health’s training manual uses one sachet in 250ml of cooled boiled water for its product, while WHO-style packets are made up with about 1 litre. Throw away any mixture after 24 hours . Adults: drink as much as you want, in small frequent sips, especially after each loose stool. Children without dehydration: give an extra 50 to 100ml after each loose stool up to age 2, and 100 to 200ml from age 2. If vomiting: wait 5 to 10 minutes, then give it more slowly. For a child under 2, give a teaspoon every 1 to 2 minutes. What about other drinks? The 2026 Malaysian children’s guideline lists cola, apple juice, young coconut water, chicken broth, tea and isotonic sports drinks as unsuitable for treating dehydration. They have much less sodium than ORS, and very sugary drinks can make diarrhoea worse. Healthy adults with mild diarrhoea can usually manage with fluids plus salty food, but ORS is the better choice if you are older, unwell or passing a lot of stool. Replacing fluids and salts comes first. Medicines play a smaller part. Medicine Does it help? Loperamide Reduces stool frequency in adults. Don’t use with blood in the stool or a high fever. Bismuth subsalicylate Can help adults. Not for under-12s or people with aspirin allergy, gout, kidney problems or on blood thinners. Turns the tongue and stools black. Probiotics A 2020 Cochrane review of 82 studies found probably little or no difference to diarrhoea lasting 48 hours or more. The Malaysian children’s guideline allows selected strains as an add-on. Zinc (children) WHO recommends 10 to 14 days of zinc. The 2026 Malaysian guideline suggests it mainly for malnourished children or those likely to be deficient. Ask your doctor. Racecadotril and diosmectite (children) May be considered by a doctor. Evidence is limited. Kaolin and charcoal Ministry of Health training material says these have no benefit. The Malaysian children’s guideline doesn’t recommend kaolin/pectin. Antibiotics Usually not needed. Doctors use them for specific infections such as cholera, Shigella dysentery and some serious infections. Loperamide for adults: UK guidance is 2 capsules at first, then 1 after each loose stool, with a maximum of 6 capsules in 24 hours when bought without a prescription, for no more than 48 hours. Taking too much can cause dangerous heart rhythm problems. It is available from pharmacists for ages 12 and over under UK rules, but the Malaysian children’s guideline advises against it in children with gastroenteritis, because deaths have been reported, especially under the age of 3. Ask a pharmacist or doctor if you are pregnant or have liver disease. Antibiotics can harm. With certain E. coli infections, they can raise the risk of serious kidney complications. Don’t use leftover antibiotics. Keep eating as soon as you feel able to. Children shouldn’t go without food for more than 4 to 6 hours after rehydration has started. A strict “BRAT” diet (bananas, rice, apple sauce and toast) is no longer needed and is unnecessarily restrictive, though plain foods such as rice porridge may be easier to manage. Avoid fatty and spicy food, fizzy drinks, undiluted fruit juice, caffeine and alcohol while you recover. Babies: continue breastfeeding. Don’t dilute formula, and there is usually no need to switch to lactose-free milk. Signs of dehydration: thirst, dark urine, passing little urine, dizziness, a dry mouth and sunken eyes. In babies, also look for a sunken soft spot on the head, few tears, fewer wet nappies, and drowsiness or irritability. Adults should see a doctor promptly for: blood in the stool diarrhoea lasting more than 7 days, or vomiting for more than 2 days being unable to keep fluids down signs of dehydration that continue despite ORS diarrhoea with a high fever, or after recent antibiotics, if it is severe older age or a weak immune system Children and babies should be seen urgently if: they can’t drink or breastfeed, or are getting sicker there is blood in the stool or a fever they keep vomiting, particularly if the vomit is green they are unusually sleepy, or show signs of dehydration you are worried about a baby under 12 months, or the baby has stopped feeding Go to an emergency department or call 999 for: vomiting blood, severe tummy pain, confusion, a stiff neck, pale, blue or grey skin, severe breathlessness, or a seizure . In dengue season, diarrhoea or vomiting more than 3 times in 24 hours during a fever can be a warning sign, and needs to be checked. If you can’t eat and drink normally, some medicines can become risky, including SGLT2 inhibitors, metformin, sulfonylureas, GLP-1 medicines, water tablets, ACE inhibitors, ARBs and anti-inflammatory painkillers. UK “sick day rules” advise pausing these until you are well. Never stop insulin. We didn’t find equivalent Malaysian guidance, so ask your doctor or pharmacist for a plan in advance. Seek help the same day if you take an SGLT2 inhibitor and feel unwell, as a dangerous complication (ketoacidosis) can occur even with normal blood sugar. See our guide to blood sugar levels . Most traveller’s diarrhoea is caused by bacteria. Treat it with fluids, and carry ORS if you are travelling. If it lasts more than 2 weeks, a parasite may be the cause. Going on pilgrimage? See our guide to Umrah and Haj health . Your doctor may arrange a stool test if there is blood in the stool, severe illness, diarrhoea lasting more than 7 days, a weak immune system, or an outbreak. Chronic diarrhoea may need further tests, such as blood tests or a colonoscopy. What is cirit birit in English? Cirit birit means diarrhoea (spelled diarrhea in American English): passing loose or watery stools 3 or more times a day. What is the best ubat cirit birit? Oral rehydration salts are the most important treatment. Adults can also use loperamide for short-term relief if there is no blood in the stool or high fever. Ask a pharmacist. How do I stop diarrhoea quickly? Replace fluids with ORS and eat as normal when you can. Loperamide can reduce stool frequency in adults. Most diarrhoea clears up within 5 to 7 days. Is coconut water good for diarrhoea? Not as a replacement for ORS. Malaysian children’s guidelines list young coconut water as unsuitable, as it has much less sodium than ORS. Do I need antibiotics for diarrhoea? Usually not, as most cases are viral. Antibiotics are used for specific infections, and can sometimes be harmful. How long is too long for diarrhoea? See a doctor if it lasts more than 7 days in an adult, or sooner with blood, dehydration or a fever. Diarrhoea lasting more than 4 weeks is chronic. Can I give loperamide to my child? It is not recommended for children with gastroenteritis, as deaths have been reported, especially under the age of 3. See a doctor. Should I stop breastfeeding if my baby has diarrhoea? No. Keep breastfeeding, and give extra fluids as your doctor advises.

title: FOMEMA online result check: how to check a medical report by passport number, what each status means and what to do next
desc: Waiting for a FOMEMA result? Workers and employers can check it online for free. Where to check, what each status means, how long results take, why a result may not appear, and what happens after a Suitable or Unsuitable result.
headings: Where to check a FOMEMA result · How workers can check (MyIMMs) · How employers and agencies can check (FOMEMA portal) · What each FOMEMA status means · How long does a FOMEMA result take? · What to do if a result doesn’t appear · What happens after the result? · Sabah and Sarawak
keywords: Guides FOMEMA online result check FOMEMA Foreign worker medical examination Medical report MyIMMs kencing manis gula hba1c darah tinggi hypertension bp tekanan darah mengandung hamil pregnancy antenatal klinik doctor doktor gp saringan check-up checkup medical
body: Workers can check for free on the Immigration Department’s MyIMMs “Fomema Status Inquiries” page, using their passport number or name and nationality. Employers and agencies log in to the FOMEMA portal at portal.fomema.my and open “Medical Result”. This is also where you print the medical report or unsuitable letter. Under normal circumstances, results reach Immigration headquarters within 7 working days of the examination. A “Pending” status shows which step is holding things up. If nothing appears at Immigration, the usual cause is a mismatch in the passport number, name, gender, date of birth or nationality. A result is valid at Immigration for 180 days. Some Unsuitable results can be appealed, but only if FOMEMA emails to say the case is eligible. Where Who can use it What you need MyIMMs: Fomema Status Inquiries Anyone, including workers. No login needed. Passport number and nationality, or name and nationality FOMEMA Online Portal Employers and agencies Employer or agency login FOMEMA’s official website is fomema2u.com.my . When we tested older addresses in November 2026, fomema.com.my and fomemaonline.com didn’t work as result checkers. Checking a result is free. We found no official route that needs a payment or an agent, so be wary of anyone who charges you just to look up a result. Open the Fomema Status Inquiries page on the Immigration Department website. Fill in one of the two forms: Passport No and Citizen (your nationality), or Name and Citizen . Submit the form to see the status held by Immigration. Enter your details exactly as they appear in your passport. This page shows the status held by Immigration. The full medical report and any unsuitable letter are available through the employer’s portal, so ask your employer or agency for a copy. Immigration’s systems may change. If the link stops working, check the Immigration Department website . Log in to the FOMEMA Online Portal as an employer or agency. Open Medical Result . Enter the worker code or passport number, then choose Search . You can search up to 10 workers at a time. For a medical report, go to Registration History and choose Print Report . For an Unsuitable result, use Print Unsuitable Letter . Workers can check their status on the Immigration page, while employers can see the full result in the FOMEMA portal. Status What it means Pending Select Clinic A clinic hasn’t been chosen yet Pending Examination The worker hasn’t attended the examination Pending Lab and X-ray Transmission The laboratory and X-ray results haven’t been sent yet. You may also see Pending Lab or Pending X-ray Transmission. Pending for Certification The clinic hasn’t sent the result to FOMEMA. Check with the clinic. FOMEMA Review The result is under review before release to Immigration Suitable The worker is medically fit, and the employer can go on to renew the permit Unsuitable The worker is not medically fit. The reason appears under “Reason”. Expired The result is more than 180 days old, or the form’s validity has ended. A new form must be bought. Cancelled The employer has asked for a refund Result to Immigration: within 7 working days of the examination, under normal circumstances. FOMEMA Review: the final result comes within 5 working days after certification. Attending the exam: the registration form is valid for 30 days from payment. Certification: if the examination isn’t certified within 30 days of the clinic visit, the status becomes Expired. Validity: a result is valid at Immigration for 180 days from the examination date. Annual exam: since 16 December 2023, all foreign workers have to be examined every year. Check the status in the FOMEMA portal. A Pending status tells you which step is holding things up. If it says Pending for Certification, contact the clinic that did the examination. If there is no record at Immigration, the most common cause is a mismatch in the passport number, name, gender, date of birth or nationality. Employers can correct this under Register Worker , using the edit option. If you can’t correct it, email cs@fomema.com.my with the amendment form, passport copies, the permit or approval, and a screenshot. This can take up to 3 working days. Contact FOMEMA: WhatsApp 03-2782 8777 or email cs@fomema.com.my , Monday to Friday, 9am to 5pm, except national and Selangor public holidays. If the result is Suitable: the employer can go on to renew the work permit (PLKS). Immigration advises applying 3 months before the permit expires. If the result is Unsuitable: Appeals are only possible if FOMEMA emails to say the case is eligible. Register the appeal on the portal within 2 weeks of certification, and submit any extra test results within 4 weeks of registering the appeal, or the case will be closed. Not appealable: tuberculosis confirmed by radiologist audit, malaria, pregnancy, HIV and hepatitis B . Syphilis: FOMEMA’s appeal FAQ says it has been appealable since 20 July 2026, with treatment and 6 months’ monitoring, although another FOMEMA page still lists it as non-appealable. Check with FOMEMA. Going home: workers who are not cleared must be sent home. For PLKS holders, the Check Out Memo has been online only since 1 September 2025, through MyPASS@JIM or FWCMS. Immigration counters no longer accept these applications. Some long-term conditions, such as diabetes and high blood pressure, can be cleared through a 6-month monitoring programme. See our full guide to the FOMEMA medical check-up for tests, fees and appeals. FOMEMA covers Peninsular Malaysia and Labuan. Sabah and Sarawak have their own arrangements. In Sarawak , foreign worker health screening is run through SAFHIS , and employers see a fit or unfit result. In Sabah , check with the state Immigration office or your appointed medical provider. How do I check my medical report online in Malaysia by passport number? For a foreign worker’s FOMEMA medical examination, open the Immigration Department’s MyIMMs “Fomema Status Inquiries” page, enter the passport number and choose the nationality. It is free and doesn’t need a login. How do I check my FOMEMA result online? Open the Immigration Department’s MyIMMs “Fomema Status Inquiries” page and enter your passport number or name with your nationality. Employers can log in to the FOMEMA portal and open “Medical Result”. Can a worker check their own FOMEMA result? Yes. The MyIMMs page is public and doesn’t need a login. For the full medical report, ask your employer or agency. How long does a FOMEMA result take? Under normal circumstances, the result reaches Immigration within 7 working days of the examination. Cases under FOMEMA Review get a final result within 5 working days after certification. What does Pending for Certification mean? The clinic has not yet sent the result to FOMEMA. Contact the clinic that did the examination. Why is my FOMEMA result not showing? It may still be pending. If there is no record at Immigration, check that the passport number, name, gender, date of birth and nationality match exactly. How long is a FOMEMA result valid? It is valid at Immigration for 180 days from the examination date. Does FOMEMA cover Sabah and Sarawak? No. FOMEMA covers Peninsular Malaysia and Labuan. Sabah and Sarawak have their own screening arrangements. What is the FOMEMA login page? Employers and agencies log in at portal.fomema.my. FOMEMA’s official website is fomema2u.com.my.

title: Normal body temperature (suhu badan normal) and fever in adults: the numbers and when to see a doctor
desc: Is 37.5°C a fever? Normal body temperature is lower than most people think and changes through the day. What the numbers mean, which thermometer to trust, how to treat a fever safely in Malaysia, and when to see a doctor.
headings: What is a normal body temperature? · What temperature is a fever? · How to take your temperature properly · Treating a fever at home · Common causes of fever in Malaysia · When to see a doctor
keywords: Prevention Normal body temperature Body temperature Fever Demam denggi aedes nyamuk mosquito kencing manis gula hba1c mengandung hamil pregnancy antenatal kecemasan emergency a&e hospital aesthetic estetik kecantikan beauty kulit skin botox filler laser facial
body: Modern studies put average adult temperature nearer 36.6°C than 37°C. It is lowest in the early morning and can reach 37.7°C by late afternoon. A temperature of 38°C or above by mouth is generally a fever. An ear reading is about 0.6°C higher than by mouth, and a forehead reading is about 0.6°C lower. Older people may have a serious infection with little or no fever. New confusion or sudden weakness can be the first sign. In Malaysia, use paracetamol for fever and avoid aspirin, mefenamic acid and ibuprofen until dengue has been ruled out. See a doctor if a fever lasts more than 2 days without improving, and urgently for confusion, a stiff neck, purple spots, breathlessness or dengue warning signs. In dengue, you can get worse as the fever falls. The familiar figure of 37°C comes from a German doctor’s measurements in 1851, which were taken in the armpit. Modern studies have found lower averages: A 1992 US study of 148 healthy adults found an average oral temperature of 36.8°C , with an upper limit of 37.7°C. A 2017 study of more than 35,000 UK patients found an average of 36.6°C . A 2023 US study of nearly 400,000 outpatient visits found that no group had an average as high as 37°C. “Normal” differs from person to person, and it changes with: Time of day: lowest in the early morning and highest in the late afternoon Age: tends to be lower in older people Menstrual cycle: about 0.3 to 0.7°C higher in the second half of the cycle Your thermometer and where you take the reading Small Malaysian and Japanese comparisons suggest that people living in hot climates may have slightly different resting temperatures, but nothing supports using a different fever threshold in Malaysia. Oral reading What it generally means Below 35°C Hypothermia. See a doctor right away About 36.5 to 37.5°C Normal for most adults 37.5 to 37.9°C Low-grade fever (there is no agreed range) 38°C and above Fever Above 39.4°C Call or see a doctor Above 40°C See a doctor right away Above 41.5°C Hyperpyrexia, a medical emergency The site of the reading matters. As a rough guide, ear and rectal readings are about 0.6°C higher than oral readings, and forehead readings are about 0.6°C lower. That means a forehead reading of about 37.4°C can correspond to an oral reading of 38°C. Armpit readings are the least reliable. You can feel hot, shivery or unwell with a reading below 38°C. How you feel matters as well as the number. Older people: more than half of older long-term care residents with a serious infection don’t develop a typical fever. For them, a temperature above 37.8°C, repeated readings above 37.2°C, or a rise of more than 1.1°C above their usual temperature can be significant. A low temperature can also be a sign of sepsis. Normal temperature varies through the day, so one borderline reading matters less than how you feel and how it changes. Use a digital thermometer under the tongue, as the NHS advises. Keep your mouth closed until it beeps. Wait after hot or cold drinks. A small study suggested about 15 minutes after a cold drink and 23 minutes after a hot one. Rest after exercise too. Forehead (infrared) thermometers: follow the instructions, make sure your forehead is dry and uncovered, and don’t use one in sunlight or a draught. Let it adjust to the room for 10 to 30 minutes if it has been moved. A 2015 review found that home-style thermometers, including ear, forehead, armpit and oral types, missed around a third of fevers, and forehead devices aren’t recommended for detecting one. If you feel ill, go by how you feel as well as the number. Avoid mercury thermometers. The WHO has called for them to be phased out, because of the danger if they break. A fever is part of the body’s response to infection, and it doesn’t always need treating. Medicine is usually unnecessary below about 38.3°C if you feel all right. Take it if you feel unwell. Rest and drink plenty of fluids. In suspected dengue, the Malaysian guideline advises more than 2 litres a day, and not plain water alone. Paracetamol: 500mg to 1g, at least 4 hours apart, with no more than 4g in 24 hours. If you weigh under 50kg, you may need less. Many cold and flu remedies also contain paracetamol, so check the label. See our guide to painkillers . Avoid aspirin, mefenamic acid and ibuprofen until dengue has been ruled out, because of the risk of bleeding. Guidance from other countries may recommend ibuprofen for fever, but this advice doesn’t account for dengue. Cooling: Malaysian dengue guidance lists tepid sponging. Other guidance says extra cooling is only needed for very high temperatures, around 41°C. Don’t use rubbing alcohol. Antibiotics don’t treat viral fevers, including dengue, flu and most coughs and colds. Don’t have injections, massage or cupping when you have suspected dengue. Dengue : fever for 2 to 7 days, with headache, body aches and sometimes a rash Influenza , colds and COVID-19 Urinary tract infections , especially with back pain or burning urine Leptospirosis , from water or soil contaminated by animal urine, which can cause fever, red eyes and jaundice Typhoid : prolonged high fever and tummy pain Malaria , after time in forest areas of Sabah, Sarawak, Kelantan or Pahang, or travel abroad Tuberculosis : a long-lasting cough, night sweats and weight loss A fever without a clear cause: doctors use the term “fever of unknown origin” for a temperature above 38.3°C lasting more than 3 weeks, with no cause found after investigation. Infections, cancers and autoimmune conditions can all cause it. Fever or heat illness? In hot weather, heat exhaustion causes heavy sweating, cool clammy skin and tiredness, and should improve within 30 minutes of cooling down and drinking. Heatstroke is an emergency : look for confusion, seizures or collapse, and call 999 . Malaysia recorded 45 heat illness cases, including 2 deaths, in early 2024. Go to an emergency department or call 999 for a fever with: confusion, unusual drowsiness or difficulty waking severe headache with a stiff neck a purple or dark rash that doesn’t fade breathlessness or chest pain a seizure severe tummy pain Dengue warning signs need hospital care straight away, even if the fever is going down: tummy pain or tenderness vomiting or diarrhoea more than 3 times in 24 hours bleeding from the nose or gums, black stools or unusually heavy periods drowsiness, restlessness or irritability cold, clammy skin or difficulty breathing See a doctor promptly if: your fever has lasted 24 to 48 hours without improving, and in any case by 3 to 4 days your temperature is above 39.4°C you are pregnant, over 65, or have a weakened immune system or a long-term condition such as diabetes you have recently had a baby or a miscarriage you have recently been in a forest area or abroad What is a normal body temperature for an adult? About 36.5°C to 37.5°C for most adults, although modern studies put the average nearer 36.6°C. It changes through the day. Is 37.5°C a fever? It is usually considered at most a low-grade fever when taken by mouth. A fever is generally 38°C or above. A reading of 37.5°C on the forehead may be closer to 38°C by mouth. Is 38°C a high fever? It is a fever, but there is no agreed definition of a high fever. See a doctor if it lasts more than 2 days, if it goes above 39.4°C, or if you have any danger signs. Is 36°C normal? It can be normal, especially early in the morning or in older people. A reading below 35°C is hypothermia. A low temperature with feeling very unwell may be a sign of serious infection. Which thermometer is the most accurate at home? A digital thermometer used under the tongue is a good choice. Forehead and ear thermometers are convenient, but they can miss fevers. Can I take ibuprofen for a fever in Malaysia? Avoid ibuprofen, aspirin and mefenamic acid until dengue has been ruled out, because they can increase the risk of bleeding. Use paracetamol instead. How many days of fever is too long? See a doctor if a fever lasts more than 24 to 48 hours without improving, and in any case by 3 to 4 days. In dengue season, see a doctor early.

title: Sawan (seizures and fits): first aid, causes and epilepsy in Malaysia
desc: If someone has a fit in front of you, what should you do? Step-by-step seizure first aid, why you should never put a spoon in the mouth, when to call 999, what causes seizures, and how epilepsy is treated in Malaysia.
headings: First aid: what to do if someone has a seizure · What is a seizure? · What causes seizures? · Febrile seizures (sawan demam) in children · Epilepsy (epilepsi) · Living with epilepsy in Malaysia
keywords: Guides Sawan (seizures) and epilepsy Seizure Epilepsy Sawan kencing manis gula hba1c darah tinggi hypertension bp tekanan darah mengandung hamil pregnancy antenatal kecemasan emergency a&e hospital klinik doctor doktor gp
body: During a seizure: time it, move dangerous objects away, cushion the head, and stay with the person. Once the jerking stops, turn them on their side. Never put a spoon, your fingers or anything else in their mouth. A person can’t swallow their tongue. Don’t hold them down, and don’t give food, water or pills until they are fully awake. Call 999 if it is a first seizure, it lasts more than 5 minutes, seizures repeat without recovery, the person is injured, or they have trouble breathing. One seizure isn’t the same as epilepsy. Epilepsy generally means two or more unprovoked seizures, or one with a high risk of more. Up to 70% of people with epilepsy can become seizure-free with the right treatment. Don’t stop medicines without specialist advice, especially in pregnancy. Stay calm and time it. Note when the seizure started. Make the area safe. Move sharp or hot objects away. Only move the person if they are in danger, such as on a road or near water. Cushion the head with something soft, such as a folded jacket, and loosen anything tight around the neck. When the jerking stops, turn them on their side in the recovery position, to keep the airway clear. Stay with them until they have fully recovered. Speak gently and tell them what happened. What not to do: Don’t put anything in their mouth , including a spoon, stick, wallet or your fingers. A person can’t swallow their tongue. In Malaysia, doctors still have to warn people against using a spoon. It can break teeth and block the airway. Don’t hold them down or try to stop the jerking. Don’t give food, water or pills until they are fully awake, as these can enter the lungs. Don’t crowd them or try to wake them up. When to call 999 it is the person’s first seizure , or you don’t know whether it is it lasts more than 5 minutes , or longer than is usual for them another seizure starts without them recovering in between they don’t recover fully, or they have trouble breathing they are seriously injured they have had three or more seizures in 24 hours A seizure lasting 5 minutes or more is called status epilepticus and is a medical emergency. Stay with the person until they have fully recovered and tell them what happened. A seizure is a sudden burst of electrical activity in the brain that temporarily affects how it works. Not every seizure involves falling and jerking. Type What it looks like Tonic-clonic The person loses consciousness, goes stiff, falls and jerks, then is tired and confused afterwards Focal Starts in one part of the brain. There may be twitching, lip-smacking or strange smells or feelings, and the person may stay aware Absence A few seconds of blankness, more common in children, and easily mistaken for daydreaming Seizure or faint? Someone who has fainted usually wakes within about 30 seconds and recovers quickly. See our guide to low blood pressure and fainting . Call 999 if someone who has fainted is shaking or jerking, or hasn’t woken within a minute. Epilepsy High fever in young children (see below) Low blood sugar , especially in people taking insulin Stroke, head injury, a brain tumour or infections such as meningitis and encephalitis Alcohol or drug intoxication or withdrawal Low sodium or high calcium levels in the blood Eclampsia , a serious complication of pregnancy. A seizure in pregnancy or after birth is always an emergency. Seizures caused by a temporary problem are called “provoked” seizures and may not happen again once that problem is treated. In about half of people with epilepsy worldwide, no cause is found. Febrile seizures are fits triggered by a fever, usually in children aged 6 months to 6 years. They are frightening, but few children go on to develop epilepsy. Call 999 or go to an emergency department if it is the first one, it lasts more than 5 minutes, your child has trouble breathing, the twitching affects only one side, your child is still sleepy after an hour, or it happens again within 24 hours. Don’t try to cool your child by sponging. See our guide to fever in children . Epilepsy generally means two or more unprovoked seizures, or one seizure with tests showing a high risk of more. A Malaysian community survey estimated that about 8 in 1,000 people have had epilepsy at some time, although that figure rests on a small number of confirmed cases. Tests: a detailed account from someone who saw the seizure is very useful, so try to film it if it is safe. Doctors may arrange an EEG (brainwave test), an MRI or CT scan, blood tests and a heart tracing (ECG). A normal EEG doesn’t rule out epilepsy. Treatment: Anti-seizure medicines are the main treatment. Generic options include carbamazepine, lamotrigine, levetiracetam, oxcarbazepine and sodium valproate. The choice depends on the type of seizure, your age, and whether you might become pregnant. Up to 70% of people can become seizure-free. More than 30% continue to have seizures despite treatment and may be referred to a specialist centre. Surgery can help selected people whose seizures start in one area of the brain. Ketogenic diets , under medical supervision, can help some people whose seizures don’t respond to medicines. Stopping medicines: your doctor may discuss this after at least 2 years without a seizure, but seizures do come back in a substantial proportion of people. Reduce them only under specialist guidance. Rescue medicines: for long seizures, doctors may prescribe midazolam or rectal diazepam, and train family members in how to use them at home. SUDEP: sudden unexpected death in epilepsy happens in about 1 in 1,000 adults with epilepsy each year. The risk is highest in people with uncontrolled tonic-clonic seizures, particularly at night. Taking your medicines reliably is the most important way to reduce it. Words matter. The old Malay term gila babi is stigmatising and is no longer used by doctors. The recommended word is epilepsi . Common triggers: missed medicines, lack of sleep, stress, alcohol and periods. Keep a seizure diary. Safety at home: choose showers over baths, or have someone nearby when bathing. Swim only with someone who knows what to do. Avoid ladders and working at heights. Pregnancy: Malaysia’s drug regulator warns that sodium valproate carries about a 10% risk of birth defects and up to a 30 to 40% risk of serious developmental problems. It should only be used in women if there is no alternative. Plan pregnancy with your doctor, ask about folic acid, and don’t stop your medicine without talking to your doctor first. Driving: Malaysian law requires you to declare any condition likely to endanger the public when applying for or holding a licence, and knowingly driving with such a condition is an offence. Malaysian clinical guidelines suggest that driving may be allowed if epilepsy is well controlled and you have been seizure-free for at least a year, but public buses, heavy machinery and commercial flying are not allowed. Ask your neurologist and JPJ about your situation. Support: Persatuan Epilepsi Malaysia and the Epilepsy Council of the Malaysian Society of Neurosciences provide information for patients and families. What is sawan in English? Sawan means a seizure or fit. Sawan demam is a febrile seizure, a fit triggered by a fever in a young child. What should I do if someone has a seizure? Time it, move dangerous objects away, cushion the head, and stay with them. Turn them on their side once the jerking stops. Call 999 if it lasts more than 5 minutes or is a first seizure. Should I put a spoon in someone’s mouth during a seizure? No. Never put anything in their mouth. A person can’t swallow their tongue, and objects can break teeth or block the airway. Does one seizure mean I have epilepsy? Not necessarily. Many single seizures have a temporary cause. Epilepsy generally means two or more unprovoked seizures, or one with a high risk of more. How long can a seizure last before it is an emergency? Call 999 if it lasts more than 5 minutes, or longer than is usual for the person. Can epilepsy be cured? Up to 70% of people become seizure-free with treatment, and many children outgrow it. Some people can eventually stop medicines under specialist guidance. Can you drive with epilepsy in Malaysia? You must declare it. Malaysian clinical guidelines suggest driving may be allowed when epilepsy is well controlled and you have been seizure-free for at least a year. Ask your neurologist and JPJ. Is sawan dangerous? Most seizures stop by themselves within a few minutes. The dangers are injuries, seizures lasting more than 5 minutes, and rarely sudden death, so treatment and first aid both matter.

title: Umrah and Haj vaccines for Malaysians (vaksin umrah): meningitis jab, certificates and health checks
desc: Going for Umrah or Haj? What Saudi Arabia and the Malaysian Ministry of Health require, when to get the meningitis vaccine, what your certificate must show, how the Haj health exam works, and how to stay well in the heat and crowds.
headings: Which vaccines do you need for Umrah and Haj? · The meningitis jab: timing and your certificate · Where to get the vaccine in Malaysia · The Haj health exam · Other vaccines to consider · Side effects, pregnancy and who should check first · Staying well on your trip
keywords: Prevention Umrah and Haj vaccines Meningococcal vaccine Umrah Hajj kencing manis gula hba1c darah tinggi hypertension bp tekanan darah mengandung hamil pregnancy antenatal vaksin suntikan jab immunisation klinik doctor doktor gp
body: Saudi Arabia requires a meningococcal ACWY vaccine for Umrah and Haj pilgrims, given at least 10 days before arrival. The Malaysian Ministry of Health advises having it at least two weeks before departure. A conjugate vaccine is valid for 5 years and a polysaccharide vaccine for 3 years. The certificate must show the vaccine name and date. If the type isn’t shown, it counts as valid for 3 years only. Saudi Arabia also requires COVID-19 vaccination proof from Umrah pilgrims aged over 65, pregnant women and people with certain chronic conditions, and advises a flu vaccine for all. Haj pilgrims must pass a health exam before receiving their offer. Saudi rules exclude people with conditions such as kidney failure on dialysis, advanced dementia, or late or high-risk pregnancy. Heat is one of the biggest dangers. More than 1,300 people died of heat-related causes during Haj 2024. Drink regularly, avoid direct sun and ask your doctor about any water tablets you take. These are Saudi Arabia’s published requirements for the 1447H (2026) season, the latest available at the time of writing. Check for updates before you travel , especially for Haj 2027. Vaccine Requirement Applies to Meningococcal ACWY Required. At least 10 days before arrival. All pilgrims COVID-19 Proof required for some Umrah pilgrims. Saudi Haj rules refer to “specific groups”. For Umrah: over-65s, pregnant women and people with listed chronic conditions Influenza Advised, using the current season’s vaccine All pilgrims, especially older people and those with chronic illness Polio and yellow fever Only for travellers from listed countries Malaysia isn’t on these lists Routine vaccines Saudi Arabia advises being up to date Diphtheria, tetanus, whooping cough, polio, measles, mumps, chickenpox In Malaysia: in May 2024 the Ministry of Health said Malaysian pilgrims “are required to take meningococcal vaccines” for both Haj and Umrah. For the 2025 Haj season, the ministry also made COVID-19 and flu vaccines compulsory for pilgrims aged 65 and over or at high risk. Requirements for 2027 hadn’t been confirmed when this guide was written, so check with Tabung Haji or your Umrah agency. Meningococcal disease spreads easily in crowds and can be fatal: about 1 in 6 people with bacterial meningitis die. The World Health Organization reported 11 confirmed cases linked to Umrah between January and March 2025. None of those people had been vaccinated. When to have it: Saudi rules say at least 10 days before arrival . The Malaysian Ministry of Health advises at least two weeks before departure . Following the Malaysian advice meets both, and allows time for your body to build protection. Vaccine type Accepted for Conjugate (ACWY or ACWYX) 5 years Polysaccharide 3 years Type not shown on the certificate 3 years only Your certificate should: clearly show the vaccine name and the date you had it have your name spelled as in your passport be an official vaccination certificate, not just a payment receipt Keep it with your passport and carry it on your trip. Saudi rules differ in how they describe checks for each country, and the WHO advises pilgrims to carry proof. Ask your agency how they will check it. If your earlier vaccine is still within its valid period, you don’t need another dose, as long as your certificate shows this. Have the meningitis vaccine at least two weeks before you travel, and keep the certificate with your passport. Umrah: the Ministry of Health said in 2024 that Umrah pilgrims should get the vaccine at private healthcare facilities. Many private GP clinics offer it, but stock varies, so call first and ask for the vaccine type and whether a certificate is included. Haj: vaccination is available at government facilities or privately. In the 2025 season, the COVID-19 vaccine was free at selected clinics, and the flu vaccine was free at selected government facilities for pilgrims aged 60 and over with a chronic illness. Check the current arrangements with Tabung Haji. Prices at private clinics vary, so ask what is included. Allow several weeks if you are going in a busy period. Malaysian Haj pilgrims must pass a health examination before they can receive their offer. In recent seasons: the exam is done at premises registered with Tabung Haji, and is free at government facilities you bring your MyKad and offer letter your status is shown by SMS, THiJARI or MySejahtera people who don’t meet the standard are advised to postpone Conditions that Saudi Arabia says should not travel (1447H rules): kidney failure needing dialysis heart failure with symptoms on minimal effort lung disease needing oxygen cirrhosis with liver failure severe neurological or psychiatric disorders that affect thinking, and dementia pregnancy in the last trimester, or high-risk pregnancy active infections such as open tuberculosis active cancer on chemotherapy, or severe immune-suppressing treatment Stable high blood pressure and diabetes don’t automatically rule you out, but get them under control well before the exam. Haj 2027 is expected around mid-May 2027, subject to the sighting of the moon, with the first flights from Malaysia around April. Influenza : strongly recommended by the US CDC for pilgrims. Respiratory infections are very common during Haj. Pneumococcal : pneumonia is among the most common reasons pilgrims are admitted to hospital. CDC advice covers those aged 65 and over and younger people with chronic illness. Ask your doctor. Hepatitis B : worth considering, as sharing razor blades at the end of the pilgrimage carries a risk. Use only licensed barbers and a new blade. Tetanus : check whether you are up to date. Common side effects: a sore or red arm, muscle pain, headache and tiredness, usually lasting a day or two. Serious reactions are rare. Mild illness generally doesn’t stop you being vaccinated. If you have a fever or are moderately unwell, ask your doctor whether to wait. Don’t have the vaccine if you have had a life-threatening allergic reaction to a previous dose or to one of its ingredients. Pregnancy: speak to your doctor. Saudi authorities have advised that pregnant women, children, frail older people and those seriously ill consider postponing. Children: Saudi rules don’t set a minimum age, and travel health guidance covers those aged 1 and over. Ask your doctor about the right vaccine for your child. Heat: temperatures can reach 50°C. Drink fluids regularly, avoid direct sun and rest in the shade. If you take water tablets (diuretics), ask your doctor before you go whether they need adjusting. Know your temperature numbers and danger signs . “Haj cough”: coughs and chest infections spread easily. Wash your hands, and wear a mask in crowds. See a doctor for fever, breathlessness or a cough that is getting worse. MERS: avoid camels and raw camel products. About 35% of people with this infection die. Seek medical advice if you develop a fever or cough within 14 days of returning, and tell the doctor you have been to Saudi Arabia. Medicines: carry them in their original packaging, with documents listing your conditions and treatment. Malaysian Haj pilgrims have also been registered for an International Patient Summary through MySejahtera. Diabetes: pack your medicines, syringes, glucose meter and fast-acting carbohydrate. Ask your doctor how to adjust doses for long walking days. Feet: long walks can cause blisters. People with diabetes or numb feet should wear protective footwear and cover any sore. Tummy upsets: keep to safe food and drink, and see our guide to diarrhoea (cirit birit) . Is the meningitis vaccine compulsory for Umrah from Malaysia? Yes. Saudi Arabia requires it for pilgrims, and the Malaysian Ministry of Health said in 2024 that Malaysian Haj and Umrah pilgrims are required to have it. How long before Umrah should I get the vaccine? At least two weeks before you leave, as advised by the Malaysian Ministry of Health. Saudi Arabia’s minimum is 10 days before arrival. How long is the meningitis vaccine valid for Umrah? A conjugate vaccine is accepted for 5 years and a polysaccharide vaccine for 3 years. If the certificate doesn’t show the vaccine type, it is accepted for 3 years only. Can I get the Umrah vaccine at a Klinik Kesihatan? The Ministry of Health said in 2024 that Umrah pilgrims should go to private healthcare facilities. Haj pilgrims can be vaccinated at government facilities. Do I need a flu vaccine for Umrah? Saudi Arabia advises it, and it is especially worthwhile for older people and those with chronic illness. Proof isn’t listed as a requirement for Umrah. Can I perform Umrah while pregnant? Speak to your doctor first. Saudi Haj rules exclude pregnancy in the last trimester or high-risk pregnancy, and authorities have advised pregnant women to consider postponing. What is “Haj cough”? A common term for coughs and chest infections that spread among pilgrims in crowded conditions. See a doctor for fever, breathlessness or a cough that is getting worse.

title: Malay medical terms in English: what cirit birit, bisul, buasir, sawan and other health words mean
desc: A plain guide to the Malay words Malaysians use for common illnesses and symptoms, from cirit birit to kayap, with the English and medical terms, words that have two meanings, and links to our guides.
headings: Stomach and bowels · Fever, coughs and breathing · Heart, blood and diabetes · Head, nerves and pain · Skin · Eyes · Women, babies and urinary problems · Swellings and injuries · English to Malay: common searches
keywords: Guides Malay medical terms in English Malay language Medical terminology Common illnesses kencing manis gula hba1c darah tinggi hypertension bp tekanan darah mengandung hamil pregnancy antenatal kecemasan emergency a&e hospital klinik doctor doktor gp aesthetic estetik kecantikan beauty kulit skin botox filler laser facial
body: Common words: cirit birit is diarrhoea, muntah is vomiting, loya is nausea, sembelit is constipation and buasir is piles. Skin words: bisul is a boil, kurap is ringworm, panau is a fungal skin patch, ketuat is a wart, kayap is shingles and nanah is pus. Some words have two meanings. Pening can mean dizziness or a headache, lelah can mean asthma or tiredness, and batuk kering can mean a dry cough or tuberculosis. Sawan means a seizure or fit. The old term gila babi for epilepsy is stigmatising, and doctors now use epilepsi. If you aren’t sure of the right word, describe what you feel and when it started. A doctor can work out the rest. Malay English Good to know Cirit birit Diarrhoea Also written cirit-birit Muntah Vomiting Loya Nausea, feeling sick Sembelit Constipation Buasir Piles (haemorrhoids) Sakit perut Stomach ache, tummy pain Gastrik Gastric pain, gastritis Often used for any upper tummy pain, including reflux and ulcers Kembung perut, angin Bloating, wind “Angin” can also describe a traditional idea of illness Keracunan makanan Food poisoning Malay English Good to know Demam Fever Demam panas High fever A description, not the name of a disease Selsema, selesema Common cold Can also refer to influenza Batuk Cough Batuk kering Dry cough, or tuberculosis Check which is meant Kahak Phlegm (sputum) Sakit tekak Sore throat Resdung Nasal allergy, sinus problems Used for allergic rhinitis and sinusitis Lelah Asthma, or tiredness Context decides which Semput Breathless A symptom. Severe breathlessness is an emergency Sesak nafas Shortness of breath Severe breathlessness is an emergency Malay English Good to know Darah tinggi High blood pressure (hypertension) Darah rendah Low blood pressure (hypotension) Not the same as kurang darah Kurang darah Anaemia Kencing manis Diabetes Sakit jantung Heart disease A heart attack is serangan jantung Angin ahmar Stroke A medical emergency Malay English Good to know Sawan Seizure, fit Doesn’t always mean epilepsy Epilepsi Epilepsy The old term gila babi is offensive and shouldn’t be used Pening Dizziness, or headache Tell the doctor which you mean Sakit kepala Headache Migrain Migraine Often one-sided, so people may say sakit kepala sebelah Pitam Blackout, feeling faint Naik pitam means furious Pengsan Fainted, unconscious Call 999 if the person doesn’t wake quickly Kebas Numbness, pins and needles Numb hands at night can be carpal tunnel syndrome Kejang Stiffness, cramp For a fit, the word is sawan Sengal Aching, stiff joints Sengal tulang means rheumatic pain Sakit pinggang Lower back pain Sakit sendi Joint pain Urat saraf terkepit Pinched nerve Malay English Good to know Bisul Boil (furuncle) Nanah Pus Kurap Ringworm (tinea) A fungal infection, not a worm Panau Pale or dark skin patches (tinea versicolor) Kudis Sores, itchy skin infection Often used for scabies Kudis buta Scabies Ketuat Wart Kayap Shingles (herpes zoster) Cacar air Chickenpox Campak Measles Beguk Mumps Some dictionaries also list goitre Jerawat Pimple, acne Ruam Rash Ruam panas is heat rash Ruam lampin Nappy rash Gatal Itchy In casual speech, it can also mean flirtatious Malay English Good to know Sakit mata Eye pain or trouble Often used for conjunctivitis, but can mean any eye problem Mata merah Red eye A symptom. Often conjunctivitis Ketumbit Stye Also called tembel Rabun Blurred vision Rabun jauh is short-sightedness Malay English Good to know Senggugut Period pain (dysmenorrhoea) Keputihan Vaginal discharge Mengandung Pregnant Keguguran Miscarriage Bayi kuning Newborn jaundice Batu karang Kidney or urinary stones Can also be used for gallstones Kencing berdarah Blood in the urine (haematuria) Always worth checking Kencing tidak lawas Weak flow, difficulty passing urine Common with an enlarged prostate Malay English Good to know Bengkak Swelling Swollen legs (kaki bengkak) in both legs should be checked Lebam Bruise Luka Wound, cut Melecur Scald, burn blister Lemah badan Weakness, feeling weak English Malay Diarrhoea (diarrhea) Cirit birit Constipation Sembelit Nausea Loya Dizzy Pening Fever Demam Cold or flu Selsema Cough Batuk Rash Ruam Bruise Lebam Food poisoning Keracunan makanan Asthma Lelah Kidney stone Batu karang Stroke Angin ahmar Wart Ketuat Piles Buasir Talking to your doctor You don’t need the medical word. Say what you feel, where it is, when it started, and what makes it better or worse. If a word has two meanings, such as pening or lelah , explain what you mean. If you are more comfortable in another language, ask the clinic if someone can help you, or bring a family member along. This guide explains language only and doesn’t diagnose illness. If you are concerned about symptoms, see a doctor. Call 999 for an emergency, and see our guide on clinic or emergency department . What is cirit birit in English? Diarrhoea, which means passing loose or watery stools 3 or more times a day. What is bisul in English? A boil, a painful, pus-filled lump under the skin caused by an infected hair follicle. What is buasir in English? Piles, also called haemorrhoids: swollen veins in or around the back passage. What is sawan in English? A seizure or fit. It doesn’t always mean epilepsy. What is bengkak in English? Swelling or swollen. What is selsema in English? The common cold. Selsema or selesema can also be used for influenza. What is muntah in English? Vomiting, or being sick. What is nanah in English? Pus, the thick fluid that can collect in an infected wound or boil. What is kayap in English? Shingles, a painful blistering rash caused by the chickenpox virus becoming active again. What is the meaning of gila babi? It is an old and stigmatising Malay term for epilepsy, and shouldn’t be used. The accepted word is epilepsi.

title: Bartholin cyst, ovarian cysts and fibroids: symptoms, treatment and when to worry
desc: A lump near the vaginal opening, a cyst found on a scan, or fibroids causing heavy periods: most are harmless and treatable. What Bartholin cysts, ovarian cysts and fibroids are, how they are treated, and the signs that need a doctor straight away.
headings: Bartholin cyst · Ovarian cysts (cyst ovari) · When pelvic pain is an emergency · Ovarian cancer warning signs · Fibroids
keywords: Women's health Bartholin cyst, ovarian cysts and fibroids Bartholin cyst Ovarian cyst Uterine fibroids mengandung hamil pregnancy antenatal kecemasan emergency a&e hospital saringan check-up checkup medical aesthetic estetik kecantikan beauty kulit skin botox filler laser facial
body: About 2 in 100 women get a Bartholin cyst. It is usually a painless lump on one side of the vaginal opening. If it becomes infected (an abscess), it gets very painful, red and swollen. Warm baths can help a small cyst drain. An abscess needs a doctor, who may drain it or fit a small catheter. Women over 40 with a new vulval lump should have it checked for cancer. Most ovarian cysts are “functional” cysts linked to the menstrual cycle and disappear within a few months. Larger, persistent or post-menopausal cysts need monitoring. Sudden, severe pelvic pain with vomiting, dizziness or fainting can mean a twisted or burst cyst. Go to an emergency department. Fibroids affect up to 8 in 10 women by age 50. Many cause no symptoms. Treatment depends on symptoms such as heavy periods, and fibroids almost never become cancer. The two Bartholin glands are pea-sized glands on either side of the vaginal opening that produce lubricating fluid. If a gland’s opening becomes blocked, fluid builds up and forms a cyst , usually on one side. It is most common between the ages of 20 and 50. Cyst: a soft, usually painless lump near the vaginal opening, from pea to golf-ball size. It may be uncomfortable when walking, sitting or having sex. Abscess: if the cyst becomes infected, it becomes very painful, red, hot and swollen, sometimes with fever or pus. It is usually caused by common skin or gut bacteria, and only occasionally by an STI such as gonorrhoea or chlamydia. See our guide to STI testing . Home care: sit in a few inches of warm water (a sitz bath) several times a day for 3 to 4 days, or use a warm compress. This may help a small cyst drain. Take paracetamol or ibuprofen for pain. Don’t squeeze or try to burst it. Treatment by a doctor: Antibiotics , if the cyst is infected or there is an STI Catheter drainage: after a small cut under local anaesthetic, a tiny balloon catheter is left in for about 4 weeks so a new opening forms Marsupialisation: a minor operation that creates a permanent opening, often used for cysts that keep coming back Cysts can come back after any treatment, about 1 in 10 after marsupialisation and more often after simple drainage. If you are over 40 , a new vulval lump should be checked, and a small sample (biopsy) may be taken, as Bartholin gland cancer, although rare, needs ruling out. Ovarian cysts are fluid-filled sacs on or in an ovary. They are very common and usually harmless. Functional cysts are the most common and are linked to the menstrual cycle: a follicle that doesn’t release its egg, or the sac left after ovulation filling with fluid. They usually disappear within a few weeks to 3 months. Other types include dermoid cysts (which can contain hair or skin tissue), endometriomas or “chocolate cysts” caused by endometriosis (see our guide to period pain and endometriosis ), and cystadenomas. PCOS is different: the “cysts” are many small follicles, not true cysts. See our PCOS (PMOS) guide . Symptoms: often none. Cysts are frequently found by chance on a scan. Some cause pelvic pain, bloating, pain during sex, needing to pass urine often, period changes or feeling full quickly. Monitoring and treatment: a cyst is usually checked with an ultrasound , often repeated a few weeks or months later to see if it has gone. UK guidance suggests small simple cysts under 5 cm in women who still have periods usually need no follow-up. Larger, persistent or complex cysts may need an MRI, blood tests or keyhole surgery to remove them. After the menopause , any cyst should be checked more carefully, with repeat scans and blood tests. Most ovarian cysts are found on an ultrasound and simply rechecked to see if they have gone. Go to an emergency department or call 999 for: sudden, severe pain in the lower tummy or pelvis, especially on one side, with vomiting, dizziness or fainting. An ovarian cyst may have twisted the ovary (torsion) or burst. pelvic pain with fever, fast breathing or cold, clammy skin very heavy vaginal bleeding severe pain or fainting if you could be pregnant, which may be an ectopic pregnancy. See our guide to early pregnancy warning signs . See a doctor soon for a Bartholin lump that becomes painful, red or swollen over hours or days, or comes with fever or pus. Most ovarian cysts aren’t cancer. But ovarian cancer is the fifth most common cancer in Malaysian women , and there is no screening test for it. Malaysian gynaecologists report that about three-quarters of cases are found at an advanced stage. See a doctor if you have any of these on most days, roughly 12 or more times a month: persistent bloating, or a swollen tummy pain in the tummy or pelvis feeling full quickly, or loss of appetite needing to pass urine more urgently or often These symptoms are usually caused by something less serious, but they are worth checking, especially if they are new. Regular Pap smears and HPV tests check the cervix, not the ovaries. Fibroids are non-cancerous growths of muscle in or on the womb. They are very common, affecting between 2 and 8 in 10 women by age 50, and are more common in women of Asian or African background, with obesity or with a family history. Symptoms: many women have none. Others have: heavy or painful periods, which can lead to iron-deficiency anaemia pressure or a swollen tummy needing to pass urine often, or constipation pain during sex less often, difficulty getting pregnant or miscarriage Treatment depends on your symptoms, the size and position of the fibroids, and whether you want children: No treatment if they cause no problems. Fibroids usually shrink after the menopause. Medicines: tranexamic acid and anti-inflammatory painkillers for heavy periods, hormonal contraception or a hormonal coil (see our contraception guide ), or injections that shrink fibroids temporarily.
